📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Capcom is bringing Mega Man: Dual Override to the Switch 1 & 2 in 2027 and to build some excitement, it's been revealing the Robot Masters you'll be facing in the game.

Industry observers note that this week it's officially declared the sixth Robot Master, 'Boat Man'. Here's the official description, along with a look (via Rockman Corner):.

A coastal fishing robot with a timid nature, Boat Man drops anchor in Mega Man: Dual Override! Teased for being hesitant to venture the high seas, this nautical nemesis unleashes a typhoon of tyranny against all who doubt him!

As our sixth Robot Master, Boat Man casts a wide net against those that ridiculed him. Will he bait you into his tidal trap? Or will you take the plunge into his aquatic arena to battle him willingly?".

This follows Capcom announcing the winner of the Mega Man: Dual Override Robot Master design contest earlier this week. It's "Cleanser Man"!

These Robot Masters will be joined by Cook Man, Tank Man, Twinkle Girl and Jet Man, with more Robot Master Reveals to come.

What do you think of the latest Robot Master reveal? Let us know in the comments.

Lauren’s push for him was hardly a secret in certain circles. Jeff might be the man with the billions, but Lauren has his ear.

Details on Bond 26 are being kept under wraps, including the title and premise. At this point, it also feels unlikely that it'll be released in 2027. However, we do know that Denis Villeneuve will be directing the movie, meaning this will be a Dune reunion for him and Pattinson. There is a lot of speculation surrounding who will join Pattinson, as names are being thrown out for the next Bond villain. And, of course, many are wondering who will be the next Bond girl with rumors placing Margaret Qualley in the lead as a strong candidate.

It has been revealed that regardless of what actually unfolds within the next 007 movie, this newly introduced report suggests that Robert Pattinson will be well compensated for the role. What's more is that this reported deal comes near the end of a year that saw him headline multiple high-profile movies. And, of course, can be seen in the upcoming Dune: Part Three, as well as 2028's The Batman: Part II. Needless to say, the man is booked and busy.

Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 writer states the games industry "is eating itself" amid mass layoffs

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (545 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Gamesradar

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Clair Obscur: Expedition 33's writer and Sandfall Interactive's former narrative lead, Jennifer Svedberg-Yen, thinks the game industry is "eating itself" and "losing so much institutional knowledge" through mass layoffs and studio closures.
  • A lot of what's happening really breaks my heart.
  • "I come from an investment background.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Clair Obscur: Expedition 33's writer and Sandfall Interactive's former narrative lead, Jennifer Svedberg-Yen, thinks the game industry is "eating itself" and "losing so much institutional knowledge" through mass layoffs and studio closures.

"I look around the game industry. A lot of what's happening really breaks my heart. I feel that the industry is eating itself. I feel that we are losing so much institutional knowledge. We're making it extraordinarily difficult for a younger generation of developers to have formative experiences. There's so much disruption in the industry right now," she says in an interview with GamesBeat.

"I come from an investment background. My original background was in private equity. I've seen that side. It frustrates me, because I think about it as, to use an agricultural analogy – in the past we've over-harvested the soil. We've tried to extract everything we can from the land. What we really need to do is cultivate the land. We need stewardship over the land. That means not over-harvesting. That means reinvesting in the land, in making sure there are nutrients put back into the land, so we can grow bigger and better things. I feel that we are not doing that as an industry," she adds.

Svedberg-Yen's not content with watching the chaos unfold, though. The award-winning writer is now working to set up a narrative investment fund to help developers along "between the seed stage and going to publishers." As she explains, many smaller creators need to develop a demo before pitching their games to publishers. "But to make a demo you need money. To get money you have to go to publishers." Her investment fund will hopefully help devs crack the "chicken and egg question," and minimize risk at the earliest stages of production.

Recent findings suggest that "I'm not trying to compete with publishers," she says. "But I'm trying to find a way to work with them to get us back on solid ground. Above all, I really would like to champion other people and other creatives to have a chance to pursue their dreams, have a chance to make the games they want to make.".

Svedberg-Yen's comments come during a devastating year for the games industry. Xbox plans to reduce its headcount by 3,200 by next summer. Sony shuttered Bluepoint Games and made layoffs at Sucker Punch. EA closed BioWare after a whopping three-decade run. Tomb Raider studio Crystal Dynamics laid off workers for the sixth time since its last full game. Even the most acclaimed developers are still at risk, and keeping track of all the layoffs in 2026 alone would likely require a dedicated Excel sheet.

Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 has sold 8.7 million copies and made $366 million, analyst says, and that's despite the "Game Pass cannibalization.".

Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more.

He particularly enjoys writing about spooky indies, throwback RPGs, and anything that's vaguely silly. Also has an English Literature and Film Studies degree that he'll soon forget.

Barbie Rewind, out now, invites you to take a trip down memory lane with a whole bunch of life in plastic classics, and one game that was previously unreleased

📅 12 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (358 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Rockpapershotgun

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Is there a character not originally from a video game that has more games than Barbie?
  • The latest release from Digital Eclipse, aficionados of digital multi-pack games like Atari 50: The Anniversary Celebration and last year's Mortal Kombat: Legacy Kollection, Barbie Rewind has a total of 16 games from across the doll's video game history.
  • Beyond that, there's the customizable DreamHouse, where you get a whole bunch of furniture to deck it out with.

Is there a character not originally from a video game that has more games than Barbie? Maybe! I don't want to do any maths right now, but there aren't many that could touch her on sheer numbers. She's had all sorts of digital adventures, her games having a huge influence on the world of 'girl games'. As complicatedly gendered that may now be, the significance can't be understated, and as of today you can have a romp through a nice portion of that history in Barbie Rewind, a compilation of almost two decades worth of games all wrapped up in a nice little decorating game.

The latest release from Digital Eclipse, aficionados of digital multi-pack games like Atari 50: The Anniversary Celebration and last year's Mortal Kombat: Legacy Kollection, Barbie Rewind has a total of 16 games from across the doll's video game history. Starting all the way back in 1991 with Barbie for the original NES, it jumps around to the Game Boy Color with Barbie: Pet Rescue, to the SNES with Barbie: Vacation Adventure. That last one's vital because it's actually an unreleased game, making it quite a neat addition to the package.

Beyond that, there's the customizable DreamHouse, where you get a whole bunch of furniture to deck it out with. Nothing overly complicated here, it's just a thematically appropriate appendage that helps to recreate the feeling of playing with a doll house in pixel art form. Expect familiar faces like Ken, Teresa and Christie to pop up here and there as well. You'll also find a digital lookbook where you can "flip through the pages of Barbie history.".

It has been revealed that perhaps slightly disappointingly you won't find a number of beloved Barbie games like Barbie: Secret Agent or Barbie Horse Adventures: Mystery Ride. A lot of the games in this package are the 2D, pixel art entries, so that was probably meant to be the focus here. Hopefully someone will part those 3D releases somewhere down the line! In any case, if you fancy a trip down memory lane, you can pick up Barbie Rewind on Steam now.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake has been a huge success for Nintendo, becoming the fastest-selling Switch 2 game ever, shifting more than 5.2 million copies in four days.

In a recent development, nintendo declared the sales result this morning in a press release, specifying that the record relates only to Nintendo-published games. But since Nintendo's games are the most popular Switch 2 games, the fastest-selling-ever title presumably holds.

It's an incredible result for a game that's been received with enormous enthusiasm. Christian Donlan awarded The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time five golden stars in Eurogamer's review, saying: "Alongside great judgement and clever tweaks, this astonishing remake has a proper ace up its sleeve." We've also already seen a jump in US Switch 2 sales because of the game's release. So much for not launching in November near GTA 6, eh?

This level of success begs the question of whether Nintendo would consider remaking more beloved old Zelda games - or Nintendo games - to replicate this nostalgia-driven effect. Are there other Zelda games that have the pull of Ocarina of Time that haven't been remade or remastered already in some capacity?

If you're inspired to pick the game up because of this, or already have it, know that we've got a whole proverbial library shelf of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time guides to help you through the game.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • This next upgrade has a lot going for it, and it will be in players’ hands everywhere on May 20.
  • Luna 7 will take us back to Sumeru for its upcoming Archon Quest, where a new crisis that threatens to plunge the nation into chaos is brewing.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, hoYoverse just wrapped up a latest Genshin Impact Special Program, where the developer revealed everything there is to know about the game’s next major update. Truth Amongst the Pages of Purana, or as its friends call it, Luna 7, was unveiled as part of the showcase.

This next upgrade has a lot going for it, and it will be in players’ hands everywhere on May 20.

Luna 7 will take us back to Sumeru for its upcoming Archon Quest, where a new crisis that threatens to plunge the nation into chaos is brewing. Nahida is out of the picture, and someone who looks suspiciously like Il Dottore has emerged.

It has been revealed that if you complete this chapter at launch, you’ll earn up to 560 Primogems, as well as Nicole's Ascension Materials. Nicole is the first of three playable characters arriving with this update. Something else you’ll unlock if you finish the chapter promptly is a new Weekly Boss that HoYo says has “unpredictable abilities.”.

Sources indicate that and if you haven’t played in a while, don’t worry, you can refer to the Guiding Notes feature to catch you up on what’s been going on in the world. This is part of a larger effort from the team to make story progression more seamless, and also includes improved quest autosave prompts.

It has been revealed that nicole Reeyn is highest-profile and most interesting, being the first playable member of the Hexenzirkel. The mage is a 5-Star Pyro Catalyst wielder intended as a support member of the team. She can boost the ATK of all party members, even those not at the moment on the field. She also generates a shield while doing so.

Sources indicate that her Elemental Burst allows her to summon an Arcane Projection that follows the active character, sending out Coordinated Attacks that match their Elemental Type. Outside of combat, Nicole can help you find treasures by calling upon a Seelie to guide you to them. Quite fitting, as you’ll be exploring in the inside of the Witch's Lodge in Nicole’s Meeting Point in Luna 7, so bring her along.

Lohen, the Vice Captain of the Knights of Favonius' Fifth Organization, is the second fresh character. Also a 5-Star addition, he is instead a Cryo Polearm wielder designed for aggressive combat. His main use is dealing massive Cryo DMG, and he can do that by managing two resources unique to him: Joy, and Will to Win.

Through his Elemental Skill, he can enter the Masterstroke state, allowing him to build up (and consume) Joy to unleash enhanced skills. The more his teammates fight, the more Will to Win he biulds, which can later be used to boost his effectiveness further. For an even more powerful display of force, bring along a Hexerei character when he’s on your team.

In a recent development, prune is the third and final addition. Prune is a 4-Star Anemo Catalyst wielder, and her kit is inspired by her Witch Hunter aspirations. Using a bell and a hammer, she can deal DMG of several elements at once, and trigger Swirl reactions.

Sources indicate that nicole, and Lohen will debut in Luna 7’s first half, while Prune will follow in the second. The first half will also see a Durin rerun, with Mavuika returning in the second half. You can look forward to a new limited-time event as part of Luna 7, with a focus on Klee's Little Hexenzirkel.

You’ll find a series of mini-games you can play alongside Prune, as well as Qiqi, Yaoyao, and Sayu. If you play, you could earn the Super Awesome Magic Key, an exclusive weapon skin. Miliastra Wonderland is doing its thing, too, with a latest sports festival for you to take part in.

Sources indicate that one latest gameplay addition worth calling attention to is that Manekins can now perform actions in Teyvat. The Kamera, which you can use to capture moments with Manekins, is getting upgraded, too, with new editing tools and assets.

Before you pick the game back up, be sure to check out our recently-updated Genshin Impact codes page for some free stuff you may be missing.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

If I can pinpoint one disappointing aspect of GTA 6 that most will agree on, it's the fact that it runs at 30 fps.

Industry observers note that many of us remember when this was normal for consoles (especially the PS3/Xbox 360 era), but these days, it's unusual for a major game to not offer a 60 fps or 40 fps performance option. Unfortunately, even if you're rocking a PS5 Pro, GTA 6 moves at a filmic 30.

That's disappointing news for anyone who shelled out $900+ for the more powerful PS5 Pro expecting better performance (or vindicating news, if you're a PC Gamer reader waiting for the arbitrarily delayed PC version), but Rockstar insists there was no way around it.

Speaking to Kotaku, technology production director Marc Chambers explained that the current consoles just aren't powerful enough to keep up without significant compromises.

Recent findings suggest that "Our base presentation makes use of ray-traced reflections and global illumination. On the PS5 Pro, this is enhanced with the addition of ray-traced shadows, as well as overall added clarity through the use of PlayStation Spectral Super Resolution (PSSR)," he stated. "The PS5 Pro features an upgraded graphics processor and upscaling technology that we leverage to increase the game’s visual fidelity. While the PS5 Pro’s central processor is slightly better than the PS5 base console, it is not powerful enough to run the game’s complex simulation at higher frame rates.".

Head of development Rob Nelson framed the decision to skip performance mode in much simpler terms to IGN:.

In a recent development, "It wouldn’t have been acceptable to anybody. The simple answer is, when you ask the technical team, they’re, like, ‘Have you seen it?’ There’s too many compromises that would’ve had to have been made to do that, is the short answer," he remarked. "Too much, too much.".

Keep up to date with the most key stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

While I don't actually have a problem playing a slow-paced game like GTA 6 at half the usual framerate so long as it's consistent and smooth, I can't deny that these quotes left me cracking a smile in the direction of my PC.

The world of Leonida does look unbelievably impressive at times—both in terms of pure graphical oomph and the density of vehicles, NPCs, and reactive foliage—but a great PC is going to demolish it. I've been searching for a game that will make this RTX 5090 actually flinch, and honestly, I'm doubtful even GTA 6 will be it. Barring a suite of PC-only enhancements that raise its requirements by a lot, I can't imagine a game that targets an Xbox Series S will have trouble blowing past 60 fps on top PC hardware.

This is putting into perspective for me that, while I wasn't looking, the current consoles got old. That's fine, to be clear—we're in the middle of a tech pause that has me happily playing older games anyway—but it's a wasted opportunity that GTA 6 is debuting exclusively on mid hardware.

We have to wait an unspecified amount of time to get what is destined to be the best version of this generational game. As Chris remarked in his writeup after 100 hours with GTA 6, "It's (mostly) great. But it will be (mostly) so much greater when it comes to PC.".

I often find it quite dull that the main takeaway far too many people have taken from Dark Souls, aside from thinking that the most interesting thing is its combat, is that it's all so bloomin' grimdark. I'm not saying I need sunshine and rainbows, I'd just like a vibe that's even remotely trying to be different from FromSoftware's seminal work. And so! I am quite pleased to discover MycoRelic, a Soulslike that pits you as a robot that covers its body in mushroom parts that offer elemental powers.

MycoRelic, from the offset, has this low-poly style that almost reminds me of oldschool RuneScape in a way I clown with quite quickly. The game looks good! The vibes look odd and, thankfully, not particularly derivative of medieval aesthetics. But while I am vibes-first when it comes to games, a Soulslike does live and die by its systems, and the systems here sound quite intriguing.

For starters, there are no classes to speak of, just various weapons with their own moves and stats, and armour that "suits your playstyle and aesthetic." Huzzah! A game that understands one of the best bits of Dark Souls is dressing up. When you start out, you just have a "decrepit, moldy frame," but over time you can replace parts of it to improve your health, stamina, frame integrity, and the "potency of your fungal magic." Mycellic music to my ears.

Different fungi have different powers, and can be combined to create new effects, or used in a multitude of ways; healing water can restore your friends or put out a fire for example. And oh, yes, there's co-op too, though I don't know if it's the friction-heavy Dark Souls kind or the seamless, hassle-free kind. On top of all this you've got an air-dash and can glide too, offering up some tasty platforming potential not typically found in the genre. I like it! And it just came out in 1.0 after a period of early access. If you fancy giving it a go, there's still a demo on Steam, or you can just pick up the full thing.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Tom Hiddleston has revealed the call from Marvel bosses that proved to him how integral Loki was to Avengers: Doomsday.

"The call came from [Marvel Studios president] Kevin Feige and [co-president] Louis D'Esposito, and it was very clear there was no way of continuing a story about the multiverse without Loki," Hiddleston told Empire magazine. "They wanted me to be part of it. That's what they mentioned.".

Hiddleston also mentioned that the multiverse – a narrative concept now reaching critical mass thanks to the MCU – and Loki are effectively intertwined at this point, making the notion of ignoring the former trickster god all but impossible.

Hiddleston remarked, "At this point, having expanded what we can call the multiverse in a way that isn't a niche reference now, and Loki's position as the God of Stories, on the substantial chair at the End of Time, holding the branches of many timelines together, there was no way to continue to talk about the multiverse without acknowledging his position.".

Away from Doomsday, the newfound God of Stories has also been a crucial component for Marvel's so-called 'Multiverse Saga', a sprawling chapter of MCU movies and shows that kicked off with WandaVision, Falcon and The Winter Soldier, and Loki in 2021, and culminating with Avengers: Secret Wars in 2027.

Loki has largely been at the forefront of the more multiverse-heavy adventures, inadvertently splintering the multiverse in Loki season 1, before acting as the force to hold them together in Loki season 2.

Loki also doorstepped Peggy Carter and Steve Rogers just after their iconic dance in Avengers: Endgame – as revealed during the new ending of Endgame's Encore re-release.

In a recent development, of course, Loki isn't the only notable Marvel figure rocking up in Avengers: Doomsday. Far from it. Alongside him is Robert Downey Jr.'s Doctor Doom, Steve Rogers, plus the casts of Fantastic Four and Thunderbolts. Several OG Avengers are also on the scene, plus multiple members of Fox's X-Men team, including Professor X, Magneto, and Cyclops.

Avengers: Doomsday hits UK cinemas on December 16 and US cinemas on December 18.

For more, we've done our best TVA impression and untangled the Marvel timeline for you.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that the 9-1-1 franchise is heating up amid the 2026 TV schedule. While the fall finales of both the Mothership and 9-1-1: Nashville air this week, there's going to be a lot more on the way in the newly introduced year. This includes a much-anticipated I Know What You Did Last Summer reunion between Jennifer Love Hewitt and Ryan Phillippe. I'm excited, but what I didn’t expect was Hewitt’s intense take on working with her former co-star again.

In a recent development, hewitt and Phillippe starred together in the first IKWYDLS film, which was released back in 1997. While Phillippe’s Barry Cox is eventually murdered in the movie, Hewitt’s Julie James becomes the focal point of the sequels. So it’s been close to 30 years since the original movie, and it's great that Barry and Julie are finally back together in some sense.

Following speculation that Phillippe and Hewitt would be reuniting, Hewitt recently confirmed that he would indeed guest star on 9-1-1, reprising his Nashville role as Detective Rogue Kelly. Surprisingly, this is actually the first time that they’ve seen each other since filming wrapped on IKWYDLS, and Hewitt recalled to People just what the atmosphere felt like before the crossover came together. And her take even makes me a bit anxious:.

I was so nervous. I had dry mouth and like a full racy heart. Everybody was like, ‘Are you excited?’ I was like, ‘I feel like I’ve forgotten how to act.’ Yeah, it was amazing. We greeted each other with just a big hug and he was like, ‘This is going to be really fun.’ I said, ‘I think it is.’ And it was just, it was a dream.

It has been revealed that I love that even though they’ve worked together before, Hewitt can still have those nerves, and I can’t say I blame her. Reuniting with someone you haven’t seen in years -- even if it's on your own turf -- can be intimidating. It sounds like the mood instantly shifted when Phillippe came to set, in a good way, and it makes me even more excited to see how it all turns out.

Sources indicate that phillippe only joined 9-1-1: Nashville for Season 2, so the fact that the two reveals are already jumping at the chance to do a crossover featuring him and Hewitt is pretty great. Plus, seeing Phillippe and Hewitt together again is like a '90s-infused dream, and it sounds like they had the time of their lives. Hewitt admitted just how much fun they’ve had from seeing the Internet reacting to the news. She also shared how great it’s been to welcome Phillippe to the 9-1-1 Universe, especially after she reunited with Freddie Prinze Jr. for 2025’s I Know What You Did Last Summer:.

It has been revealed that he and I have had the best time with people’s reaction. We’ve been DMing going, ‘Did you see it?’ I think we broke the internet. We’ve been having the best time. It was so great because I got to go back and do the movie with Freddie [Prinze Jr.] and sort of have that, and do [our characters] Julie James and Ray again. But this was very different because it was like, [Ryan’s] latest in that universe. I’ve been in this universe for a while. It’s such a safe, lovely place to be with the best people. And he and I have not seen each other since I was 18 years old.

As for right now, details surrounding the next 9-1-1 and 9-1-1: Nashville crossover have not been revealed, and I'm eager to see what brings Rogue to Los Angeles. After trying to track down a serial killer in Nashville who is using biblical plagues, hopefully this trip out West will be a bit lighter for him. Of course, if anyone can help him, it’s Hewitt’s Maddie Buckley-Han, who is arguably the best 9-1-1 dispatcher in LA.

Hopefully, crossover information is confirmed soon, but considering the amount of content Jennifer Love Hewitt has been sharing on her Instagram, she is probably going to keep fans fed for the time being.

Your Daily Blend of Entertainment News.

For now, viewers can tune in for the fall finales of 9-1-1 and 9-1-1: Nashville, which air this Thursday, November 19, at 8 p.m. ET on ABC, streaming the next day with a Hulu subscription. Both reveals will then return from their midseason breaks on Thursday, January 7.

In a recent development, monster Hunter Wilds's first expansion, Ascendance, is set for release sometime next year. But, judging by some very suspect recent changes to the Wilds beta app on Steam, we may be playing some of the latest stuff earlier than we thought.

On Steam, Capcom quietly updated the Monster Hunter Wilds Beta app to now say Monster Hunter Wilds: Ascendance Beta test. You can see the change log on SteamDB (via PC Gamer), which also reveals an updated key art - all signs that point towards an impending beta for Ascendance.

According to recent reports, seeing as Ascendance itself doesn't have a release date, beyond a nebulous 2027 target, it's hard to speculate when Capcom plans to release the beta. Sometime early in 2027 would be a good guess, perhaps alongside a release date announcement.

Capcom has shown off Ascendance on multiple occasions, more recently in Sony's September State of Play, where we got to see a number of the expansion's upcoming features. A few days later at Tokyo Game Show, we got a first look at returning Elder Dragon Teostra, which we can hunt in the expansion.

Capcom is keen for Ascendance to deliver the level of challenge Monster Hunter is known for, following feedback that the launch version of Wilds simply lacked that expected level of difficulty. While post-launch updates have certainly raised the level of challenge, Ascendance looks to be the next step up.

The neighborhood kids are getting older, too, bringing exciting new stories and interactions to Starlet Town.

Farm. Decorate. Craft. Explore. Relax. Players shape their own future—and the future of Coral Island.

So, if this looks like a cosy farming sim you might be interested in, be on the lookout for its arrival on the Switch 2 soon.

Mystic Messenger's most loyal players are getting banned in droves for seemingly playing the game too much

📅 15 May 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (728 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Vg247

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Mystic Messenger, arguably one of the best dating sims around, has been dormant for about seven years.
  • According to recent reports, the free-to-play mobile dating sim has started banning players with seemingly too many Hourglasses - the game’s virtual currency - saved up in their accounts.
  • The news exploded on the Mystic Messenger subreddit overnight, with over a dozen reports from players logging in to play normally, only to receive an in-game notice that their accounts had been banned.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Mystic Messenger, arguably one of the best dating sims around, has been dormant for about seven years. Despite not receiving newly introduced content or any meaningful updates in all that time, the game remains popular with its core fans, many of whom just woke up to some shocking news about their accounts.

According to recent reports, the free-to-play mobile dating sim has started banning players with seemingly too many Hourglasses - the game’s virtual currency - saved up in their accounts. So far, it looks like players with 1,000 or more have been targeted, but others with far fewer hoards have reported getting the axe, too.

The news exploded on the Mystic Messenger subreddit overnight, with over a dozen reports from players logging in to play normally, only to receive an in-game notice that their accounts had been banned.

The message players received is identical, and doesn’t mention the specific reason for the ban. “Your account has been banned because abusive behavior has been detected from your account,” it reads, ending with a support email address the affected user can contact if they believe they’d banned in error.

It didn’t take a while for players to realise that most, if not all of the bans are for players with thousands of Hourglasses in their accounts. The virtual currency can both be acquired in-game just by playing, as well as through direct real-money purchases.

For a nearly ten-year-old game that stopped receiving content three years into its life, it’s easy to see how a dedicated group of players would be able to acquire so many Hourglasses by simply playing regularly for so long.

When contacted by the affected players, Cheritz, the developer and publisher of the game, has instructed them to send receipts of how they acquired Hourglasses (assuming they were purchased) to verify whether or not they’d been fraudulently obtained.

Considering that Mystic Messenger has practically been abandoned by its developer, certain exploits have emerged over the years that allowed players to farm Hourglasses faster than intended, but those instances have always been dealt with then and there.

The blanket and sudden nature of this ban is what’s spooked players, especially those who’ve been logging in for years and never thought accruing in-game currency from playing the game too much would make them the target of a ban.

Sources indicate that the running theory is that most of the bans are unintentional, and may be the result of a upcoming automated security system that’s been implemented. It’s entirely possible, especially if its’s AI-based, that the new system simply couldn’t distinguish between those who have earned (or bought) their Hourglasses fairly, and those who used exploits.

Sources indicate that the timing of the ban wave is also suspect. With the game’s 10th anniversary coming up in July, it could be that Cheriz is preparing to release a large upgrade for Mystic Messenger, which may include new content. If most of the playerbase is already sitting on massive amounts of in-game currency, they may simply use that to fast-track their way to unlocking the new content, which would greatly affect the developer’s bottom line.

This is a problem that other live service games have run into in the past. Just recently, extraction shooter Arc Raiders added a cap to the amount of Cred players can hold in their accounts very promptly after its launch. That currency is used to buy cosmetic sets in the store, so the logic is easy to follow.

All of that has certainly put a damper on the enthusiasm of the game’s most active players, many of whom were excited to get together in person for the coming 10th anniversary, participate in community nights and so on to celebrate.

Recent findings suggest that it’s also disheartening to see a fanbase so loyal; playing a game as regularly for so long without latest content, to be treated so poorly. Even without knowing what the game is, it’s impressive that so many people have kept the flag of their favourite game flying for so long.

November is a huge month for video games, with not only the release of the Ocarina of Time remake but also the long-awaited (and highly anticipated) arrival of GTA 6 this week.

According to recent reports, while most games decided to avoid this month, one other title that has been released over the past week is TANUKI: Pon's Summer. If you are wondering why a game starring a BMX-riding tanuki decided to go up against these two juggernauts, it seems the Zelda news caught it by surprise.

Although it was prepared for GTA 6's arrival, Nintendo only confirmed the release of Ocarina's remake in September, and then launched it at the start of November. Here's what Denkiworks co-founder and game director Liam Edwards had to say about this during an interview with Games Industry:.

In a recent development, "While we originally decided on October to launch, due to marketing opportunities with first-party platforms, we decided that the sweet spot would be just clear of GTA 6's initial launch period. What I don't think we could have accounted for was Nintendo shadow-dropping the release of Ocarina of Time [on November 5].".

He further notes how there's "probably a fair bit more of an overlap with "Switch 2 Zelda players" for Tanuki than there would be for GTA 6". Despite this, there's hope the title can still find "long-term" success through "word-of-mouth" style marketing, and that maybe some players will pick up the "BMXing Tanuki game" once they're done with Nintendo and Rockstar's games.

We gave Tanuki: Pon's Summer seven out of ten stars in our NL review, describing it as a cosy game you can get lost in.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • World of Warcraft secret hunters are a noble breed, known for scouring the MMO for years for hidden trinkets and treasures.
  • Recent findings suggest that over the past week, members of the WoW Secret Hunters Discord found a quest chain that takes place entirely on the Zephras Isle, meaning you'll need to have access to the Skyborne elves to grab this sword.
  • Then, you'll need to head to Duskwood to gather the Night Watchman's Torch, a handy light source primarily used to light up areas across the darkened woods near Stormwind.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

World of Warcraft secret hunters are a noble breed, known for scouring the MMO for years for hidden trinkets and treasures. With World of Warcraft: Forever's launch, they've uncovered a quest chain for an especially fancy sword.

Recent findings suggest that over the past week, members of the WoW Secret Hunters Discord found a quest chain that takes place entirely on the Zephras Isle, meaning you'll need to have access to the Skyborne elves to grab this sword. Navigating the island, you'll need to first pick up an ancient heirloom ring from the starting zone. Simple enough!

Then, you'll need to head to Duskwood to gather the Night Watchman's Torch, a handy light source primarily used to light up areas across the darkened woods near Stormwind. It turns out this torch has uses far beyond this one zone however, as taking it back to the Ruins of Ban'aethal on the Zephras Isle will reward you with a secret quest and the Ancient Hilt.

With the hilt and ring, you then must track down an Ancient Blade from one of several spawn locations on the Zephras Isle. Once you finally track it down, that's the end of part one of this quest chain. You get the sword: Eluvi'ana, which on its own isn't particularly strong, but is speculated to be upgraded later down the line.

You then need to get a corrupted water globe from either Darkshore or the Blackfathom Deeps dungeon depending on your faction, do a fetch quest for a hidden spirit in Ashenvale, then take your hoard of special quest items to a NPC in the latest Shen'Dralar zone.

According to recent reports, he won't give you the finished sword. Instead he sends you to gather more items from higher-level zones. You'll need to raid a secluded vault in Feralas that you can only see with the Ancient Hilt, dive underwater in Azshara, and kill Highborne Shades in Winterspring. Once you've done all that, you can then cleanse the orb up in Hyjal, speak to the fella back in Shen'Dralar, then shimmy over to the end game Dire Maul dungeon to speak to Prince Tortheldrin about *another* sword.

This is how far the World of Warcraft: Forever secret hunter community has gotten to. It's believed that grinding up the Shen'dralar reputation to Honoured is required for the next step, as Prince Tortheldrin pretty much claims as much in his dialogue. So the hunt is still on!

These sorts of secrets make up an crucial part of any good MMO: the solving of mysteries in these vast digital open worlds. In retail WoW, I have fond memories of the Waist of Time quest chain, which was an arduous and comical grind for a fancy belt during the Battle for Azeroth expansion. This secret sword quest chain may very well evolve into something as legendary as that, at least I hope so!

It has been revealed that if you're not already playing it, World of Warcraft: Forever is plenty of fun. A record-breaking number of players are making the journey through Azeroth right now, diving into quests and dungeons new and old.

According to recent reports, steam is abuzz this week with a couple of long-anticipated rolls out, but in Forza Horizon 6’s case, at least, the game isn’t even out for what will be most of its players. The anticipated sequel in the open-world driving game series doesn’t officially launch until May 19, but owners of its most expensive version - the Premium Edition - can play it right now.

That version of the game includes more than just a few days of early access, of course, but you’d think the $120 price tag would’ve only been palatable to a small group of players. Not the case with this game.

Recent findings suggest that forza Horizon 6, which has spent 16 weeks in Steam’s global top sellers list, right now occupies the number two spot, having jumped up three spots this week in anticipation of the launch. The game has also naturally been popular with players, so popular in fact that it has already overtaken the player counts of all other Horizon games on the platform.

According to recent reports, at the time of writing, the game has peaked at 128,157 concurrent players on Steam alone (via SteamDB). The figure has already climbed several times during the writing of this story, so you can only imagine how much higher it’s going to get deeper into the weekend.

It has been revealed that all of that, of course, days before the official launch on Tuesday, when, theoretically, the majority of the game’s audience will be able to start playing. In just a few short hours, Horizon 6 has already gone well above Forza Horizon 5’s peak concurrent of 81,096, as well as Forza Horizon 4’s peak 75,689 players.

Steam is the only platform that publishes player numbers, of course, but it’s easy to see how similar the enthusiasm is going to be on Xbox. Though the game is not yet part of the Game Pass line-up, those who don’t want to wait could buy the Premium Edition Upgrade to get the included content, and play it right now.

In a recent development, game Pass, and Xbox / Windows Store numbers don’t factor into Steam’s, which is another thing to consider when viewing the numbers holistically. Indeed, given how successful Forza Horizon 5 has been on PlayStation 5, Horizon 6’s upcoming release on Sony's console is bound to be even bigger.

Forza Horizon 5 has been off to a similarly flying start in the first few days of its own advanced access launch, so it’s obviously not surprising to see Horizon 6 do better there. In case you missed it, check out our review of Forza Horizon 6. In short, we really liked it, even if we expected more.

The second mode is Dread, which as the name implies, is a "brutal" difficulty mode that you can only play if you've reached Ascension 10 on every character, including The Fool. "All ascension modifiers are enabled. Bosses are stronger and buff all enemies in their Act. Curses will also pile up as you climb the Spire. Death is expected.".

You can expect a bunch of fresh balance tweaks and changes too. For starters, you'll find that rest sites can now appear a floor earlier every act. New events have been added to Underdocks and Act 2 and 3 too. 📅 11 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 2m • 📖 Standard (316 w)

Business & Policy ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Eurogamer ↗ Open Full Page

As of this week, PlayStation 5 has surpassed 100 million consoles sold

📅 11 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (316 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Eurogamer

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that playStation 5 has officially surpassed 100m consoles sold, Sony's updated sales data revealed.
  • The figure represents 'sell-in' units, meaning those shipped to retailers, as opposed to 'sell-through' which tracks consoles actually sold to consumers.
  • Nevertheless, this is an impressive achievement, and gets the PS5 ever closer to the PS4's 117m, which it achieved by June 2022.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that playStation 5 has officially surpassed 100m consoles sold, Sony's updated sales data revealed. The milestone was reached on 10th November, almost exactly six years on from the console's launch.

The figure represents 'sell-in' units, meaning those shipped to retailers, as opposed to 'sell-through' which tracks consoles actually sold to consumers. In other words, the number of PS5s in people's homes is smaller than that 100m.

Nevertheless, this is an impressive achievement, and gets the PS5 ever closer to the PS4's 117m, which it achieved by June 2022. It also means the PS5 has almost matched the original PlayStation in units sold (102.4m). As impressive as the numbers are, historical data shows that PS5 sales have been in decline.

Sony hasn't shied away from discussing that fact in its earnings reports. 2.6m PS5 consoles were sold during the most recent quarter (Q2 of FY2026), well below the 4m sold over the same period the year prior. In fact, Q2 of FY2026 is the lowest second quarter on record in terms of units sold since the PS5's launch.

However, it's also worth noting that, small though it may be, the second quarter's result is higher than the first quarter's 1.6m, the second-lowest of any single quarter since the PS5's launch, beaten only by Q4 of FY2025's 1.5m.

Recent findings suggest that if numbers don't recover in the third and fourth quarters, this may be the PS5's lowest year ever in terms of units sold. Although the second quarter's sales boost can be attributed to the high anticipation of Grand Theft Auto 6, the overall downturn is largely due to the console's higher price; Sony raised the PS5 and PS5 Pro's prices on several occasions since 2020. The firm's bottom line, however, hasn't been affected much, as its plan to generate more revenue from its already-engaged audience continues to work.

The upcoming update adds a newly introduced chapter to the Planarcadia arc, and introduce a new playable character.

The new narrative chapter will also unveil more about Mortenax Blade, the Trailblazer themselves, and the husk of the Aeon.

Industry observers note that mortenax Blade is the hero of this chapter, and he’s going to step into the World in Canvas. The goal is to - by borrowing the power of Voracity - excise Shuhu from his body and end the curse.

Sources indicate that the Trailblazer goes on a trip of their own in Version 4.3, this time to Inkford Hermitage, right on the edge between the World in Canvas and the real world. They’re going to undertake this journey to warn Graphia of the Asat Pramad threat.

Recent findings suggest that in case you hadn’t already guessed, Mortenax Blade is this version’s new playable character. The 5-Star Fire-Type swordsman is on the Path of Nihility. Blade’s Ultimate allows him to enter an enhanced state by deploying a special Bounded Field.

While the field is active, all enemies receive more DMG. Entering this state is also how Blade unlocks his skill, which uses a Sword Formation to deal more damage. This is then used to essentially unlock a second, more powerful Ultimate for him.

The benefits of Mortenax Blade’s kit extend to his teammates, too. Any ally who attacks an enemy with him on the team, they inflict a debuff on them. This also builds up a special Charge that Blade can later use with his Skill.

Sources indicate that version 4.3’s launch arrives alongside the Gift of Tempered Blade event. Through it, you can claim a latest Trailblazer Outfit piece for free, but only after getting Mortenax Blade from Warping. The first phase’s rerun will be Yao Guang, and the second phase will bring back both Cyrene and Phainon.

According to recent reports, you can also expect the Wispae Amusement Park to arrive within the World in Canvas, which you’ll get to design. You can blueprint where the rides will go, pick the different themes, set visitor routes and more.

Starward Mode is another new addition, which can be found in Memory of Chaos, Pure Fiction, and Apocalyptic Shadow. Starward will see you take on three different stages, which you’ll need three teams for. Clearing each challenge with full stars will reward you 100 Stellar Jades extra per chase.

Sources indicate that there’s more coming down the line, too. A fresh Fate/Stay Night [Unlimited Blade Works] collaboration will arrive in a content up this summer. The event will give players a chance to earn Gilgamesh or Archer for free by logging in.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Xbox have confirmed that Wolfenstein 3 is indeed in production at Indiana Jones and the Great Circle devs MachineGames and that Doom makers id Software have started work on their next game after losing a bunch of staff to the mass layoffs across Microsoft's gaming division this year.

"A single person will soon be able to wield capabilities that once required entire nations," isn't part of the marketing spiel for either of those games. Instead, it's something Xbox CEO Asha Shama has bellowed amid a rant outlining how she sees the company's future.

The Wolfenstein and id confirmations came as Xbox had a bit of a social media party to commemorate their 25th birthday. Sharma, ever keen to be seen right next to any positive news coming out of the company, confirmed Wolfenstein 3 is in production by posting a photo showing a few lines from its script. Around the same time, she shouted out Doom: The Dark Ages Revelations' incoming Slaughter Mode, adding that "the team is already working on its next game".

The official id Software account responded to note that this next game is being made by their "teams in Texas and Frankfurt, with game direction once again by Hugo Martin", and that "it'll be some time before [they're] ready to share more".

We're incredibly excited about our next project, a upcoming game from our teams in Texas and Frankfurt, with game direction once again by Hugo Martin. It'll be some time before we're ready to share more but we can't wait for you to see what we're working on.

Alongside hollering about these couple of games, Sharma put out a 25th anniversary statement which for the most part does the sort of bigging up of Xbox's past you'd expect. Good times were had, we blazed a trail and made lots of money, etcetera. The final section saw the exec attempt to look forward to the next 25 years for Xbox.

Recent findings suggest that "While modern games demonstrate the heights of human craft in ways unimaginable just decades ago, the cost, resources, and risk required to create them have grown just as dramatically," she wrote. "As a result, too many ideas never become games, and too many games fall short of what their creators imagined. For decades, this has been the unavoidable tradeoff of ambition. We must change this.

According to recent reports, "Throughout human history, the scale of what we could create was determined by the people, capital, and resources we could command. That relationship is beginning to break. A single person will soon be able to wield capabilities that once required entire nations. A small team will be able to build worlds that today demand hundreds of developers and hundreds of millions of dollars. And our largest studios will be able to pursue ambitions as far beyond today's games as Microsoft Flight Simulator 2024 is from its first entry in 1982.".

Industry observers note that that certainly sounds a lot like the sales pitch the biggest proponents of generative AI keep wheeling out, while avoiding saying generative AI out loud in the hopes of making it more palatable to folks who might not make the connection. I'm waiting for Sharma to put out another post revealing that she accidentally mixed another section of the Wolfenstein script into her celebratory musings, but I'm not holding my breath.

Xbox parent firm Microsoft are still at the moment subject to a BDS movement boycott over their reported ties to the Israeli military.

According to recent reports, the world of The Simpsons has officially arrived in Monopoly Go, and there's a whole lot for players to dive into. The show's creative team even produced a upcoming animated short, featuring Mr. Monopoly, and Mr. Burns.

Recent findings suggest that available June 3 through July 29, the fresh event allows Monopoly Go players to jump in the world of The Simpsons. You'll be able to build, and explore all around multiple iconic locations from the show.

Along the way, you'll run into Simpsons characters like Homer, Marge, Bart, Lisa, and of course, Mr. Burns. Developer Scopely teamed up with the show's creative team to create many references, and Easter Eggs for you to discover. You'll find some of those on chance cards, but most of the world has been changed to be part of The Simpsons, including getting to bribe Chief Wiggum to escape jail.

The developer promises a deeply connected world with Simpsons narratives and characters that alter seasonal maps, and offer unique sticker sets and animated sequences to dive in. Incidentally, this is The Simpsons' first appearance in a mobile-exclusive game in 13 years.

Here's a breakdown of everything you can expect, straight from Scopely:.

Episodes: Narrative-driven encounters that create stories inspired by The Simpsons. Episodes play out across seasonal boards, sticker sets, and minigames, all capped off with an animated short.

Sticker sets: Every Episode comes with its own limited-time sticker set, taking cues from the latest Simpsons story. Collectible artwork, character journeys and other rewards are yours to claim for the duration of each Episode.

The Simpsons Run: Every two weeks, a latest Springfield character will take over the Free Parking tile, kicking off character-driven runs.

Simpsons-themed Shutdowns and Heists: Monopoly Go's shutdowns and heists get a Simpsons makeover, with Springfield-inspired chaos and disasters.

Bribe Wiggum: This changes Go to Jail to allow players to bribe Chief Wiggum, giving you a chance to earn a bigger reward, but not without introducing an element of unpredictability.

Simpsons chance cards: The chance card collection grows with over 50 Simpsons-themed cards full of memes, references and one-liners from the show.

If you're excited to jump in tomorrow, be sure to check out these Free Monopoly Go Dice Links before you dive into the new content.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, katsuhiro Harada, formerly director on the Tekken series, is known for not pulling his punches.

  • According to recent reports, the panel were asked about the advantages of console development, as well as specific challenges when creating games for certain platforms.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, katsuhiro Harada, formerly director on the Tekken series, is known for not pulling his punches. This truth was reinforced recently, as he said he wished the Xbox Series S "wouldn't be released" at a developer panel. All while a member of the Xbox team was in the room.

Per Inven Global, Harada was sitting on a panel at the Console Game Developers Conference 2026 in South Korea. The panel was moderated by former Sony president Shuhei Yoshida, and featured Shift Up CTO DongKi Lee (Stellar Blade), Too Kyo Games CEO Kazutaka Kodaka (Dangenrompa), CD Projekt Red associate game director Paweł Sasko (Cyberpunk 2077), Ludeon Studios CEO Tynan Sylvester (Rimworld), and of course CEO of the newly formed VS Studio Katsuhiro Harada (Tekken).

According to recent reports, the panel were asked about the advantages of console development, as well as specific challenges when creating games for certain platforms. Harada led the charge, speaking to the advantages consoles provide for fighting game developers, as the hardware is ideal for tournaments and esports events. Following this, he took an opportunity to speak about a console that drew his ire.

"That noted, there's something I really want to say while I have the floor. Since a senior Xbox official is actually in attendance here today, I wish hardware like the Xbox Series S wouldn't be released," Harada said (translations to English via Inven Global). Harada then asked Sasko from the CD Projekt Red team whether he was "upset inside" because of the Xbox Series S.

Sasko proceeded to "burst out laughing" according to Inven Global, before responding: "It constantly throws challenges at us and forces us to optimize our code very cleanly.".

Industry observers note that harada followed up with additional thoughts: "You just used a very polite and elegant way to say "Xbox Series S sucks," right? (laughs) Low memory is an concern, but the hardest part is that it's a device so similar to Series X while having awkwardly lower performance. When porting to Switch 2, developers can shift their mindset to 'Switch 2 is a distinct device for Nintendo fans!' But with Xbox, after delivering your absolute best output, it feels like having to do extra work for a slightly weaker child.

It has been revealed that "Furthermore, in markets like the US, there are more Series S users than Series X users, so we can't just cut corners. Yet after launch, Series S users direct their complaints at us developers rather than Microsoft, asking 'Why is texture resolution lower only on Series S?'".

Sasko stepped up to offer some perks to the Series S. While he agreed that many players the full technical context behind the Series S' weaknesses, he pointed out that optimisation for weaker hardware like the Series S made games run "significantly better" across all platforms. He even had a Cyberpunk 2077 example, as optimisation work done for the Switch 2 version were applied to all platforms "to great effect". Sasko also pointed to the affordability side of the argument, saying that the cheaper price of the Series S allows for market expansion.

Recent findings suggest that harada responded: "Director Paweł packaged Series S so gracefully that the Microsoft representative in the audience keeps nodding along. I'm worried they'll feel reassured and release a successor like 'Helix S' for the next-gen Xbox as well (laughs).".

It has been revealed that here, Shift Up's DongKi Lee ended the topic with some optimism for Microsoft's future consoles: "Personally, I am looking forward to the next-gen Xbox 'Helix'. From an engineer's standpoint, if you provide us with a dev kit first in Korea as early as possible, we will put in our best efforts to develop for it.".

Earlier this year Harada founded Vs Studio with SNK's support, with other veterans from Bandai Namco's Tekken team hopping on board for whatever it's working on. As for the Xbox Helix consoles, in this current hardware environment with bloated costs for RAM and other components, it's reportedly looking a tad expensive. Maybe a Series S equivalent is on the cards?

SPOILERS ahead for Eternally Yours, now streaming with a Paramount+ subscription, with new episodes dropping on Thursdays.

I knew Eternally Yours would be one of my favorite fresh demonstrates on the 2026 TV schedule ever since it premiered, but in the past few weeks, my love for the show has doubled. And that’s all to do with the impressive amount of exciting setups I’m seeing from the comedy. It’s also so nice to have a new vampire family to follow after all my Twilight rewatches.

Industry observers note that given Eternally Yours is a half-hour comedy, you’d think it wouldn’t lean into a larger storyline until later on, but the fact that it does makes me feel confident about the quality and longevity of the series from the creators of Ghosts. Let’s talk about three big developments that I think are being laid out already in Season One.

It has been revealed that fresh comedies can be difficult to get on board with early because oftentimes they need some time to settle in, and not every network or streaming service is willing to bet on them. Eternally Yours has been killing it with its Season One rollout, and is expected to be renewed (per TV Insider). One plotline that has me excited to tune in for more episodes is what happened in Episode 4, “Halloween”.

In the episode from a couple of weeks ago, we learn about something called the Wolfsbane Chalice, which the vampire coven has been in possession of for many years. Basically, it helps protect them from werewolf attacks. While most of the episode revolves around some of the coven thinking Max allowed it to be lost, it was Phyllis who used it for a special Halloween drink and accidentally broke it. I’m convinced this is setting up a confrontation with werewolves, and it’s not the only clue so far.

Industry observers note that that brings me to Episode 6, “Eternal Sunshine of Phyllis’s Mind,” where I think two developments that will have a payoff later came up. The first is the flashback for Emma, where we learn that she had a werewolf stalker named Larry who killed off a number of her boyfriends. Between the loss of the Wolfsbane Chalice and this story, I’m convinced either the finale or an episode down the line will see the return of Larry in the present day, who comes out to get Emma’s fresh man, Max.

In a recent development, the final setup, which is definitely my favorite, also comes from last week’s episode. Phyllis is one of the best parts of Eternally Yours so far, but I was curious if they would address how messed up it is that her memories are always being wiped.

Your Daily Blend of Entertainment News.

Thankfully, “Eternal Sunshine of Phyllis’s Mind” not only brought it up, but it seemingly fixed the problem when Jesse decides to tell his wife he’s a vampire at the end of the episode. While I thought Phyllis not knowing she’s in a vampire coven would last for a while, now that it’s not, I’m actually so excited about what happens next.

Sources indicate that it’s going to be hilarious to watch as Phyllis unpacks the secret world she lives in, and I’ll be curious if she decides whether she wants to be a vampire, too. I also wonder if her finding out will also create more problems for the coven, like her accidentally telling a werewolf?

I’m honestly so astonished at how many exciting plot lines Eternally Yours has been setting up in just six episodes, and I can’t wait for the rest of the season.

Sarah El-Mahmoud has been with CinemaBlend since 2018 after graduating from Cal State Fullerton with a degree in Journalism. In college, she was the Managing Editor of the award-winning college paper, The Daily Titan, where she specialized in writing/editing long-form features, profiles and arts & entertainment coverage, including her first run-in with movie reporting, with a phone interview with Guillermo del Toro for Best Picture winner, The Shape of Water. Now she's into covering YA television and movies, and plenty of horror. Word webslinger. All her writing should be read in Sarah Connor’s Terminator 2 voice over.

Industry News: Horu is a sci-fi 4X RTS inspired by Star Wars: Empire at War in which spaceships are spellcasters who can summon black holes

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (562 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rockpapershotgun

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that clicking a random link this morning, I was dazzled by the glare of a thousand laser batteries firing simultaneously.
  • It has been revealed that but then I realised that I wasn't looking at a live newsfeed, but merely the Steam page for Horu, a real-time 4X strategy game in which you can "command hundreds of thousands of units across land and space", in the summary of developer David "GlassBeaver" Nadaski.
  • In development for years, and running on a custom C++ engine, Horu is inspired by 2006 hybrid RTS Star Wars: Empire at War - good, not great, in the words of turncoat jankonaut Graham, and the subject of many mods.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that clicking a random link this morning, I was dazzled by the glare of a thousand laser batteries firing simultaneously. My ears trembled beneath the trundle of a million caterpillar tracks. Balls of ice, bolts of lightning, shipments of rare alloys, and cascades of drop pods went screaming down my nerves and detonated in my frontal cortex, painting starlanes across the inside of my skull. "Oh god, they've finally found us!" I yelled, hiding beneath my desk. "I for one welcome our new galactic overlords!".

It has been revealed that but then I realised that I wasn't looking at a live newsfeed, but merely the Steam page for Horu, a real-time 4X strategy game in which you can "command hundreds of thousands of units across land and space", in the summary of developer David "GlassBeaver" Nadaski. There's also a magic system, this being "the spice that makes your enemy's defeat bitter", which is a very genteel way to characterise glaciating a tank formation or conjuring a miniature blackhole.

In development for years, and running on a custom C++ engine, Horu is inspired by 2006 hybrid RTS Star Wars: Empire at War - good, not great, in the words of turncoat jankonaut Graham, and the subject of many mods. Horu's way of bettering Empire at War is seemingly to add a shedload more of everything. You can engage in a fleet battle that looks like two migrating ant hives colliding, even as a frankly unnecessary quantity of cyborgs pour over the forgeworld beneath and get their shit kicked in by some tornado-summoning sorcerers.

Industry observers note that offensives appear to work like this: any drop ships that push through the fleet battle add meat to the ground invasion, with the option of deploying wormholes to sneak your troops behind the defending armada. On the ground, you're basically out to capture control points. You're allegedly spared from "continuous babysitting" by semi-autonomous squadron commanders and an orders system that lets you queue up objectives, before units engage in battle.

Industry observers note that you can still give individual orders to units, but that seems like a recipe for acute wrist injury. There's also a boarding action mechanic whereby your hijackers move through vessels room by room. Again, I struggle to understand how you'll have time and dexterity to oversee such skulduggery when there are a bajillion particle cannons going off all at once.

Industry observers note that outside of combat, there are planets to develop, shipyards to build, spy networks to groom, research trees to water, and stock markets to manipulate. It all looks like business as usual for an imperial 4X. Honestly, I can imagine the maximalist warfaring being a hot mess, and then there's the fact that the dev is running a Kickstarter "to fund the remaining assets needed for a playable build: more spaceships, more units, more animations, more sounds, more music, and everything in between." I've been burned by Kickstarter overpromising before. Still, I can only admire the vindictive intellect that would have me play a little game of FTL inside what looks like one of the larger PvP scraps from Eve Online.

You can read more on Steam. Release date there is currently none. For an equally populous strategy experience that's closer in style to Supreme Commander, check out Sanctuary: Shattered Space.

Hell Let Loose's original developers' Napoleonic-era extraction game, Hunger, gets December early access release, and an open beta this month

📅 11 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 1 min read (294 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Eurogamer

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, good Fun Corp, the studio made up of the original developers behind Hell Let Loose, has finally unveiled a release date for its anticipated next project: Hunger.
  • Hunger's first and only open beta has also been announced, taking place 27th-29th November, the weekend prior to its early access launch.
  • Though it may appear as yet another extraction shooter on the surface, Hunger offers more complex and intertwined systems than most.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, good Fun Corp, the studio made up of the original developers behind Hell Let Loose, has finally unveiled a release date for its anticipated next project: Hunger. The extraction shooter-slasher game enters early access on Steam on 3rd December, and there's good news if you're eager to try it out before then.

Hunger's first and only open beta has also been announced, taking place 27th-29th November, the weekend prior to its early access launch. Unlike past tests, this one is available for anyone who requests access on Steam.

Though it may appear as yet another extraction shooter on the surface, Hunger offers more complex and intertwined systems than most. For one, combat has a focus on melee with only a few intentionally clunky firearms available. Though this is a PvPvE game, the vs environment side includes the sort of puzzle-solving, questing and dungeon-raiding typical of RPGs. The game's alternate history, plague-ravaged European setting gives it a grimey, steel-and-mud look few games have.

Beyond the in-match experience, Good Fun's ambitions extend to Hunger's MMO-style progression, its hub area with distinct characters and varied playable classes - all of which can be sampled in the upcoming beta.

Industry observers note that hunger just came off a very successful closed beta, which clearly didn't suffer by kicking off right alongside Modern Warfare 4's DMZ early access. Hunger is currently among Steam's most-wishlisted games, with over 700,000 wishlists, according to the developer.

Industry observers note that the launch version includes three large maps, six playable characters, and five Mastery trees with more than 100 Masteries to unlock for your characters. Hunger has only been unveiled for PC so far, but will presumably arrive on consoles following its early access journey.

Original Story: We've already talked a little bit about the Newly introduced Zealand trick and how it's pretty much the number one topic on social media when it comes to Xbox and GTA 6 right now, so it's naive to think nobody's going to try it this Wednesday.

If you're not in the loop, this refers to people changing their region on Xbox to access GTA 6 at local midnight time in Upcoming Zealand, which equates to 6am EST / 11am GMT on Wednesday, November 18th.

Over the past couple of days, there's been a ton of debate online about whether it's "OK" or "safe" to switch regions in order to play GTA 6 early on Xbox Series X and Xbox Series S, and if you listen to what the majority say, the answer is that Xbox "don't care" if you do it, and that it's happened on many occasions without bans in the past.

However, it's true that Xbox specifically states in its TOCs that you shouldn't change regions unless you've actually moved to the country in question, and over on X/Twitter today, Windows Central editor Jez Corden and YouTuber Colt Eastwood revealed that they talked about this exact topic during a recent visit to Xbox's headquarters in Seattle.

Here's what they had to say about it in response to another of WC's writers (apologies for the profanity in the tweet!):.

A lot of people still believe that the risk is extremely low though, with some even arguing that it's "fear mongering" to suggest that Xbox will start suspending or banning people for wanting to play GTA 6 a few hours early.

There are others in the industry, such as The Verge editor Tom Warren, who also believe it's a non-matter:.

The reality is that nobody knows for sure whether Xbox will take action against people switching their consoles to Upcoming Zealand to play GTA 6 early this Wednesday, but based on historical evidence, it seems pretty unlikely.

Sources indicate that is it worth taking the risk though? That's the bit we'll leave up to you, and speaking personally, I would never want to recommend doing something like this in case Microsoft suddenly decides to throw the ban hammer around.

Let's wait and see how it all pans out on Wednesday, eh?

Sources indicate that are you using the Upcoming Zealand trick for GTA 6? Are you worried about the risks? Tell us below.

#51719. Industry News: Guide: 50 Best Wii Games Of All Time

📅 03 Nov 2020 • ⏱️ 27m • 📚 Deep Dive (5375 w)
