Industry News: Guide: 50 Best Wii Games Of All Time

📅 03 Nov 2020 | ⏱️ 27 min read (5375 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nintendolife

⏱️ ~27 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, 19th November 2026 marks the 20th anniversary of Wii's Japanese launch, so it's the perfect time to revisit our list of the best games on the system.
  • Nintendo changed the game with Wii, the little motion-controlled console which broke away from the competition and started a revolution.
  • Despite its reputation as a casual, 'kiddy' console, the huge library of Wii games has some of the most fantastic and varied titles on any system, and the very best Nintendo Wii games took advantage of its unique features in brilliant ways.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, 19th November 2026 marks the 20th anniversary of Wii's Japanese launch, so it's the perfect time to revisit our list of the best games on the system. Keep an eye out for more Revolution-ary features coming later today and over the weekend!

Nintendo changed the game with Wii, the little motion-controlled console which broke away from the competition and started a revolution. Its brilliantly compact design (the size of three DVD boxes, remember?) and approachable controller helped it open up gaming to a whole latest audience, young and old alike.

Despite its reputation as a casual, 'kiddy' console, the huge library of Wii games has some of the most fantastic and varied titles on any system, and the very best Nintendo Wii games took advantage of its unique features in brilliant ways.

To highlight the best of the best, we've compiled the following list of our top 50 Wii games ever.

Releasing at the zenith of the plastic instrument craze, Guitar Hero III: Legends of Rock on Wii intergrated the Wii Remote's rumble and speaker into the gameplay — hardly a game changer, but a welcome addition in a game which plays largely the same regardless of platform. Rock on.

One of the very best 3D Sonic games in our books, Sonic Colors managed to translate the classic 2D gameplay and introduce a gimmick that complimented rather than disrupted that gameplay.

The Wisp power-ups gave Sonic upcoming abilities which tied in beautifully to some strong level design and delivered the best Sonic experience we'd ever had in three dimensions. Also available in Ultimate form on Switch.

Bringing two-player cooperative play to the series' chaotic mix of surgery, touch/pointer-based gameplay and drama that makes ER look like a trip to the school nurse, Trauma Center: Latest Blood made you feel like a regular Dr. Clooney with a Wiimote in your hand instead of a scalpel. It also featured proper character dialogue and diabolical schemes behind the scenes. Let's just hope it's not this dramatic in a real Emergency Room.

It has been revealed that and yes, we know the character's name in ER wasn't Dr. Clooney. We know and we don't care.

Pandora’s Tower delivers an involving resource and time-management RPG experience with an imaginative action and combat system. Its overall aesthetic, as well as its focus on a relationship between two characters, are bold design choices that work well as long as you’re willing to invest in the game world.

In a recent development, it’s a pity that the experience, most notably the action segments that take up a large part of the 12-15 hour adventure, are partially undermined by technical failings. As a result, it’s questionable whether many will engage in multiple playthroughs in pursuit of happier endings.

Still, Pandora's Tower has much to recommend it, as long as you’re willing to look beyond some of its faults.

There are plentiful ways to enjoy Cave Story these days, and none of them are bad.

The WiiWare version will be mighty difficult to get hold of if you don't already own it and have it downloaded (the Wii Shop is no longer in operation), but regardless of where or how you play this indie platforming gem, it comes heartily recommended - and this version was a winner.

A purist might argue that Rock Band 3 suffered from some bloat where its predecessor offered the most streamlined four-man bandplay ever. Each to their own, of course, but when you look at Rock Band 2's playlist and streamlining of the basic experience offered in Harmonix's first entry in the series, the purists might have a point.

SEGA found a new home for its light gun games on Wii, and House of the Dead 2 & 3 Return was a must-have title for fans of the series or genre - two classic games fused together perfectly.

It has been revealed that although House of the Dead 2 now feels a little dated, its younger zombie-brother remains excellent, a gore-fest with hours upon hours of zombie-blasting arcade action. Depth and longevity seekers need not apply and should be redirected to a close cousin, Capcom's Resident Evil: The Umbrella Chronicles.

Some might say this is the finest version of the finest Pikmin game, offering the best of all worlds with Wii Remote pointer functionality and a surprisingly good multiplayer component, too.

The sequel might make the fruit look tastier in gorgeous HD, but Pikmin 2 is still the gold standard of the series in our book, whether you play on GameCube, with some Newly introduced Play Control! on Wii, or on Switch.

Winding back the clock to Mega Man's NES roots with a potent throwback, Inti Creates and Capcom tapped into our nostalgia beautifully with Mega Man 9, returning the bombardier bleu to his original 8-bit stylings in the first numbered entry in the original series for 12 years.

In a recent development, simply making it look authentic wouldn't have been enough, though. Fortunately, Inti Creates crafted a tight little run-and-gun platformer worthy of bearing that hallowed digit.

An early showcase of the Wii Remote (or the 'Form Baton' as it's known in-game), WarioWare Smooth Moves brought the anarchic micro-gameplay and aesthetic of the handheld series to the Wii in an entry which surely ranks as the most widely played of any WarioWare title.

You never quite knew what was coming next, and this ranks up there alongside Wii Sports as an off-the-wall demonstration of the console's potential in those first few months.

The Wii might not be the first system that springs to mind when asked to think of classic horror games, but Silent Hill: Shattered Memories is up there with the greatest titles in the genre — all the better for really making use of its host console's features, whether it's the speaker in the controller or intelligent use of motion controls to draw you into this reimagining of the Silent Hill series' first entry.

There's really only one thing you need to know about Red Steel 2, and that is that the sword combat absolutely, positively delivers in the way you want it to.

The rest of the game does have some challenges and without the stellar controls would have been more of a step sideways rather than forward for the genre, but shooting and slicing dudes is just too much fun to pass up.

A foul-mouthed, gorily stylised 'lightgun' shooter in the B-movie mould, The House of the Dead: Overkill has its tongue impaled through its cheek and is best served with buckets of popcorn.

It's yet another slice of mature entertainment on that most family-friendly of consoles, and further proof that the breadth of genres found in Wii's software library was second to none.

World of Goo is a masterful game which marries addictive physics-based puzzling with a fun gooey aesthetic and some biting social commentary to produce one of the best-ever games on Wii or whatever system it appears on.

Industry observers note that this special game was a 10 then, it's a 10 now, and shall always remain a 10. And the IR pointer in the original game still trumps the gyro-based equivalent (which needs frequent recentering) and the touchscreen option in the Switch re-release. Just spectacularly good.

Industry observers note that nintendo missed out on any GTAs on its home consoles, but Rockstar's Bully was much more than a consolation prize. Set in the Bullworth Academy, aspiring miscreant Jimmy Hopkins must negotiate the pitfalls and perils of private school life in an open world game that plays a little like a teenage GTA. The Molotov cocktails are replaced with stinkbombs, the AK47s with slingshots.

With an appropriately mischievous and juvenile setting (which arguably suits the sandbox gameplay even better than GTA's mature mayhem), this was a great addition to the 'mature' shelf in the console's library.

Another awkward transition to the TV screen for a game which began life on a handheld, we wouldn't recommend playing the WiiWare version of Phoenix Wright: Ace Attorney - Trials & Tribulations these days — besides the fact that you can no longer access the Wii Shop, there are too many excellent alternative ways to play.

This port really should have included pointer controls, but even given its sloppy presentation on Wii, the base game is still pretty ace.

There may have been some initial resistance to Visceral’s decision to turn Dead Space into a rail shooter, but the final product is so well-crafted that you can’t help but be impressed by the level of quality it delivers.

Dead Space: Extraction manages to come through on its promise of a cinematic experience by embracing the genre’s limitations and bending the expectations of what an on-rails game can and should do, all the while playing to the Wii’s strengths and pushing its technical abilities to newly introduced highs.

While the main story mode may lack in longevity for some, Extraction is definitely worth experiencing at least once, and it’s a title that horror and shooter fans alike shouldn’t miss.

Now available to play on Switch along with its predecessor, No More Heroes 2: Desperate Struggle continues the stylish (mis)adventures of Travis Touchdown in a sequel infused with the same punk-aesthetic, referential humour and sassy surrealism as the first game, except with the splintered edges sanded down to a still-pleasingly rough-and-ready finish.

Sources indicate that next Level Games managed to recapture all the character and energy of the original Punch-Out!! on Wii while adding a beautiful cel-shaded graphical style.

With all the fighters from the NES game returning, the motion controls were cute, if a little hit-and-miss, but the option to play using the old-school control style made this a truly excellent upgrade of a classic boxer where it's all about watching your opponent.

An excellent little explorative RTS game that holds its own against the Pikmin series.

According to recent reports, you're put in charge of a village and it's your job to ensure your citizens' happiness while expanding your kingdom upwards and outwards. Little King's Story is one of those games that is loved by all who play it, yet remains one of Wii's many 'hidden' gems.

If it sounds at all enticing, we recommend tracking down a copy while they're easy to source — you won't regret it.

A gorgeous side-on action RPG, 2009's Muramasa: The Demon Blade was ahead of the wave of side-scrolling platformers that would arrive from indie studios over the next few years, and Vanillaware's eye-catching adventure through Japanese folklore is still a treat many years later.

Combining the original two Lego Star Wars trilogies from the GameCube era, the now-misleadingly named LEGO Star Wars: The Complete Saga offers hours of low-barrier family fun with dozens of playable characters blasting and lightsaber-ing their way through galactic locales, all to the sound of John Williams' iconic score.

This Danish plastic take on the series was infused with charm from the beginning. Reimagining key scenes from the six movies in silent slapstick (and with DS versions of all of them scaling the games down in a generally admirable fashion), the Lego characters and the comedic, playful tone of the entire game made it a great co-op experience to blast through with friends or younger relatives.

The moveset might be small, but that can't be remarked for the roster. We can honestly say that leaping around with a Force-infused Yoda (who usually hobbles with a cane) like some crazy, laser-sword-wielding frog is some of the most fun lightsaber combat we've ever engaged in. The fancy-pants newer version on Switch might be better overall, but the original 'complete' Lego Star Wars remains hugely accessible and still brings a smile to our face.

Before the sublime Rayman Legends, there was the sublime Rayman Origins.

A 2D platformer par excellence (as they say in Ubisoft's homeland), the limbless wonder always had an impressive heritage in the platforming genre, but this arguably raised him up alongside the invention and beauty of Nintendo's own offerings — perhaps even higher if you ask players who aren't fans of Super Mario's 'Newly introduced' adventures.

A Wii port of the 2002 GameCube remake featuring upcoming controls, Resident Evil (or Resident Evil Archives: Resident Evil to give its full title) provides what we came to expect from Wii re-releases of previous-gen titles: a more accessible, incrementally improved control experience with box art that's a bit rubbish.

Just concentrate on the horror of the game rather than the horror of the box and you're golden.

PlatinumGames' MadWorld presented an inky black-and-white aesthetic highlighting the ultra-violence of the action whenever red blood sprayed across the screen. Which happened a lot.

Tapping into the visual style of Frank Miller's dark graphic novel Sin City, MadWorld is another example that the Wii's reputation as a family-friendly console, though warranted, is only partially correct. In fact, it had an incredibly varied catalogue and this Sega-published hack-and-slash brawler was a fine example.

Capcom's adventure Zack & Wiki — a cute pirate/monkey combo — never came to another console, but it's absolutely worth seeking out.

In a recent development, point-and-click is the name of the game - if you fondly remember Sam and Max or Day of the Tentacle, you will be at home here. You use the Wii Remote to point at the screen and press 'A' to move Zack to that location and check items. When you need to interact with an object, though, you'll need to use gestures (so, to saw down a tree, you need to move the remote forward and backwards repeatedly, etc).

You'd think this would get old fast, but this is a fantastic little adventure and was another great showcase for the hardware back in 2007.

A sequel to Treasure's cult classic N64 rail shooter (which didn't make it to the West until it appeared on Wii's Virtual Console in 2007), this sequel improves on the experience and is arguably the better of the two games — yet another fantastic addition to a huge and impressively varied console library.

We're thankful we didn't have to resort to importing this one back in the day.

A 20th anniversary collection of some of the most popular Kirby games ever, 2012's Kirby's Dream Collection: Special Edition spans the puffball's debut on Game Boy through his NES and SNES adventures and also includes his N64 outing; so, that's Kirby's Dream Land, Kirby's Dream Land 2, Kirby's Adventure, Kirby's Dream Land 3, Kirby Super Star and Kirby 64: The Crystal Shards in one very convenient package.

According to recent reports, convenient for Japanese and North American players, that is — it never saw the light of day in PAL regions. Cue our sad European Kirby eyes.

A poor port of a great game, we can only assume residual affection for the original software itself is elevating the WiiWare releases in your estimations.

Phoenix Wright: Ace Attorney is a corker, but of the myriad ways available to play it these days, this is probably the last version we'd recommend.

Super Paper Mario blends classic platformer with some of the RPG elements of its predecessors and throws in a world-flipping mechanic that gives you a whole latest perspective on traditional 2D platforming courses. It diverges heavily from Thousand-Year Door's way of doing things, and as a result, divides series fans.

Regardless of where you fall on the spectrum of fandom, the Wii entry is a beautiful game with fiendish puzzles and an intriguing, unique flip mechanic.

Recent findings suggest that A co-development between Intelligent Systems and Nintendo SPD, Radiant Dawn is a direct sequel to Path of Radiance and could even accept save data brought over from its predecessor which boosted character stats. It was well worth doing, too, as Radiant Dawn was noted for its high difficulty and any advantage was welcome.

This Wii entry brought back dark magic into the fold and increased the scope and number of characters in comparison to Path of Radiance, but wasn't the sales success Nintendo had hoped.

Recent findings suggest that despite being proclaimed as absolute pinnacles of the series, with many fans citing one of these two as their franchise favourites, the GameCube and Wii entries represented a low point sales-wise, which unfortunately signalled a retreat back to portable hardware only. Indeed, it would be 12 years until the series would grace a television screen once again.

Recent findings suggest that the first 2D entry to come to a home console since Mario World in the early '90s, 2009's Upcoming Super Mario Bros. Wii brought chaotic — a little too chaotic for some — four-player local multiplayer to the series for the first time.

This game gave old-school fans yearning for a side-on Mushroom Kingdom adventure something to chew on, with plenty of clever nods to the past, although as with the rest of the 'Fresh' series, you could argue that the visual presentation was a little bland. Cracking music in this one, though.

Arriving in a red Wii case which really made it stand out on the shelf, anyone put off by the Newly introduced series' 'wah's and cuteness missed out on a real platforming treat in NSMB Wii.

No More Heroes certainly isn’t perfect; the tasks you’re given in between missions are dull (calling to mind the same boredom experienced when you had to get a job in Sega’s Shenmue), the Grant Theft Auto-style driving sections border on pointless (we can only assume they’re intended to be a thinly-veiled dig at the successful franchise), and the general gameplay doesn’t actually change during any of the assassination missions.

In a recent development, but regardless of these points, it still entertains in a way that few other games can manage. It’s a chaotic riot packed with gleeful videogame references, over-the-top dialogue, and some seriously awesome-looking combat action.

A far more accessible proposition than Killer7 ever was, No More Heroes is so wonderfully amusing that it’s easy to forgive its minor shortcomings; Suda 51’s epic fully deserved to garner the kind of attention and praise that unfortunately eluded its predecessor.

Coming from Hironobu Sakaguchi, the creator of Final Fantasy, The Last Story was an impressive RPG and one of the last big releases for the system. While it struggled from a technical perspective at times, it's an ambitious title that's worth playing today if you missed out back in 2012.

Along with Xenoblade Chronicles and Pandora's Tower, it's also notable as one of the titles North American players campaigned to see released in that territory — Nintendo, who published that game elsewhere, eventually granted XSEED publishing rights and it introduced six months after PAL regions.

Taking Kirby back to his classic game style following a couple of genre departures, Kirby's Return to Dream Land was a worthy return and yet another glittering gem in the Wii's platforming lineup.

With all the colour and creativity you'd expect from HAL, and a ton of content to delve into, this was a wonderful trip to Kirby's land of dreams.

A gorgeous, low-stress game that transports Kirby into a world of fabric and thread, Kirby's Epic Yarn was the first of Good-Feel's material-based platformers and is arguably still the best.

We adore it. Anyone who notes it's lacking in the challenge department is correct... but missing the point entirely. Kirby's Epic Yarn is one of the most joyous and creative games on Wii, or indeed any platform. (It's also available on 3DS in Extra Epic form.).

You played it, your mum played it, your granddad played it; more to the point, you all enjoyed it. Drawing people in with a gimmick is relatively easy, but Wii Sports managed to genuinely entertain entire families and get them playing video games together for an extended period — perhaps for the first time ever.

This pack-in brought huge numbers of people together in silly Mii form and showcased the potential of motion controls to gamers from all generations. It's quite simply one of the most key video games ever made, and the most killer of apps.

Introducing Wii Remote control into Retro's Prime template, Metroid Prime 3: Corruption was an excellent conclusion to the trilogy (well, until the next entry turned up 18 years later to make it a quadrilogy a tetralogy four), a series that proved Samus could not only survive the jump into 3D first-person shooting, but absolutely flourish in that genre.

According to recent reports, originally planned as a Wii launch title, but pushed to August 2007 (a delay? For a Metroid Prime game? Inconceivable!), Prime 3: Corruption as a separate release was subsequently rendered a tad redundant with the launch of the entire trilogy on one glorious disc, but this is still a cracking shooter on its own.

Showcasing the chonky new MotionPlus accessory (eventually built into the updated Wii Remote Plus), Wii Sports Resort offered the kind of motion-tracking fidelity many of us had imagined the Wii would offer out of the gate.

Highlights of this game — which introduced Wuhu Island and expanded on the original game with a bunch of fresh activities — included fencing and throwing a frisbee for an adorable pooch.

Following the online exploits of Mario Kart DS, it was almost a given that Mario Kart Wii would follow suit and include the ability to play against the world — thankfully, despite the console's rather anaemic online capabilities, the experience was nothing short of stunning.

From the outside, the Wii entry might have sacrificed some of the kart racing series' personality, but the online multiplayer with support for up to twelve players, optional motion controls (who could forget that plastic wheel accessory?), and additional vehicles and characters helped make it one of the most accessible entries in the series.

According to recent reports, successful, too. It sold a staggering 37.38 million copies.

In a recent development, this revival of Rare's treasured Donkey Kong Country series came after developer Retro Studios had successfully reinvented Nintendo's Metroid as an exploratory first-person shooter, so we shouldn't have been surprised that the team was able to recapture the spirit of that 16-bit platformer series three console generations later with Donkey Kong Country Returns. However, just how good the 2010 game turned out still came as a massive shock.

The 3DS port was equally impressive, although having played the excellent Tropical Freeze, it's tougher to return (ahem) to Returns these days, even Forever Entertainment's Switch port which combines the two versions into an HD dish with the tiniest dusting of tweaks.

Still, when it comes to resurrections, Retro was Nintendo's go-to studio for a long minute there and DKC swung back in fabulous form on Wii.

The third entry in the scrap-'em-up series, Super Smash Bros. Brawl was the first to introduce Sonic the Hedgehog and Solid Snake, and included the lauded Subspace Emissary mode.

Picking up the baton from the celebrated GameCube entry, Brawl pushed the series in an all-encompassing direction as far as content was concerned, and set the precedent for the 'more is more' approach to stages, fighters, music, and more that kept Masahiro Sakurai occupied eight days a week for many years after.

Showcasing the sort of swordplay we'd hoped Twilight Princess would contain, The Legend of Zelda: Skyward Sword was a beautiful entry in the series which dared to try some newly introduced ideas, something the franchise desperately needed at the time.

It arguably didn't get everything right, and why Nintendo ditched the beautifully accurate IR pointer in favour of a gyro alternative which required constant re-centering — especially when everyone already had the IR sensor hooked up anyway! — is still a source of confusion for us. We found the MotionPlus swordplay itself excellent, though.

Sources indicate that chronologically, this is the very first game in the Zelda timeline, so it's pretty much required reading for series fans. While it has its naysayers, we look back on our time with Skyward Sword very fondly.

Sources indicate that this was arguably the game which proved that third parties had mastered the grammar of the 3D language Nintendo invented with Ocarina of Time. Okami is a gorgeous Japanese adventure with an oddball cast of characters, fabulous music, and an unforgettable art style.

The HD version on Switch is probably the best way to play these days, but the Wii port of Clover's PS2 original was a delight back in 2008.

A remarkable breath of fresh air for a franchise that was getting a little stale, this put the Resident Evil series on an action-based path away from the fixed-camera, pre-rendered, 'staged' survival horror of the previous games.

What you lost in nail-biting tension was more than made up for by the brilliantly chunky gunplay and impeccable progression through a story that continually ups the ante and adjusts difficulty automatically to keep you on the edge of your seat without pushing you off entirely.

While the additional pointer controls arguably make the Wii version a little too easy, you've still got the option to play with a GameCube controller if you wish (or that chainsaw variant if you're proper hardcore). Subsequent remasters might have upped the resolution, and the remake is a marvel in its own right, but there's a genuine argument that the Wii Edition of Resident Evil 4 remains the best way to play this genre-defining classic, even all these years later.

As groundbreaking as it was, the 3D Zelda formula was starting to look a little tired by the mid-2000s, so while Twilight Princess is a very fine game, it lacked the impact of its predecessors.

In a recent development, the additional 'waggle' implemented in the Wii version didn't live up to the ideas of 1:1 swordplay we'd imagined, either. And did the entire world really need mirroring just to make Link right-handed? Still, at the time this was the only way to play the game in 16:9 and it made for a satisfyingly meaty Wii launch title in North America.

Not one for the purists, perhaps — you'll want to track down an expensive copy of the GameCube version for the left-handed, canonical geography of Hyrule (or just play Twilight Princess HD on Wii U).

2010's Xenoblade Chronicles was epic in scale and setting in a way few games of the era were, and this isn't a title to rush through. You'll need many hours to examine and enjoy its incredible complexity, enhancing your abilities and exploring the world's ecosystem as you go.

Industry observers note that the creativity Monolith Soft employed in producing this world was staggering. In terms of presentation, the immense landscapes remain a delight to traverse. While some close-up camera angles expose the Wii's graphical limitations, the art design more than compensates. Although some of the voice acting is hit-and-miss, the soundtrack is superb, genuinely enhancing the experience.

The sublime Definitive Edition on Switch is the easiest and best way to catch up with the first entry these days, but this game delivers a huge (and hugely enjoyable) JRPG experience wherever you play, laying a foundation that Monolith would build on with its sequels.

Collecting the original Prime trilogy in one handy package with upcoming Wii controls for the first two, difficulty options, and other enhancements for the earlier GameCube entries, Metroid Prime Trilogy is arguably one of the best compilation offerings in video games, ever.

The enhanced versions of the first two games were released separately in Japan as part of the Newly introduced Play Control! line, but in the West we got this thrilling uberdisc.

Purists may point to a handful of missing visual effects compared to the originals, and they're not wrong, but whichever way you look at it, this is a spectacular package - a great way to play these games, and a hardcore crown jewel on the most casual of consoles.

Industry observers note that with Super Mario Galaxy 2 Nintendo gave us that rarest of treats — a direct sequel to one of its finest games. While anyone who played and fell in love with Super Mario Galaxy would have been overjoyed to hear there was more on the way, the expectations couldn't have been higher. Somehow, Galaxy 2 expanded on the first game's inventiveness, turning up the colour dial to eleventy-stupid.

It has been revealed that this was EAD Tokyo tearing up the textbook and pasting it back together in fascinating, surprising ways, flexing its beefed-up, confidently creative muscles with a huge variety of environments and obstacles, plus Yoshi and a host of fresh power-ups. It's a brilliant time.

In a recent development, to argue over which Galaxy is better is pointless, really — they're both wonderful and utterly essential, so if you never got around to playing the sequel, carve out some time as soon as possible. Inexplicably, it was missing from the 3D All-Stars collection, but it arrived on Switch eventually. Even if it hadn't, this game is truly worth hunting down a Wii for.

Where Sunshine faltered, Super Mario Galaxy truly did shine. Taking Mario into space gave Nintendo the opportunity to play with gravity and give the character a whole newly introduced (final) frontier of planetoid playgrounds to blast between, setting the stage for endlessly creative snippets of platforming perfection.

All that aside, there's also Rosalina and the Lumas' story to enjoy if you go looking for it; an affecting and underrated aspect of an utterly sublime game.

It's available to play on Switch (in two flavours, in fact), and you really should — Super Mario Galaxy is an infectiously fun trip through the cosmos which begged the question: Where could the plumber possibly go next?

It has been revealed that and there we are — the finest Wii games available to humanity! Such a variety of genres and quality games from all developers, and so many we should catch up on.

Before we finish, let's answer some common questions readers have about the Wii and its catalogue.

The Wii release date was slightly different depending on where in the world you lived, although the three major territories all got it in 2006.

It launched first in North America, followed by Japan a couple of weeks later and the following week in Europe and Australasia.

Here's when Wii released in each of the three main territories:.

According to Wikipedia’s list of Wii games, a total of 1612 Nintendo Wii games were released for the console.

The exact number of releases varies depending on the territory (Europe, Japan, North America), but you'll find all Wii games listed by region on that page.

Industry observers note that this depends on the model you have. The original Wii is backwards compatible with GameCube games and has controller and memory card ports for its predecessor under the flap on the top side of the console.

Later Wii models — specifically the RVL-101 revision without a stand and the Wii Mini — removed backwards compatibility with GameCube games, unfortunately.

It has been revealed that according to Nintendo, Wii Sports is the best-selling Wii game, with 82.90 million copies sold. Wow!

It's worth remembering that Wii Sports has a pack-in with many Wii consoles (and Nintendo sold 101.64 million Wiis in total), so it's unsurprising that it's the most popular Wii game.

In terms of software that was sold separately, the next best-selling Wii game is Mario Kart Wii, which sold 37.38 million copies worldwide. In 2018, a decade after the game launched, we reported the figure as 37.14 million, which means Nintendo managed to shift a further 24,000 copies in the Switch era. Crazy!

You can check out Nintendo's Top 10 if you're interested in the rest of the Wii's best-sellers.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that jennifer Svedberg-Yen, lead writer of the hit 2025 RPG Clair Obscur: Expedition 33, has revealed that she is no longer with developer Sandfall Interactive.
  • Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 was universally acclaimed and won an astounding list of awards, including just about every narrative-focused prize you can name: Best Storytelling at the Golden Joysticks, Best Narrative at The Game Awards, Outstanding Achievement in Story at DICE, Best Narrative at the GDC Awards, Best Narrative at the BAFTAs, and Hugo and Nebula awards.
  • Despite Clair Obscur's success, Svedberg-Yen revealed that she moved on from the game, and the studio, earlier this year.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that jennifer Svedberg-Yen, lead writer of the hit 2025 RPG Clair Obscur: Expedition 33, has revealed that she is no longer with developer Sandfall Interactive. In an interview with Gamesbeat, Svedberg-Yen noted she wants to return to her own creative efforts, including stories for film and television, and also aims to set up a new fund specifically to support the advancement of narrative design in games.

Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 was universally acclaimed and won an astounding list of awards, including just about every narrative-focused prize you can name: Best Storytelling at the Golden Joysticks, Best Narrative at The Game Awards, Outstanding Achievement in Story at DICE, Best Narrative at the GDC Awards, Best Narrative at the BAFTAs, and Hugo and Nebula awards. That makes it particularly interesting that Clair Obscur is Svedberg-Yen's one and only game credit: Prior to joining Sandfall Interactive in 2020 as one of its earliest members, she spent years working in the finance industry.

Despite Clair Obscur's success, Svedberg-Yen revealed that she moved on from the game, and the studio, earlier this year. "I left Sandfall in July, after wrapping up some final stuff for Expedition," she said. "We’ve parted ways.".

That has to hurt for Sandfall, but Svedberg-Yen still has ambitions within the game industry, including the creation of an investment fund for "narrative-focused game creators, trying to bridge the gap between the seed stage and going to publishers.".

"This is the chicken and egg question a lot of people face," Svedberg-Yen said. "To get money from publishers you need a demo, but to make a demo you need money. To get money you have to go to publishers. That’s an area where I would like to help a lot of these smaller creatives to get that seed funding so they can, in a way, de-risk themselves in the eyes of bigger investors.

Sources indicate that "In that way I can also help them build a stronger narrative foundation from the beginning. I’ve done a lot of consulting work with different studios. I’ve discovered that quite a lot of studios don’t really know how to think about narrative, or how to integrate it into their pipelines and their processes. They tend to think it’s a very narrow thing, when in fact it can influence all aspects. Part of this would also be an incubation program to help these studios develop those narrative foundations.".

Svedberg-Yen said a lot of studios think of narrative as "a skin," something thrown on near the end of the development process once everything else is assembled. But that's like trying to solve a puzzle without knowing whether there's actually a solution at all, she continued, "whereas if you start from the very beginning, when everyone is starting from the same jumping-off point, everything will naturally be able to tie together.".

Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

The goal is not to compete with publishers, she explained, but "to find a way to work with them to get us back on solid ground. Above all, I really would like to champion other people and other creatives to have a chance to pursue their dreams, have a chance to make the games they want to make.".

Sources indicate that that investment fund, alongside her own projects and stories, will be Svedberg-Yen's primary focus in the coming year: "The strongest feeling in me right now for 2027 is I want to help. That sounds so cheesy and idealistic. I always cringe at myself for saying it. But I don’t know how else to say it and be truthful. I want to help in some way, help the industry.".

It has been revealed that andy has been gaming on PCs from the very beginning, starting as a youngster with text adventures and primitive action games on a cassette-based TRS80. From there he graduated to the glory days of Sierra Online adventures and Microprose sims, ran a local BBS, learned how to build PCs, and developed a longstanding love of RPGs, immersive sims, and shooters. He began writing videogame news in 2007 for The Escapist and somehow managed to avoid getting fired until 2014, when he joined the storied ranks of PC Gamer. #51717. The Geekom A5 2027 Edition represents solid value for the indie generalist seeking out a compact form factor

The Geekom A5 2027 Edition represents solid value for the indie generalist seeking out a compact form factor

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1698 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Gamesradar

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that the Geekom A5 2027 won't replace a Steam Machine, but it's not designed to.
  • Upgradeable RAM and SSD via easily accessible bays.
  • Why you can trust GamesRadar+ Our experts review games, movies and tech over countless hours, so you can choose the best for you.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that the Geekom A5 2027 won't replace a Steam Machine, but it's not designed to. This is an efficiency-focused productivity cube designed to see you through more casual workflows without breaking a sweat or pulling too much power. That means it won't zipping through Cyberpunk, but its handling of lighter indie and retro titles is still impressive.

Upgradeable RAM and SSD via easily accessible bays.

Chipset prioritizes efficiency over power.

Some ports slightly too close together.

Why you can trust GamesRadar+ Our experts review games, movies and tech over countless hours, so you can choose the best for you. Find out more about our reviews policy.

The Geekom A5 2027 doesn't want to be the answer to your Steam Machine woes. I've been road testing the mini PC with a gaming mindset but, in truth, this is productivity focused device that just so happens to handle indie and retro titles particularly well.

Sources indicate that with current PC prices ravaging the industry, and no signs of those inflated rates slowing down, anyone on the hunt for a day to day productivity machine will be keen to double up on their purchase. With prices sitting well below the rest of the PC gaming market ($549 / £469 for the configuration on my desk), the Geekom A5 2027 has an interesting proposition for those with an indie-focused Steam library.

Industry observers note that the latest in a line of budget-friendly mini PCs, the 2027-monikered device refreshes its chip with an AMD Ryzen 7 7730U, while also offering expandable memory and storage. That's all wrapped up in a compact, sturdy brick of a chassis with plenty of ports for all your day to day connections.

3x USB 3.2 Gen 2 Type-A, 2x USB 3.2 Gen 2 Type-C, 1x USB 2.0 Type-A, 2x HDMI 2.0, 1x 3.5mm audio, 1x 2.5G RJ45, 1x SD card reader.

The good thing about mini PCs is it's pretty difficult to make one that looks cheap. There are so few materials compared to the best gaming PCs on the market, higher quality builds are far more accessible at lower prices.

In a recent development, the Geekom A5 2027 falls into the same aesthetic step as its counterparts across the market, as well as its predecessors. This is a compact silver block with a tiny footprint on the desk. There's an extra air of luxury in those shiny metallic accents running around the perimeter, though, with a sturdy slightly mottled silver in the main casing.

It has been revealed that heat is mostly dispensed through vents to the rear, sitting above a set of fully labelled ports, with intake grills lining each side of the device. The bottom panel plays host to four user-removable screws, providing access to upgradeable SSD and memory bays with handy orientation information stamped into the plastic. Four rubberized feet house these screws, keeping the PC firmly in place on the desk.

Those after a mini PC for its portability will also be glad to see the tiny power adapter included. This power block is dwarfed by the units I often have to wrangle when testing the best gaming laptops, and makes for lightweight, easy backpack transport.

Sources indicate that geekom has outfitted the A5 2027 Edition with AMD's Ryzen 7 7730U chipset, alongside a cheaper Ryzen 5 7430U option. Configurations keep things conservative, with 16GB DDR4 RAM and 512GB SSDs dominating most listings (some are available with 256GB or 1TB SSD sticks).

According to recent reports, that processor tells us a lot about what Geekom wants you to be doing with its mini PC, though. The Ryzen 7 5825U refresh includes an integrated GPU, but it's not the Radeon 780M you'll find in a lot of gaming-focused mini PCs.

This is an octacore chip with 16 threads for lightweight but efficient processing, relying on a TDP of just 15W. Its use in slimline laptops over the years has given it plenty of time in the sun, but packaging it into a 2027-branded mini PC means Geekom is pitching its latest iteration as a power-efficient everyday productivity machine.

This isn't a rig designed to take on your Steam library, but it can certainly give lighter titles a go.

Using slower DDR4 RAM is going to take some of the sheen off if you're running more demanding workloads, though it is upgradeable to 64GB with a handy socketed design. That generational step down from DDR5 to DDR4 isn't going to be felt too keenly by most casual everyday uses, though. Under the hood, you'll also find space for two swappable NVMe SSDs, as well as a miniature SATA.

Ports remain plentiful as well. The front houses two USB-As with a 3.5mm audio out for easy access, all lined up in step with that glowing power button. The left panel holds that full-sized SD card reader. Two additional USB-As are at the rear, alongside two USB-Cs, two HDMI 2.0, an RJ45 and the power connection.

That's enough for a good selection of accessories, though I was a little frustrated that the two rear USB-A ports are aligned a little too close together. Chunkier cable connections struggle to sit on top of each other here, effectively rendering one of those ports redundant.

This is a cheaper iteration so there's no USB4 standard on the USB-Cs.

The Geekom A5 2027 Edition has been designed to confidently deliver seamless day to day productivity without breaking the bank, and this is where it excels. My workflow typically requires far too many Chrome tabs, separated in a splitscreen window, with image editing software and Spotify running in the background. The A5 barely broke a sweat.

Curiosity got the better of me when it came to testing the Geekom A5 2027's gaming performance, though. This is in no way a machine Geekom expects you to buy for its raw power, so my Cyberpunk 2077 tests are to be taken as an indication of upper limits rather than a condemnation of the product itself. Starting things off a little easier, though, I was glad to see those internals keeping up with lighter indie games particularly well.

According to recent reports, I could have been playing on a far more expensive machine when I booted up Stardew Valley and Islanders. Both titles ran smoothly, with no jagged edges, obviously dropped frames, or stutters - even when wildly panning around my poorly planned civilizations in the latter. Low-weight indies are this machine's bread and butter - if that's all you play, there's no reason to spend above the Geekom's price tag.

More demanding games are runnable but not entirely enjoyable.

Shadow of the Tomb Raider represents the mid-size titles that might have been in your Steam library for the last five to ten years. Games that don't stress too many GPUs in this day and age, but still represent a sizeable jump from lightweight indie titles.

To stay above 30fps here, we have to drop things down to their lowest possible settings - at 720p resolution. That's the point where Tomb Raider feels smooth enough to relax into, rather than constantly watching for dips, though there's a sizeable amount of visual sacrifice to be made at these settings. Still, it's playable and considering current PC prices I'll still take that as a win from a machine not typically designed for such outings.

Then I switched over to Cyberpunk, for science purposes.

To stay comfortably above at 30fps threshold for a lighter machine, the Geekom A5 2027 edition needs to be running on Low settings at 720p with frame generation on. Again, tests prove it runs - but it's going to be spicy.

CPU tests show what we expect from this older efficiency-focused chipset. The AMD Ryzen 7 7730U falls behind the faster, flashier AMD AI 9 HX 470 inside the Geekom A9 Max's 16,993 multi-core score and 2,740 single-core score. That's a machine that costs three times the A5's price, though.

The story's much the same in 3D Mark. The Geekom A5 2027 didn't expect to be put through these benchmarks as a budget-minded productivity-focused device, but for the sake of comparison across the price range, here's how it fared.

It has been revealed that the Geekom A5 2027 is perfectly suited to those looking for a lightweight everyday computing brick that can keep the party going with lighter indie titles after work. The mini PC's focus on cooling and efficiency makes for a sustainable performance across less demanding tasks that makes it ideal for those smaller entries in your Steam library and emulation alike.

If you're just looking for an indie runner, and have no need for a full Windows PC attached to it, the price gets a little squeakier. While it's nice having that full Windows compatibility to back you up, especially if you're looking to build a retro library, those just looking to play the indies they like may fare better with a console.

Still, for day to day workflow with room for upgradeability and nicely quiet operation, this is an easy recommendation.

I used the Geekom A5 2027 Edition as my daily driver for work across two weeks, while using it for all my indie gaming during the same period. The A5 was put through its paces in Stardew Valley and Islanders, while also being specifically benchmarked across Shadow of the Tomb Raider, Cyberpunk 2077, 3D Mark's Time Spy, Fire Strike and Steel Nomad Lite, and Geekbench 7. For more information on how we make our recommendations, check out the full GamesRadar+ Hardware Policy.

In between, I've written for Tom’s Guide, Wireframe, The Indie Game Website and That Video Game Blog, covering everything from the PS5 launch to the Apple Pencil. Now, i'm focused on Nintendo Switch, gaming laptops (and the keyboards, headsets and mice that come with them), PS5, and trying to find the perfect projector.

Now that pre-loading is live for the Rockstar Games mammoth, players across the globe can finally download the game and drool over its icon for the next week or so. But pre-orderers in Japan have noticed that GTA 6's file size comes to about 208GB on the PlayStation and Microsoft Stores, versus up to 212GB in other regions.

As reported on by GameSpark and covered by Automaton, the game also received the strictest age rating from the Japanese certification board CERO - "Z" which is recommended for players aged 18 and over - but the listing notably doesn't contain one disclaimer seen in other international ratings.

PEGI and ESRB both warn of the game's "strong sexual content." Curiously, CERO's rating includes no such disclaimer. Together, some fans have taken the lack of "sexual content" disclaimer and smaller file size as signs that GTA 6 might not include some of the risque content we know it'll flaunt elsewhere in the world - based on NSFW leaks and a past rating that already clued us into the fact GTA 6 might be the first GTA to feature full-on sex scenes.

According to recent reports, the potential regional censorship isn't too surprising, though, considering how trimmed down GTA 5's Japanese release was at the time. Rockstar had to remove and alter a bunch of GTA 5 scenes to comply with the country's normally strict content guidelines, including Trevor's controversial torture segment and multiple scenes featuring nudity. Baldur's Gate 3, The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt and many more have been subject to similar restrictions in the past.

It has been revealed that earlier this week, GTA 6 became the most pre-ordered game in PlayStation and Xbox's history. That's also not a huge surprise, either. The juggernaut game's lavish marketing blitz took over London's Selfridges and Rockstar is even hosting an entire music festival starring a couple A-listers.

Microsoft 365 isn't quite living up to its name this week, as its services have suffered an extended outage that's knocked the likes of Outlook, Teams, and Copilot for six. As of writing, the manufacturer are finally reporting "encouraging recovery progress in Europe" and are busy "addressing the remaining areas of disruption", but that's only after chunks of November 12th and 13th have seen people, businesses, and institutions left unable to use stuff they rely on.

Industry observers note that that latest patch was given by Microsoft to the BBC, who've had a live report on the outage running, since it's affected the likes of schools, government services and medical services. IGN and Kotaku's reports differ on whether any Xbox services appear to be affected. The Xbox status support page currently indicates all is swell, but Downdetector does show a recent uptick in reports of concerns.

It has been revealed that "We regret that today’s outages caused disruptions for our customers, and we are working to address the concern," Microsoft exec Charles LaManna wrote in response to a support thread on the topic in the early hours of November 13th UK time. "We will continue to share more information as soon as we have it, and for now I can confirm that there is no indication this is the result of malicious or cyber activity.".

As much as it's slightly reassuring that there at the moment looks to have been no significant hack, the time it's taken to deploy proper fixes is concerning, with Microsoft noting some of their early attempts at rectifying things "not taking as expected".

According to recent reports, the debacle has rather emphasised how far from ideal it is that so much key infrastructure across the world runs on one clump of tech which all go down in a heartbeat, but to a certain degree that is the peril of relying on anything. One can only hope that Microsoft's ongoing efforts to fire vast numbers of staff into the sun and embrace AI haven't factored into lots of their services going tits up for an inconvenient amount of time.

Review: GTA 6 (PS5) - The Greatest Open World Game Ever Made

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1606 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Pushsquare

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • What does eight years and an estimated $1 billion get you?
  • In this long-anticipated crime sandbox, Rockstar has assembled the most technologically accomplished open world ever made, expanding on its groundbreaking work with Red Dead Redemption 2.
  • But crucially, with its dual protagonists Jason and Lucia, it’s grown up a bit.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

What does eight years and an estimated $1 billion get you? Well, GTA 6.

In this long-anticipated crime sandbox, Rockstar has assembled the most technologically accomplished open world ever made, expanding on its groundbreaking work with Red Dead Redemption 2.

But crucially, with its dual protagonists Jason and Lucia, it’s grown up a bit.

This is the franchise at its most mature, shedding the cartoonish cultural caricatures of GTA 5 without losing the biting social commentary the series is known for.

The fictional state of Leonida is undoubtedly the star here; a dense and gigantic urban sandbox populated by an unfathomable array of art assets.

Whether it’s the easy-living coastal island of Key Lento or the mean streets of Crosstown, Rockstar’s artistry is utterly unprecedented.

Zoom in and you’ll see insects attracted to discarded food wrappers; a single convenience store has more unique art assets than entire districts in other open world games. This is remarkable stuff, delivered at such a scale it’s going to leave other publishers with their heads in their hands.

It feels alive, too; a casual visit to a gas station saw me berated by a cyclist for my wayward driving (I told him to chill out), while a brief pause on the side-walk ended up with my car getting hijacked by a masked criminal.

Recent findings suggest that in over 150 hours of play, I’m still discovering random events that add depth and character to the open world. And even when the scripting is pushed to the background, the way every NPC feels designed, with distinctive personality and unique body types, makes this package an unfathomable feat.

But while Leonida is the standout, Jason and Lucia are the vehicles that guide you through it.

Just like GTA 5, each character has their own individual life, but the game is at its best when it brings them together.

Industry observers note that I’ve never seen romance made into a mechanic quite like this, aside from perhaps the handholding in ICO, which is repurposed here. (Complete with DualSense haptic feedback when the characters touch.).

Jason is a bit of a beige blank slate, but Lucia brings genuine “girl power” to the story without pandering or feeling insincere.

In fact, in contrast to past GTAs, the many women in this instalment feel much more believable; the game frequently flips expectations on their head, without it ever coming across as forced.

A secret twist revealed in the opening moments adds gravity to the couple’s situation and becomes the driving force behind the story, which takes the pair from pillar to post, fulfilling the whims of a ragtag roster of ne’er-do-wells.

The campaign does fall into cliche territory at times, as the pair bounce from one bad idea to another in order to fulfil their ultimate ambition, and it’s something the characters seem to acknowledge. (“When are we going to get to call our own shots?” Jason wearily ponders at one point.).

But the mission design remains inventive throughout, regularly adding bespoke mechanics and interactions to keep things fresh.

According to recent reports, in one early mission, Jason indulges his inner-PowerWash Simulator, as he rinses down a boat while other characters commentate key plot points. I won’t spoil the best moments, but needless to say there are missions here that will be remembered for a long time.

There’s also a slate of optional pastimes running concurrently to the main campaign which add genuine variety to the sandbox.

Sources indicate that I was most enamoured by Jason’s home entertainment setup, which includes a distinctly PS4 coded console that can be powered up. I’ll leave you to discover his selection of fully playable games.

But beyond that, the ability to go hunting or even play a round of golf means you can lose yourself in this sandbox for hours at a time, and never really tire of the activities available to you.

Some of the action sequences remind me of all-time classics like Uncharted 3 – fist-pumping, set-piece heavy rollercoaster rides that push Rockstar’s engine to its limits, all within the confines of a meticulously designed open world.

Controller response is vastly superior to the studio’s previous games, with the cover shooting system feeling much more natural and the aiming mechanics buoyed by a pretty fun “bullet time” mechanic.

However, the game does fall into the trap of introducing heavily armoured bullet sponge enemies towards its conclusion, as it runs out of ways to make human-on-human encounters interesting.

That said, I really appreciated the agency GTA 6 gives you over how you approach each situation; non-vitals can be targeted to incapacitate enemies without murdering them, while it’s perfectly possible to sneak in and out of many areas without ever being detected.

According to recent reports, this all builds a criminal profile which changes how the police and wider world will interact with you. Meanwhile, you can influence Jason and Lucia’s relationship itself, opting to keep them close or distant depending on how you want things to play out.

Sources indicate that an early optional objective allows you to decorate Jason’s idyllic beach house in anticipation of Lucia’s arrival. Complete it in time and the couple will grow closer; ignore it and she’ll acknowledge you didn’t go the extra mile.

Other interactions are subtler: a kiss and cuddle on the balcony of the pair’s Vice City penthouse will strengthen their bond, but it’s up to you whether you want to invest in their relationship or not.

Multiple endings mean there are actual consequences to your actions, even if some decisions along the way feel more like an illusion than something truly meaningful.

The plot does begin to drag in its latter phases, and I do think Rockstar could have tightened up the roughly 60 hour storyline, which will likely take the average player around 80 hours to complete when accounting for the vast amount of side content as well.

(A 100% save could take anywhere up to 300 hours or more, depending on how much support you get from guides.).

As a crime sandbox, I also wanted to mention the ‘Wanted’ system, which has come on leaps and bounds.

A coordinated robbery can be accomplished without ever triggering a traditional car chase, as the game accounts for your outfit, vehicle, weapons, and much more.

Successfully scouting out your targets, and planning accordingly with a change of clothes and getaway car, can see you slip past the police undetected. Few moments in gaming are more satisfying than when you casually drive past a fleet of incoming cop cars, with a bag of successfully looted narcotics in your trunk.

Some players may respond negatively to the life sim elements here, which reward you for exercising and require you to occasionally put gas in your car or eat something.

But I think it adds to the immersive nature of the open world, and concessions have been made to the realism when it makes sense; a quick request to Scooter Bros, for example, will see your favourite car instantaneously delivered to your current location, so you don’t have to wait around.

The biggest downside to the outright awesome spectacle of the open world is that it runs at 30fps on the PS5 Pro, with no option to double the frame rate or tailor the presentation to taste, as has become standard in most other games.

Objectively this is disappointing, but given the sheer scale of Leonida I think it’s a necessary compromise.

It should be noted that despite all this, the frame pacing is solid and the game feels smooth and responsive as a result. I encountered very few (if any) instances of slowdown – even when flying over the map in a jet or speeding down highways being chased by rival gangs.

The audio presentation matches the high standards of the visuals, with different engine growls depending on how you’ve modified your vehicle. (Midnight Club fans may be excited to learn the racing missions here rival most dedicated franchises like Need for Speed alone.).

There are multiple fist-pumping audio cues, which leverage the title’s enormous licensed soundtrack to excellent effect. But credit must also go to composer duo Justice, who bring their distinct brand of disco-inspired electronica to the soundscape, elevating some of the best missions to impressive highs.

According to recent reports, and I was blown away by how much texture the DualSense adds, with one of my favourite features being the feedback you feel when you pass cars at speed on the highway. The only thing I didn’t like was the use of adaptive triggers, which feel far too stiff and lack the nuance of first-party games.

GTA 6 is the deepest, densest, most accomplished open world since Red Dead Redemption 2.

Rockstar has set a upcoming sandbox standard here, with a world that feels alive and populated with real people; Leonida is a place where it appears almost anything can happen at any time.

According to recent reports, crucially, despite the 30fps cap, the gameplay feels responsive and you have much more authorship over how you want to approach it. I enjoyed preparing for my robberies and feeling like I was rewarded for the legwork.

The audiovisual presentation is a upcoming high for the industry, with a frankly flabbergasting array of art assets bringing it all to life.

But I think Jason and Lucia’s ragtag romance, which is central to everything in the game, also demonstrates an unexpected maturity – without completely removing the silly sense of downright dumb humour the series is known for.

Despite unprecedented expectations, GTA 6 delivers – and then some.

In response to a Reddit post speculating about possible Sentinel news on Skyrim's birthday, the official Bethesda Game Studios account chimed in to temper everybody's expectations.

Industry observers note that "Hey everyone, wanted to pop in to say that we aren't going to have any big announcements tomorrow," the social media account wrote. "We're excited you're excited but we will not be sharing anything upcoming on Sentinel for some time.".

The Elder Scrolls fans have already been waiting for the series' next mainline follow-up for, erm, also quite some time. Specifically, Skyrim came out in 2011, The Elder Scrolls 6's first reveal trailer reared its head in 2018, and BGS' Starfield took to the stars in 2023 - a wait so long that it had even the most faithful among us questioning if a new Elder Scrolls could ever recapture the series' magic.

So, there you have it - don't expect to see or hear about Sentinel anytime soon. Better yet, lock it up in some corner of your brain and be pleasantly surprised when it does miraculously reappear in 20XX.

In the meantime, Bethesda isn't letting Skyrim's 15th anniversary go by without a few celebrations. For one, the seminal role-playing game is deeply discounted on all platforms, in the very unlikely scenario you haven't tried it out yet.

According to recent reports, the Elder Scrolls Online Season Two: Echoes of Skyrim is also joining the festivities by adding the Greymoor Chapter into the base game for free, giving everyone access to a few famous Skyrim locales and more. A brand-new, separate Golden Pursuit campaign will let you earn some Skyrim-centric goodies up until 2nd December, as well.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Where do you even start with a game like GTA 6?
  • Industry observers note that we've all spent the last 13 years trying to figure out what GTA 6 might look like by the time it arrives, and the answer is perhaps more simplistic than some had theorised - it's basically GTA 5 mixed with Red Dead Redemption 2, but with a ton of added detail and ambition on top.
  • Before we get to the open world, which is surely the most incredible aspect of the entire game, we should first touch on the story of Lucia and Jason.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Where do you even start with a game like GTA 6? Not only is it the most highly-anticipated video game we've ever seen, but it's also attempting to live up to ridiculous expectations set by its predecessors over the years. GTA 3 revolutionised how we thought about 3D open-world epics, Vice City and San Andreas pushed things to the next level, GTA 4 took yet another massive step into the HD era, and GTA 5 propelled the series into another stratosphere.

Industry observers note that we've all spent the last 13 years trying to figure out what GTA 6 might look like by the time it arrives, and the answer is perhaps more simplistic than some had theorised - it's basically GTA 5 mixed with Red Dead Redemption 2, but with a ton of added detail and ambition on top. That's all it needed to be, and I reckon people are going to absolutely love it.

Before we get to the open world, which is surely the most incredible aspect of the entire game, we should first touch on the story of Lucia and Jason. These two amateur criminals accidentally run into each other and establish a relationship (which can alter between platonic and romantic depending on how you interact throughout the campaign), and after a simple score goes wrong, they find themselves being dragged into more and more dangerous scenarios. That's the basic premise, and the rest is up for you to discover yourself.

According to recent reports, the GTA 6 Extended Preview from a few months ago left me very concerned about whether there was enough intrigue to the two main characters (along with the NPCs for that matter), but I needn't have worried. Lucia is a fiesty, hot-headed personality - the type of person who thinks less about the consequences and more about the high life she's determined to acquire - while Jason is extremely laid back to a hilarious extent at times, although also highly capable in pretty much any situation he finds himself in. The two bounce off each other really nicely, and their dynamic definitely remains engaging throughout the campaign's duration.

While I really don't want to spoil anything story-related, the mission structure is very much what you'd expect from GTA 5 and RDR2. In other words, there's a well-balanced mix of laid-back and humorous missions along with more intense shootouts and getaways that significantly ramp up in intensity. They've managed to get really inventive and ambitious with some of the later missions in particular, and I think there's no doubt they're the best of any GTA game.

According to recent reports, I also want to point out the use of music in GTA 6's missions, which caught me off-guard and became one of my low-key favourite features. In a nutshell, if you find yourself in the likes of a shootout or a getaway, you'll often notice that curated tunes play in the background to amplify the situation. The developers sometimes even go a step further by making the lighting around you pulsate to the beat, or by introducing lyricists to create a menacing vibe, and it can turn an otherwise generic mission into an amazing one. Seriously, I can't overstate how much I love this feature.

The story itself takes 40ish hours if you completely rush it (which admittedly I've been doing for the most part to hit this embargo), but if you take your time and do at least a decent amount of the optional stuff, it's likely more around 60-100+ hours. As I say, I've enjoyed all of those hours, and I think the campaign seriously hits its stride in the final third - the vast majority of memorable moments are saved for the latter stages.

I don't want you to fixate on the 40-100+ hour figure though, and that's because GTA 6's open world is so incredible and so vast that you could be playing it for months, and likely years, and not see everything it has to offer. We've never seen a GTA world like this - traffic levels are extremely high, the number of NPCs on the streets is ridiculous, it always feels like something's happening around every corner (there are so many random encounters!), you'll find loads of buildings you can go into, there's so much detail on everything... it's just an absolute dream for anyone who loves the idea of immersing themselves in this game.

In a recent development, GTA 5 had an amazing open world too, but after going back and playing it for the purpose of this review, there are two major differences that stand out - there's far less actually happening in the world at any one time (and therefore much less to interact with), and the map just feels tiny in comparison. GTA 6's state of Leonida incorporates so much more than just Vice City itself, including many other highly-populated areas such as Key Lento and Ambrosia. The first time you actually see Vice City in a mission (assuming you haven't gone and explored it previously) is a highlight of the entire game - it immediately appears so vast and so incredibly detailed that it feels like a next-gen experience.

Recent findings suggest that the way in which you interact with that world as a player has evolved as well. Cops are smarter than ever, and not only prove a tough challenge when attempting a getaway at three stars or more, but they also remember what you look like - and therefore you sometimes have to disguise yourself by changing into different outfits. Stealing a car now requires you to think about what kind of lock system it has on it, and whether there's a tracker fitted that will alert the police to your location. Cars can even run out of fuel now! Every element feels more in-depth than we've seen in GTA in the past, but Rockstar has crucially balanced the impact just right, so it's never to the detriment of your ability to just have fun.

I do think you'll get the most out of the game if you pace yourself though. It feels intentionally designed to encourage a slow playstyle where you explore, hang out, browse the fully-featured social media and news feeds on your phone (complete with video clips and comment sections), take part in games like pool and minigolf, engage in countless side-missions and random encounters, watch and play a ridiculous amount of purpose-built content on your in-game TV, and ultimately just see what you can discover without rapidly jumping from mission-to-mission. The amount of content here is overwhelming, but in a really satisfying way.

Of course, it's almost a given at this point that GTA 6 looks visually incredible, and I can confirm that it's definitely a stunner on Xbox Series X. There's some occasional pop-in, but it's minimal, and I only ran into a few tiny bugs during the review period (which may have been ironed out for release anyway). The performance is mostly very smooth considering the circumstances as well - yes, it's a bit jarring at first to go back to 30FPS if you've been playing 60FPS games for the most part in recent years, but give it an hour-or-two, and you probably won't care anymore. Seriously, it's a total non-issue for me at this point, and I'm more than happy playing at 30FPS.

It should be noted that I played around 30 hours on a VRR-enabled display during the review period, and around 10 hours without one. I was perfectly happy with the performance in both cases, with the only noticeably substantial frame rate drops occurring during very rare and visually intensive gameplay sequences.

Industry observers note that so, is there anything I don't like about GTA 6? The only thing I'd say is that it doesn't top my tier list in terms of greatest GTA stories ever, although it's probably still in the top three. It's a narrative that'll fully invest most players from start to finish, and there are shocking moments and twists that are bound to last long in the memory, but I also reckon it gets a bit too convoluted and farcical at times. That remarked, the final third of the campaign is jam-packed with intense story elements and incredibly action-packed missions, guaranteeing some truly jaw-dropping moments.

In a recent development, its tone can also feel overly harsh and uncomfortably serious in specific circumstances, but hey... this is Grand Theft Auto after all. Every GTA has its moments like that, but the impact feels more striking this time due to the enhanced sense of realism. Fortunately, there's plenty of lighthearted humour to be found along the way as well.

Somehow, GTA 6 lives up to the hype. Rockstar Games has crafted the most incredible open world I've ever experienced in a video game, packed with so much detail that I'll want to continue exploring it for months and likely years to come. It's coupled with a campaign that's full of extremely entertaining missions, led by two main characters who I've become much more invested in than I'd anticipated.

I'd have been fuming if you'd told me in 2013 that I'd have to wait 13 more years for the next GTA game, but now that it's finally here, I'm just relieved they've somehow managed to pull off another Game of the Decade contender once again.

Round Up: Spare A Thought For These Games Launching On 'GTA 6 Day'

💡 Key Takeaways
  • We interrupt your Grand Theft Auto 6 playtime to bring you the following announcement: there are more games launching today.
  • Yes, while 19th November 2026 will forever be known as 'GTA 6 Day ', a handful of other games are also braving the launch window and are releasing on Switch today.
  • We know that your adventures in Leonida will take priority, and that's okay, but we thought it was only right to highlight the other experiences that didn't back down from the massive boy's launch intends.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

We interrupt your Grand Theft Auto 6 playtime to bring you the following announcement: there are more games launching today.

Yes, while 19th November 2026 will forever be known as 'GTA 6 Day ', a handful of other games are also braving the launch window and are releasing on Switch today.

We know that your adventures in Leonida will take priority, and that's okay, but we thought it was only right to highlight the other experiences that didn't back down from the massive boy's launch intends. And no, we're not highlighting everything launching on Switch today, since, well, the eShop is always bombarded with questionable titles that probably aren't worth checking out.

If, however, you're on the hunt for something with fewer Vice City vibes, here are some other options launching today.

There's every chance that you have already played through Bedtime Digital's Figment and Figment 2: Creed Valley when they launched on Switch 1 a few years back, but the Switch 2 versions are also launching today with some neat performance bumps. We're talking 60fps at 1080p and "enhanced graphics". Sounds ripe for a replay, if you ask us.

Published and developed by room6, this is a roguelike all about gathering cute pixel art plushies to your aid and using their powers to survive a nighttime onslaught of monsters. Need we say more? It seems to strike that balance of cute/creepy pretty well, and we can see it being quite the time sink, with 40 recruitable plushies, 100 items and 20 costumes available to mix up every run.

In a recent development, those who frequent Japanese merch stalls will no doubt recognise the Sumikkogurashi gang. This one sees the team of adorable little blobs tasked with helping out at onsen inns to ensure their smooth running. There's plenty of minigames and scope to expand the inns further, but come on, the cuteness is the substantial draw here. Just look at those little guys!

It's The Binding of Isaac again (again). This re-release features all of the game's DLC content and the chance to play it with up to four players online.

Desperate for more throwback shooting after breezing through Boltgun? Auroch Digital has got you covered. After launching on other consoles last month, Warhammer 40,000 Boltgun 2 finally arrives on Switch 2 today with even more strafing, shooting and scary monstrosities. The score features a surprise cameo track from composer Mick Gordon (DOOM, DOOM Eternal, Wolfenstein: The Upcoming Order), which is an added bonus for music fans.

Industry observers note that naturally, the eShop will be home to many more debuts today, but the above selection gives a pretty good range of options (and a certain quality that a bunch of the other releases lack). Let us know in the comments if there's another newbie today that we've missed!

#51708. How Origame Digital are channelling and defacing Lovecraft over a trilogy of "inherently indigenous" anti-fascist games
