How Origame Digital are channelling and defacing Lovecraft over a trilogy of "inherently indigenous" anti-fascist games

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 17 min read (3382 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rockpapershotgun

⏱️ ~17 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, much like the H.P.
  • When I first set foot in Downtown, in the unassuming body of a Rockhopper penguin, I thought the broad idea was to satirically redefine modern settlements built by European colonisers as Lovecraftian relics, intrusions from the cosmic beyond.
  • I'm only somewhat correct about all this.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, much like the H.P. Lovecraft novella it alternately riffs on and skewers, Penguin Colony takes you to an ancient alien city of crabby cuboid geometry and helical designs – comparable at a glance to Lovecraft's "terraces of every sort of provocative disproportion", but here given strangely everyday, anachronistic-seeming labels, such as "Downtown". Later, you're shown flashes of footage of the streets of Melbourne in Australia - developer Origame Digital's base of operations, and a city built on stolen Wurundjeri Woi-wurrung and Bunurong Boon Wurrung land.

When I first set foot in Downtown, in the unassuming body of a Rockhopper penguin, I thought the broad idea was to satirically redefine modern settlements built by European colonisers as Lovecraftian relics, intrusions from the cosmic beyond. This irony seems most pointed in sections where you steer a group of Māori characters, journeying south to prevent an expedition of German and British Nazi occultists from resurrecting a surviving elder being they call the "one true Aryan king". Playing as one of the Māori voyagers, you witness the cyclopean city as a realm of spectral high rises and square windows, rearing out of a swamp of blood and bone.

I'm only somewhat correct about all this. Penguin Colony's reference points are wide-ranging and precise, with the persona of a disinterested penguin serving partly as a means of critical distance from Lovecraft, and partly, as a kind of camouflage for an extremely complex political artwork. It's easy to treat the game's critique as wholly retrospective - an alternately mocking and outraged investigation of a horror author whose bigotry is often reduced to an apologetic footnote or tinny performative disclaimer, drowned out by dread augurs of tentacles in the dark. It's a test of interpretative rigour, amongst other things, for hasty white European reviewers who might slip and slide past the more elaborate allusions into idle chat about Soulslikes.

Speaking to me over videocall, Origame Digital founder and director Naphtali Faulkner acknowledged the broad objective of reframing colonial cities as unearthly aberrations, cutting against cosier visions of colonised Australian land. "There's a bit of an matter with Australian games, where they tend to be tourism pieces, sometimes," he comments. "Not in a bad way, but they do not bring up the violence of this country, in anything. They will comfortably sidestep that for a lot of reasons – one is, a lot of the families that are affected by that are still around. Is it [a non-indigenous developer's] place to tell that story? No. But also, you have this sort of 'Australiana' stuff happen quite a lot, where it's tin roofs and red dirt, that kind of look you see on a postcard.".

Still, Penguin Colony's "first colonial city" isn't just a response to 'Australiana'. It's also a monument to 2b2t, the ancient Minecraft "anarchy" server that is infamous for its vicious player culture, and somewhat admired for the colossal strangeness of its desecrated geography. 2b2t is an incarnation of Mojang's sandbox building sim that is so 'pure' and unsparing in its priorities that license owners Microsoft can't entirely acknowledge it. The server's central spawn has been repeatedly built up, defaced and degraded over 16 years of constant operation, forming a nightmare landscape of lavafalls and Wither holes and floating seas and basalt barricades.

"We took data from that, and we modified it, and made it playable," Faulkner tells me. "We had to subdivide it, and it had more detail and stuff, and really transform it a lot, but the whole thing was: what is 2b2t? It's the most realistic depiction of colonisation in a videogame. When you do Minecraft, it's basically a colonisation simulator where you go extract the trees and stuff but it all magically regrows. 2b2t's only rules are there's no rules, and also nothing respawns. You have the Spawn - the Spawn is the most heart-wrenching thing to look at when you first see it, because you know what Minecraft is in your head, you've seen those rolling green hills, and then to see it basically be destroyed into oblivion, is a very strong emotion.".

As an inadvertent digital document of colonialism, 2b2t doesn't offer much hope of reparation and redress. "The only way to build back the Spawn is to go back and replant everything," Faulkner claims. "And you know, fix the damage that was done, but we all know what gamers did to it, right? They've done various incursions and things like covering it in lava or water, or making it so that you can't leave without cheats." Still, Faulkner considers it "a fascinating relic of gaming". In general, he is interested in how fiction makers might preserve virtual landscapes that reflect "player-run digital ecosystems of people basically going beyond what the designers thought.".

2b2t's presence within Penguin Colony is illustrative of how Origame Digital are using Lovecraft over the course of a planned trilogy of "inherently indigenous" Lovecraftian games – not just rebutting the author's anglophilia and white supremacism, not merely flipping the racial power dynamics so as to "make the indigenous people the skull-measuring scientists", but taking Lovecraft's mythos to unfamiliar places and forcing it to serve a politics that Lovecraft himself would despise.

Faulkner himself came across Lovecraft's work around 15 years ago, having been introduced to it by a university friend. He was unmoved, initially, by the author's descriptions of eldritch threats and incomprehensible dimensions. "You know how Lovecraft's described, with Cthulhu - 'unknowable horror', 'madness inducing'," he indicates. "And then you see it and it's kind of like an octopus. It's a bit underwhelming." Faulkner grew more intrigued by Lovecraft, however, after seeing other artists adapt his work. He points to the Shadows Over Innsmouth music video created by Carpenter Brut - a contributor to Hotline Miami 2: Wrong Number's OST - and also, to Victor LaValle's The Ballad of Black Tom, an adaptation of Lovecraft's The Horror at Red Hook written from the perspective of a Black man. "I started to understand that Lovecraft isn't just the author's works," he says. "It's this all-encompassing thing that has inspired so much stuff.".

According to recent reports, even as he pondered Lovecraft and the broader, somewhat dissociative genre of the Lovecraftian, Faulkner was also investigating his own heritage as a Ngāi Te Rangi person living in a former British colony, tracing patterns of invasion, conquest and assimilation that, he says, have repeated themselves since the days of the Romans and Vikings. "I think the reason that I decided to do this, was that when I started to get Lovecraft, it was when I was really starting to have the understanding that every indigenous person has at some point about what colonisation is," he says. "You know, where you have to learn your own family history, and you have to learn why things are the way they are at the moment. And so to me, it was like that thing of, when you start seeing Lovecraft as this thing about displacement, invasion, destruction, language - it reached me at the perfect time in my life when I was already looking at this stuff, and I thought that it was a really apt analogy.".

Faulkner also sensed that even Lovecraft enthusiasts who are less mindful of the author's politics were yearning for a fresher kind of Lovecraftian fable. "When it comes to indigenous stuff, the thing is that we're not really represented in anything, and our histories are rarely given a platform to say stuff, especially in games," he goes on. "But what I'd sort of looked at with Lovecraft, was that I think fans were ready for it, because people had gotten a little tired of these direct, 1-to-1 adaptations, that still exist in the space of the unknowable horror is unknowable, rather than trying to say, why is the unknowable horror scary?".

The idea of the "unknowable" pervades Lovecraftian fiction, as does the idea of "cosmic indifference", that terror of being engulfed in a vaster universe of forms and forces that barely register the existence of human beings. This "unknowability" is concentrated in the balefully blank gaze of Psurumin, the otherworldly entity at the far end of Penguin Colony - the last Earthly remnant of an empire spanning hundreds of planets. "I stare into its eyes," intones Howard Blakely, the game's English narrator, and an initially unconsenting member of the doomed Nazi expedition. "I stare deep within, and yet I see nothing. I am not even a speck of inane curiosity.".

Industry observers note that penguin Colony overlaps this Lovecraftian "cosmic indifference" with Faulkner's grief and bewilderment at how perpetrators of empire have insulated themselves from feelings of responsibility or shame. "For example in the southern hemisphere here, Australia and Upcoming Zealand, the idea was that the missionaries would say 'don't worry, we're saving them, we're turning them into Christians, we had to kill the ones who resist'," he states. "And the soldiers that had immense trauma and guilt from doing that would be consulted by a priest and told, 'you were doing it for the greater good'.".

"To me it's saying: how could they do that to us?" Faulkner goes on. "What made them do that? To me as a younger person, it was very 'unknowable'. You've probably talked to other indigenous people, I hope, before in your life, and it's this kind of thing especially where there's a lot of pain there, because... how could someone choose to do that? And even to this day, there's a question around even saying sorry about it. Or there's questions around people, they want to sort of move on from history, and never bring it up, never acknowledge it again, whilst the injustice of colonisation is still present.".

Industry observers note that howard Blakely is a mirror of sorts for this culture of denial and obfuscation. For all his apparent awareness that Psurumin does not regard him as a fellow being, and that to release the creature would be calamitous, he succumbs to the idea that he can ship the starspawn home as yet another trophy for the British Empire. He dreams of being honoured as a great pioneer by "the London School of Eugenics", and retiring to a cottage in Western Victoria. These reflections are accompanied by archive illustrations of colonial officers storming the frontier, and video snapshots of Psurumin statues in Melbourne's civic centres.

It has been revealed that blakely is similarly befuddled about his German Nazi hosts, who are initially his captors. While cautious of them, he also doesn't see the Nazis as altogether bad. After all, some of them are fellow scholars – surely, they are too refined, too cultured, to be altogether irredeemable. "He doesn't see himself in history, as he walks through this place," Faulkner comments. "He doesn't see the Nazis as the people that we see them as." In this, Blakely echoes Dyer, narrator of Lovecraft's At The Mountain Of Madness, who comes to admire the star-faring colonisers his team unearth in the far south, calling them "men of another age and another order of being". But he is also an expression of political myopia and creeping fascism in the present.

The inspiration for Blakely came partly from Faulkner's own time in the academic world. "There are tonnes of people who are scientists first, and political thinkers 17th in their thoughts," he comments, recalling his encounters with Trump supporters as a student. "People who don't consider themselves political and then end up taking incredible political stances on stuff, until it becomes clear that they do actually have a political ideology, that's sort of formed by being around the people they're around." Faulkner's other reference points for Blakely include Elon Musk, once "washed through the media as a green, eco-warrior guy", latterly an advocate for 'great replacement' theories and far-right uprisings.

Recent findings suggest that faulkner indicates that Penguin Colony's anti-fascist sentiments are especially aimed at "the rise of gen-Z fascism", expressed in online transphobia and anti-Semitic memes. "There's been a huge uptick in people trying to vindicate Hitler, and trying to rehabilitate him in the eyes of this young generation," he says. "What they say is things like 'the painter was right'." Faulkner thinks that this neofascism has "petered out a little bit" over the past ten years, but is still on the march. Above all, he sees its resurgence in the genocide of Palestinians in Gaza, and in the qualms many self-described anti-fascists have about condemning it.

Industry observers note that "I and every indigenous person I know, in and out of the games industry, have no nuanced emotions about what is happening there," Faulkner continues. "We know what this is. Like, it's our family stories come to life. We can see what this was. We're not just hearing stories anymore. And we're not just noticing the violence happening to the indigenous people right now. We're noticing how the mostly white, non-indigenous people are still conflicted on it and confused on it, and they don't have clarity on this. The idea with this game was to really bring this into focus, because the games industry likes to say that indigenous people are welcome. And they want to welcome us at our events. What does that mean? You guys want us here to talk, but you're not going to acknowledge the genocide of indigenous people that's happening in front of you, that every single human being at this point knows about.".

Penguin Colony ends with a statement calling out the games industry at large for holding its collective tongue about the Israeli military's brutal campaign, noting that such "cowardice" will be "recorded by the art that it makes". The flipside of that sentiment is that art can be a record of courage and principle, advancing and nourishing a culture in which xenophobia and colonial ideology are unable to thrive. I see this idea expressed, again, in the journey of the Māori group, who are equipped to prevent Psurumin's return because they have made doing so a tradition and a practice.

Recent findings suggest that "They know from generations of story, that you have to do it," states Faulkner. "That it's a responsibility to do it, when it happens." Thwarting Psurumin is part of the Māori's creative lifework, part of their journey together. "It is the job of our descendants to carry forward the story of our resistance," intones one of their group, the game's second narrator. "To create song, dance and story, so our people move toward the light and away from darkness... Every 100 years, to compose newly introduced haka and follow new paths unknown to our enemy.".

According to recent reports, as a whole, Penguin Colony aims to be one such path away from darkness, its methods a mixture of bald and oblique, overt and covert. I have barely broken the surface in this piece. There's an angry hopefulness to the game that coexists with the spectacle of a distinctly 'double-A' penguin bumping and slithering along boulevards of blue-toned, recessed stone. The player is invited to participate in that hope by the game's closing "expedition" screens, which present all the lore you've gathered – including photographs taken by the Nazis, and textual fragments of devious origin – as a web of stars, floating over an illustration of the Zodiac.

The invocation of constellations is gently subversive because a constellation is an act of selective reading, stringing together sparks in a void. Treat the lore as something you can individually exhaust or "100%", as in many RPGs, and your selective reading will vanish into the mass of motes. Rather than 'completing' the star map in solitude, the game invites players to reach out to each other and compare their constellations – a homage to a "pre-social media" era when the distribution of information was less the province of monolithic digital platforms, and also, a framework for political solidarity. "As we live in a world which continues to push us further apart, we invite you to come together, talk, share, and interpret what you saw," the game suggests.

Industry observers note that the call isn't open to all, however. Penguin Colony is consciously designed to repel those who might identify with its Nazis, appropriating the portrayal much as alt-right memesters sought to deify Anakin Skywalker, in the run-up to this year's US midterms. As a rhetorical apparatus, Penguin Colony is full of traps, easily overlooked if you focus on its headline politics. "We have a character voiced by a German trans woman – they can't enjoy it," notes Faulkner. "It just makes their skin crawl." There are many more such snares in the game. The commentary on Israel and Palestine, especially, pervades Penguin Colony in ways I don't think any player has yet discovered.

The lore of Penguin Colony also harbours clues about Origame's future "inherently indigenous" Lovecraftian games. The next game in that trilogy was actually conceived before Penguin Colony, and will be set decades from now. Faulkner envisages it as a loose retelling of Shadows Over Innsmouth, Lovecraft's story about fishpeople cults and miscegenation in a remote coastal town. "It's this idea of, what does Lovecraft look like in a future that we're heading towards, in the sense of social isolation and landscapes of small town decay.".

In place of a Dagon cult, Origame Digital's next game will focus on groups of secretive violent bigots, with the player playing the part of a detective - a premise that, more superficially, makes me eager for a resurrection of the photography mechanics in Origame's reputation-making Umurangi Generation. As with Penguin Colony, the concept draws heavily on Faulkner's own life experiences.

"I grew up in a cattle town, and cattle towns are notoriously pretty racist places," he claims. "The whole thing is when I left the town, when I was 18, just because I was going to university, I learned that the town had an active KKK [branch] that was being run out of the Anglican church. And this town is one town away from Grafton, which is where the white supremacist terrorist Brenton Tarrant is from – the guy who went and shot up the mosque in Christchurch. How does that happen? Where everyone knows about it, but they hush up?" The forthcoming game will look at how bitterness and neglect may give rise to such hatred, as local economies dry up and support structures are stripped away.

The second game will also take inspiration from the North American concept of a "sundown town", in which non-white people face violence if they linger outdoors after sunset - a vicious history also explored in Matt Ruff's HBO-adapted novel Lovecraft Country. "I went through a massive rabbit hole on Youtube of hearing stories of people talking about, like, getting lost on the highway, needing to stop for gas, and then realising they had to stop it for gas at a sundown town," Faulkner explains. "They stopped there. They go to pay. And the clerk just sort of gives them a look, and then nudges over to them that there's a guy in the back of the shop just looking at them. And then suddenly they're followed on the highway for an hour.".

The final game in Origame Digital's planned trilogy is far more formless, right now, but Faulkner has dreams of venturing into the realm of cooperative multiplayer. "It's not even written down on paper yet," he indicates. "We've just talked about it. For one thing, I don't know if I've got the skills to do it, because Penguin Colony had some jank, and had some technical challenges at launch, but I'm getting better at making games.".

Recent findings suggest that this multiplayer project would build on Penguin Colony's premise of playing a colony, hopping between penguin bodies while shadowing Blakely's expedition. It would also follow through on the former game's closing encouragement to make allies against inhumanity via the collective interpretation of a celestial expanse of lore. "It's about the whole group, and I think if the third one was going to make a point about coming together to solve the problem… you probably want to make that a mechanical issue," Faulkner speculates, "where we have to actually make players do these sorts of actions together.".

#51707. Destroy All Humans remake developer goes independent, splits from THQ Nordic and parent company Embracer Group

📅 11 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 1m • 📖 Standard (294 w)

💡 Key Takeaways

  • The Destroy All Humans remaker won its newfound independence through a management buyout, and wasted no time at all in co-founding Third Signal, which is described as a new group of independent studios that'll eventually provide help and resources to other indie teams.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Black Forest Games - the studio that remade the first two cult-classic Destroy All Humans games - has spun out from under former owners THQ Nordic and Embracer Group.

The Destroy All Humans remaker won its newfound independence through a management buyout, and wasted no time at all in co-founding Third Signal, which is described as a new group of independent studios that'll eventually provide help and resources to other indie teams.

"Some of the best games of the last decade came from teams of 50, not 500. Black Forest Games is one of them, and the right studio to launch Third Signal. Our vision is to build a developer driven group and give teams the independence, resources and creative freedom to continue their creative legacy and bring their own ideas to life," Third Signal CEO Andreas Tobler said in a press release.

Black Forest Games was one of Embracer Group's earliest high-profile acquisitions almost a decade ago, before the organization swallowed up countless major names (Lord of the Rings, Tomb Raider, Kingdom Come: Deliverance, more) in the following years and spat back a bunch shortly after. Most infamously, Embracer sold Gearbox and Borderlands during its massive internal restructuring in 2024.

It doesn't sound like Black Forest split with the rights to the Destroy All Humans series or its permanently mean alien protag Crypto, but the studio has noted it's still working with THQ Nordic in some capacity. The original Destroy All Humans run nosedived wildly in quality after the second game, so I'm not sure how exciting a remake of, let's say, Destroy All Humans: Massive Willy Unleashed would be nowadays, though I'd definitely be interested in seeing Crypto again in another ridiculously silly, sometimes rude and anarchic adventure.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • The developer of cozy farming game Tiny Terraces notes their sales on Steam were roughly 148 times those on the Epic Games Store, clocking in at $136,195 on Steam and $916 on Epic for a year (pre-tax).
  • Solo game dev VuVuu waded into discussion of the PC gaming store wars on Twitter.
  • This chatter began with a post from indie dev Evgeny Grishakov dissecting the revenue splits offered by Valve and Epic.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The developer of cozy farming game Tiny Terraces notes their sales on Steam were roughly 148 times those on the Epic Games Store, clocking in at $136,195 on Steam and $916 on Epic for a year (pre-tax).

Solo game dev VuVuu waded into discussion of the PC gaming store wars on Twitter. "Make sure to get Gaben seven more yachts," they added, plugging the game's Steam store page. Valve co-founder Gabe Newell does love his yachts.

This chatter began with a post from indie dev Evgeny Grishakov dissecting the revenue splits offered by Valve and Epic. Valve famously takes a base 30% from all Steam sales, while Epic only takes 12% but takes exactly 0% of your first $1 million gross every year. And yet, Grishakov says, "Steam is still the better deal for most indie games, because that’s where the players are." Many, many indie developers have told me the same thing over the years.

In the replies to Grishakov's post, multiple developers claim to see 0-3% of sales from Epic's store. The Hive developer Skydome agrees, "I will gladly pay Steam 30% for the visibility and revenue they bring." They note that, "For comparison, Epic made only 1.4% of our revenue compared to Steam last year.".

There's no questioning Steam's dominance. But an interesting exception to this rule has also resurfaced, and it's for a game I actually played pre-release at GDC earlier this year.

Recent findings suggest that kernel Hearts is a multiplayer 3D action roguelike about magical girls. One of those girls, the pink-haired Fernet, became a Fortnite skin, and a very popular one at that. Fernet was so popular that many people would buy Kernel Hearts through the Epic Games Store just to get the skin for Fortnite. This is where Epic's Fortnite-connected marketplace and more generous rev share can actually make an impact.

"That outfit alone is worth roughly $17USD, so anyone familiar with the Kernel Hearts brand will almost certainly find the EGS offer more appealing since a significant part of our game are the character's designs," Kernel Hearts dev Ephemera Games wrote in October.

Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more.

"Roughly 6 out of every 10 copies sold across PC were on the Epic Games Store, 3 on Steam and 1 on Xbox," the studio explains. "This is a pretty unusual split, especially considering that the game is available on all storefronts at pretty much the same price.".

Sources indicate that now factor in the rev share and $1 million grace period. "At 100k units sold for $20, that's $2M in revenue," Ephemera begins. "On Steam, you'd pay roughly $600k in platform fees. On Epic, your first million has 0% fees, and the remaining million has a 12% cut. That's just $120k in fees, a difference of $480,000! THATS A WHOLE OTHER GAME FUNDED!!!

"Of course, this is a simplified example that doesn't account for regional pricing, refunds, taxes, or other deductions," the studio admits, but neither Steam nor Epic offer a magical solution to the tax fairy. "But for a small studio like ours, that's a life-changing amount of money that can go directly into funding our future projects! So yeah! Put your game on EGS.".

Sources indicate that kernel Hearts is an outlier. Not every game has a highly marketable and fashionable magical girl to act as a Fortnite magnet. But even as a corner case, it's a perfectly valid data point that demonstrates how developers can make out better if they can somehow generate relevant sales on the Epic Games Store. Therein lies the problem. Situations like Tiny Terraces are infinitely more common due to Steam's dominance (attributable largely to Steam's user experience), and Epic does not seem to be making convincing moves to change that.

Tech Report: GTA 6: Where to find your first plane and helicopter right away

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that if you've just started GTA 6 you might be wondering where the nearest airplane and helicopter are located to your starting point.
  • Luckily, there's a reliable spot to snag your first few aircraft close to your starting safehouse, and you can probably steal them without raising a single alarm.
  • You'll drive about 2.5 miles southwest from Jason's house in Key Lento.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that if you've just started GTA 6 you might be wondering where the nearest airplane and helicopter are located to your starting point. There's a huge new world to explore, and the best way to do it is by air. But first, you've got to find a plane or chopper to steal.

Luckily, there's a reliable spot to snag your first few aircraft close to your starting safehouse, and you can probably steal them without raising a single alarm.

You'll drive about 2.5 miles southwest from Jason's house in Key Lento. Start the trip by driving southwest through Key Lento, then west through Abismo Key, and finally west and then north to Southwind.

Recent findings suggest that you'll be taking Sunbelt Highway (Route 1) the whole way and you'll know you're close after you cross two long bridges. Southwind is a small district located next to the Mile Zero Air Station: GTA 6's military base.

(Yes, the military base has planes and helicopters too, but it's a little trickier getting your hands on them so check out our GTA 6 military base guide before you attempt it.).

Industry observers note that the highway will make a bend to the north as you enter Southwind. On your right you'll see a concrete barrier alongside the road, and where it ends is where you want to turn right into the parking lot, at the sign for SBW (Sherwin Boatworks) and Chicki's Tiki Bar.

According to recent reports, if you're facing the water (east), on your right (to the south) is a small hangar with (typically) a few Mammoth Dodo seaplanes parked inside and around it, and often a couple more moored off the dock. Seaplanes aren't the fastest planes in the game, but they're perfect for early exploration because they can land on both water and land, and they require almost no room to get airborne.

Keep up to date with the most notable stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

There's never anyone hanging around here, either, so you won't draw any attention if you help yourself to one of these planes. Just drive one into the water and take off, or steal one from the dock.

Follow the same instructions to Southwind as above, but instead of looking to the south, look straight east from the entrance to the parking lot. There's an open gate leading out to a dock where a Buckingham Maverick helicopter is sitting.

According to recent reports, just ignore the no trespassing sign, run over to the dock, and hop into it. Now the skies are yours.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

You'd be forgiven for forgetting that Amy Hennig's superhero game Marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra exists, but apparently it's still in development despite its many troubles and rumours to the contrary.

Reassurance comes from Skydance's Slack work chat where, Kotaku says, executive producer Lu Gigliotti told the team they'd spoken "directly" with Skydance leadership and could reassure staff the game wasn't going to be cancelled. "They asked me to make sure you all hear that directly," Gigliotti reportedly told staff. "There is no truth to these claims.".

This follows a recent rumour that the action adventure title was potentially going to get the axe in the near future. The rumour originated from a Marvel 1943 fan account, and while the original X post has since been deleted, it didn't stop it from spreading online, including amongst the game's own development staff.

Sources indicate that according to Kotaku's report, Rise of Hydra is close to its alpha state, despite seemingly five years of development. The game is noted to have had multiple issues through its long development.

The current build is reportedly "light on gameplay", featuring only one interaction button. This is understood to be the result of Rise of Hydra having reportedly been originally envisioned as a Netflix game. According to the same report, the game is late and over budget, which resulted in cuts to its scope and scale throughout development.

Marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra was fully revealed in 2024, and is the debut title of Skydance Newly introduced Media, the studio headed by veteran designer and writer Amy Hennig, who's famed for her work on the Uncharted series of games.

Recent findings suggest that though the game was originally planned for release in late 2025, it was later delayed to early 2026 and then again to "beyond early 2026". Earlier this summer, Paramount Games Studio boss Shawn Kittelsen noted Rise of Hydra won't be out in 2026, but assured fans it remains in development. According to the report, Rise of Hydra was later delayed to 2027 and beyond.

Tensions are particularly high at the moment following the colossal recent Paramount and Warner Bros. merger, which has already resulted in some job losses at Paramount Games, a group that oversees the game's development, among other projects.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • So, here's what the critics are saying about GTA 6 so far:.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The first reviews for GTA 6 are officially out now, and as you've probably already seen, we've got one here at Pure Xbox! We gave the game an "Outstanding" 10/10, which isn't entirely surprising considering the history of this series.

But what about everyone else? GTA 6 is nominated for Game of the Year at The Game Awards, so does it live up to that recommendation? Are the critics overwhelmingly enamoured with it? That's what we've been intrigued to find out.

So, here's what the critics are saying about GTA 6 so far:.

"Somehow, GTA 6 lives up to the hype. Rockstar Games has crafted the most incredible open world I've ever experienced in a video game, packed with so much detail that I'll want to continue exploring it for months and likely years to come.".

"GTA 6 is the deepest, densest, most accomplished open world since Red Dead Redemption 2. Rockstar has set a new sandbox standard here, with a world that feels alive and populated with real people; Leonida is a place where it appears almost anything can happen at any time.".

"A game so good I asked our tech team if I could somehow give it 11/10. GTA 6 is an absolute masterclass in genre-mashing. With meticulous detailing and levels of immersion that almost feel dangerous, it's steeped in steamy satire — with story beats that often cut close to home as they relish in laugh-out-loud absurdity. Given the state of the industry, it's sobering that we might never see another game like this again. Grand Theft Auto 6 is a cover-to-cover masterpiece without equal.".

Recent findings suggest that "Grand Theft Auto VI is a generational game that stands toe-to-toe with many of the great crime stories and satires across other media. It showcases both the entertainment value of interactive play and the current high-water mark for technical and artistic detail in games. Hunt for and count up all the minor faults or foibles you like, but then note how you just spent another hour lost in this remarkable escape into criminality, wanton violence, egregious sex, and the elusive potential of true love.".

"This game is the culmination of everything the developer has previously achieved in the open-world space that pushes the genre to heights that, in all likelihood, no other developer will be able to reach. GTA 6 is an astonishing open-world action game that I’d wager won’t be outdone until Grand Theft Auto 7.".

It has been revealed that "GTA 6 is the highest-fidelity sandbox of its generation. Rockstar has built an open world of truly astonishing scale, scope, and quality. There's a degree of sophistication to everything GTA 6 does, and there's no aspect of the series' gameplay that hasn't been improved over past instalments.".

Industry observers note that "I regularly find myself in love with video games, but it’s extraordinarily rare that I find myself in complete awe of them. Put simply, Grand Theft Auto 6 is the single most impressive video game I have ever played.".

"A game of opposites and awe, minute detail and impossible scale, Rockstar pushes back the horizon of video games once again with GTA 6. An irreducible mix of silliness, intimacy, grand ideas and rock 'n' roll action - and a load more after that.".

"Grand Theft Auto VI delivers a remarkably immersive and ambitious open-world experience, blending thrilling gameplay, diverse activities, and a compelling relationship between Jason and Lucia. While uneven storytelling, pacing issues, and occasional performance drops prevent it from reaching perfection, the richly realized world of Leonida and its extraordinary attention to detail make this an unforgettable crime adventure that largely lives up to its monumental expectations.".

It has been revealed that "Grand Theft Auto VI is a great game that lives up to so much of the hype and expectations. Lucia and Jason are a well-written and compelling pair of protagonists, and the side characters you meet on their journey are great, even if the need to constantly raise the stakes across such a long story lessens its impact. You do have so much more freedom with how to tackle missions, though, and Leonida is a world filled with things to do and discover that will keep you coming back for a long time.".

As you can see, GTA 6 is a darling of the critics right now, and its initial rating on Metacritic sits at a whopping 99, which makes it the highest-rated game of 2026 (and literally the joint best game of all time if it keeps up this pace).

It should be noted that the vast majority of reviews are for the PS5 version, but both the PlayStation and Xbox versions are both sitting at 99 as things stand. That figure will probably change, but not to any significant degree.

According to recent reports, history tells us that we should have always expected a mainline Grand Theft Auto game to get incredible review scores, but it was really hard to see how they'd live up to expectations with this one. Nevertheless, they've somehow done it!

What are your thoughts on these initial reviews for Grand Theft Auto 6? Tell us in the comments below.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Paradox Interactive, publishers of umpteen strategy genre stalwarts including Crusader Kings, Europa Universalis, and Hearts of Iron, have announced prepares to switch overlords early next year. Fredrik Wester will make way for Mattias Lilja, as the deputy CEO takes the throne.

Recent findings suggest that while the move's been revealed this week, Lilja will properly become boss from January 4th, making this a case of getting a upcoming figurehead in place as the calendars swap. Departing CEO Fredrik Wester isn't going far, at least for now, as he'll "continue focusing on the tech giant's long-term development as a member of the board".

"My initiative was never to be CEO for life," Wester noted. "The goal was to build the foundation before passing the baton on for the next chapter in the firm’s journey. Since I returned as CEO, we’ve streamlined our strategy, rebuilt our pipeline and developed our commercial offering. Mattias has had a central role in laying this foundation, and now is the right time to hand over.".

It has been revealed that "The Board wants to thank Fredrik for his visionary leadership and outstanding contributions over these years," stated chairman Håkan Sjunnesson. "As a result, Paradox is in a strong position at a time when much of the industry is facing major challenges." He added that Lilja is "more than ready to assume the role and lead Paradox towards new gaming experiences that last for decades".

In a recent development, lilja himself declared that Paradox have "a unique DNA that has made us one of the greats in deep and engaging strategy and management games" and will be "stepping up the pace". "We will make further investments in our core business, push the boundaries of our game design, work even more closely with our loyal players, develop more and better tools and services that benefit both modders and players, and continue to sharpen our ways of working and our organisation, with player value in focus," he noted.

As Wester alluded to, he previously served as Paradox CEO from 2009 to 2018, with a brief stint as executive chairman of the board sandwiched between that and his latest stint as CEO since 2021. Lilja has been deputy CEO since 2024 and chief of staff since 2021, having originally joined Paradox as a producer in 2009.

According to recent reports, the past half decade has been a very mixed bag for Paradox. Their significant strategy flagships keep ticking along, albeit with the question of whether their next DLC will feel worth it hovering overhead near-permanently. Outside of that, however, the likes of Cities: Skylines 2, Vampire: The Masquerade Bloodlines 2, and cancelled Sims competitor Life By You have made for a track record heavy on questionable decisions and games which either flopped hard or failed to blow away expectations. Wester acknowledged back in 2024 that the manufacturer had "made the wrong calls in several projects, especially outside of our core".

With the likes of post-apocalyptic strategy game Afterworld right now in the works, it'll be interesting to see if Lilja's tenure can see Paradox finally start to nail not just their nerdy bread and butter, but also games that don't involve staring down at a major map.

'PS5 Pro Is Not Powerful Enough to Run GTA 6 at 60fps': Rockstar Explains Frame Rate Decision

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (562 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Pushsquare

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • I’ve played GTA 6 on PS5 Pro for over 150 hours and it’s a remarkable experience.
  • This is the densest open world ever designed.
  • Recent findings suggest that there is a downside to all the detail, though: the Rockstar release bucks contemporary console trends and runs at 30fps, without compromise.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

I’ve played GTA 6 on PS5 Pro for over 150 hours and it’s a remarkable experience. You can read my review through here.

This is the densest open world ever designed. The sheer amount of art assets on screen at any given time is simply unprecedented.

Recent findings suggest that there is a downside to all the detail, though: the Rockstar release bucks contemporary console trends and runs at 30fps, without compromise. There’s no Performance option, even on Sony’s most powerful platform, which will run you $900 these days.

I spoke to Rockstar’s Marc Chambers, the man in charge of Technology Production to try to understand why.

“The PS5 Pro features an upgraded graphics processor and upscaling technology that we leverage to increase the games visual fidelity,” he remarked.

“While the PS5 Pro’s central processor is slightly better than the PS5 base console, it’s not powerful enough to run the game’s complex simulation at higher frame rates.”.

In other words, it’s as many already predicted: GTA 6’s performance is limited by its robust CPU demands.

Chambers continued: “GTA 6 pushes the current-generation console hardware to its absolute limits. The complexity of simulating and rendering the environments and inhabitants in a world the scale of Leonida, while maintaining the density, visual fidelity, and player agency we envisaged, places extraordinary demands on the hardware. Bringing all of these systems together and completing the required work for every frame is only just possible within a ~33ms frame budget.”.

Sources indicate that the remarkable thing to me is, despite the drop to 30fps, I found the game to feel very responsive overall. Aiming is snappy and movement feels less cumbersome than in past Rockstar releases, like Red Dead Redemption 2.

Rockstar’s Vice President of Technology David Hynd told me that the team was able to remove one full frame of delay compared to past titles.

It has been revealed that “The input controller is sampled as late as possible during the game enhancement. As a consequence, the game is updated with the most recent input data and we minimise the time between pressing a button and seeing the results on screen,” he said.

You really do feel this: I was switching between GTA 6 and several other 60fps PS5 games during the review process, and while the frame rate difference was obvious to my eyes, it didn’t feel as dramatic as I’d expected.

“For our game mechanics, we ensured that we stripped as much ‘dead space’ out of the start of our animations as possible,” Hynd continued. “And ensured that we could seamlessly interrupt them as early as was practical.”.

There are still moments where GTA 6 feels clumsy, but it’s a marked improvement in playability compared to past games, despite the drop in frame rate.

Overall, I think Rockstar made the right decision.

The decision to lock gameplay at 30fps is objectively disappointing, but on a PS5 Pro the performance is smooth throughout, and the controller response is surprisingly good.

With the sheer amount of art assets on the screen at any given time, I think it would have been a shame to see Rockstar compromise its vision.

This is the most immersive open world ever made, and I think it’s clear the team has put as much thought as possible into making sure it feels smooth and responsive at 30fps.

Feature: 20 Wii Exclusives You Should Track Down While You Still Can

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1236 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nintendolife

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Somehow, someway, it's been two whole decades since the Revolution began and an elderly relative who had never played a video game in their life somehow, someway, thrashed you at Wii Sports bowling.
  • The little system that could went on to sell over 100 million units across its lifetime, which means that 20 years on it's still possible to pick up a good clean one for a reasonable price - something which can't be stated for a certain autostereoscopic handheld with a divergent family tree.
  • It also means that secondhand software is still plentiful for the most part, with much of the system's catalogue still available for not-silly money (plus some for silly money).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Somehow, someway, it's been two whole decades since the Revolution began and an elderly relative who had never played a video game in their life somehow, someway, thrashed you at Wii Sports bowling.

The little system that could went on to sell over 100 million units across its lifetime, which means that 20 years on it's still possible to pick up a good clean one for a reasonable price - something which can't be stated for a certain autostereoscopic handheld with a divergent family tree.

It also means that secondhand software is still plentiful for the most part, with much of the system's catalogue still available for not-silly money (plus some for silly money). So today we're rounding up 20 gems to consider picking up for your trusty Wii.

According to recent reports, if you're just looking for the Best Wii Games™, we've got you covered elsewhere. Here, we're specifically looking for games slightly off the beaten track, games that were either full-on exclusives or, in a couple of cases where I've stretched the definition, are difficult to find anywhere else.

Sources indicate that ready? Let's dive right into things...

Kicking things off with the Batman, Wayforward's take on the Cartoon Network series captured perfectly the audio-visual elements of the show with a ton of amusing dialogue and a fun, animated take on a character that — outside of his Lego iteration — had gotten pretty dark and self-serious in the movies and other games of the era.

Batman: The Brave and the Bold - The Videogame (or Das Videospiel as my German copy has it) offers simple side-scrolling brawling, but the BAM-BOOM-POW energy is infectious, and this is a great one to play with the kids. There was a DS version, although that's single-player only, so stick with Wii.

According to recent reports, steven Spielberg's making a game, everybody! Legendary Hollywood director Steven Spielberg! The moment we heard that, we imagined Indiana Jones-style derring-do, or something with aliens or dinosaurs. We didn't imagine that the title prominently flagged as "A Steven Spielberg / EA Game" would be a physics-based block puzzler/party game in the Jenga mould.

Industry observers note that however, 2008's Boom Blox turned out to be an absolute blast, especially with friends, and a game that made great use of the system's unique controller. it absolutely deserves to be revisited.

A sequel, Boom Blox Bash Party, followed in 2009, and that's a good time, too.

Dead Space: Extraction was a prequel to the 360-era sci-fi/survival horror game PS3/360 game, and perhaps benefited from low expectations, but it's a cracking, moody little rail shooter.

This one came to PS3 two years later with Move controller support, but this rail shooter was built for the Wii and made use of one of the system's best features: the IR camera-powered pointer in the Wiimotes. For accuracy and responsiveness, this fairly low-tech solution to pointer controls still trumps the gyro alternative (which constantly needs resetting/recentring) in our book, and this game is worth setting up the sensor bar.

One of the few games Europeans got which never saw the light of day in North America, Disaster: Day of Crisis is a Monolith Soft joint that showcases the Wiimote's versatility with different control schemes across its four main gameplay styles, which naturally includes those video game staples, shooting and driving.

The latter is handled with the Remote held horizontally, while outside the Nunchuk-controlled walking sections, the game becomes a pointer-based rail shooter.

Recent findings suggest that with a blockbusting story that crams in volcanoes alongside shady outfits and plenty of (melo)drama, it doesn't quite cohere as it should, and there are certainly better-looking titles on the system. But as a curio from a studio with an enviable pedigree — and a game that apparently didn't pass Reggie Fils-Aimé's quality bar for release — it's a fascinating glimpse at Monolith's Wii-era thinking before Xenoblade Chronicles dropped two years later.

Excite Truck was an underrated gem in the Wii's early life, with satisfying motion controls that paired beautifully with the wallow-y physics of the arcade monster trucks you raced.

In a recent development, it also let you load up MP3s on your SD card and make your own soundtrack, which felt like a bit of magic to some Wii gamers (read: this Wii gamer) back in 2006. Nothing like boosting over a canyon with Gwen Stefani booming through the speakers. Good times.

Having recently fired up Excite Truck, I can confirm that this holds up beautifully, with subtle controls and a suitable sense of heft and face-blasting speed. Helluva game.

Excitebots, Monster Games' 2009 follow-up, kept the arcade sensibilities and challenging terrain but switched out the trucks for on-wheel robots. It's a fantastic game that injects a little more personality into the basic structure of Excite Truck while keeping the speed and excitement.

Recent findings suggest that sadly, it's also a game which never rolled out in Europe, so we're currently tit-for-tat after Disaster: Day of Crisis. North America got the better deal, there.

Look, it's an inconsequential Zelda spin-off designed to showcase the Wii Zapper, but it is a system-exclusive inconsequential Zelda spin-off. Can you afford not to have it in your collection?

It has been revealed that hmm, probably. There's a reason this target-practice game is bottom of our Zelda list. Still, it's not unenjoyable, still dirt cheap, and it's got Twilight Princess-era Link on the box. I've somehow ended up with two copies. One of those 'oh, I don't have this' moments when you get home and realise 'yes, I already have this.'.

Another 'built for Wii' game that came to other platforms later (Vita in 2012, PC in 2016), Cing's Little King's Story added dashes of Doshin The Giant and Pikmin to a real-time strategy tale of the titular diminutive king working to expand the reach of his kingdom one citizen at a time and conquer neighbouring territories,.

Recent findings suggest that an engaging genre mash-up that holds its own alongside the previously mentioned Pikmin series while putting a fresh spin on things, this was one of the last games Cing (Hotel Dusk, Another Code) released. Two years later, the tech giant filed for bankruptcy.

When PlatinumGames' name is on the box, you expect style - and MadWorld certainly delivered that with its inky, Sin City-esque aesthetic that splattered blood red across a black-and-white canvas.

At a time when all the serious games elsewhere were shiny and brown and grey, this Sega-published chainsaw-'em-up also helped demonstrate that Wii wasn't only a console for fluffy technicolour worlds and cuddly mascots.

Sources indicate that as a hack-and-slash brawler, it's not up there with the developer's finest work - there's definitely an element of style over substance here. But when the style is this good, it's still worth the space on the shelf.

Honestly, at this point we all thought we'd have access to this on Switch one way or another — via NSO if not a proper remaster. However, at the time of writing (and discounting the now-unavailable Wii U eShop release of the Trilogy), this Metroid is still a Wii exclusive.

We can only assume it will arrive at some point — Nintendo now has the four Pikmin games on Switch, so it's about time to plug the Prime gap, too.

And staying on that theme, let's stick with Samus over the page...

Nvidia's board of directors has reportedly met to decide whether to remove the tech giant's embattled CEO Jensen Huang, as news of a second extramarital affair has come to light.

Per the Wall Street Journal, the board met on Wednesday to decide whether to remove Huang following reports he allegedly participated in another affair with an executive who worked for him.This followed the revelation of his affair with an alleged Chinese spy, which prompted a firm-wide apology from Huang and an independent investigation into whether he'd been the target of a "foreign intelligence effort".

Recent findings suggest that the board's decision has yet to be made, but there are three expected outcomes. Either Huang stays with the company and continues as Nvidia leader, despite the controversy or he is replaced as CEO, or he quits. Nvidia's share price dropped following reports of this meeting taking place.

Recent findings suggest that if Huang is fired - and perhaps even if he isn't - it's likely to severely disrupt Nvidia's operations. Huang co-founded Nvidia and led it to become one of the world's most valuable companies - it interchangeably wears that crown, alternating with Apple. Replacing Huang might change the company's focus.

Regardless, Nvidia is under major scrutiny right now because of Huang's actions. There are particular concerns around the company's chips being imported to China despite trade bans. Gamers Nexus produced a documentary on the Nvidia AI GPU Black Market, detailing much of this.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, what's the best prank you ever pulled on a teacher in school, assuming you went to school? By which I mean, a genuinely funny prank that didn't cause any injuries, break any of the more important laws (legal or ethical), or leave anybody with years of mental distress.

I'll start: I once had to write a four-page punishment essay with the topic "silence is golden", after being caught talking in class. I took the essay very seriously for the first three pages, only to end it with the phrase "...but not as golden as my arse." The teacher who set me the essay smugly tore it up without reading it - as I knew he would. Checkmate, Mr Thompson. Decades later, the last laugh remains mine.

Recent findings suggest that worst Class Ever is a new don't-call-it-friendslop asymmetrical multiplayer game dedicated to such larks. One player is a teacher, and seven others are naughty delinquent children, hiding in amongst some well-brought-up and obedient NPCs. As the wayward tykes, your goal is to do mischievous things like eating at your desk, passing notes, dropping banana skins, and playing on your phone, without being spotted by Teach.

According to recent reports, all of this takes place in a breezy modern Japanese high school, the kind familiar from a million animes. Bagsy the Protagonist Desk by the window at the back of the class! The maplist spans the curriculum, from computer labs to gym tracks to stepped lecture theatres. I don't think there are any covert edu-tainment mechanics, but if you're playing Teacher, I guess there's nothing to stop you actually explaining the periodic table while trying to work out who keeps throwing chalk at your head.

What a wholesome and whimsical place! Such happy memories! Oh crikey, the male teacher is terrifying – why can't he stop grinning? And why do I have a smoke grenade? Why is this lesson taking place in the dark? Why are the teachers permitted to punch the students and tie them to wooden posts? Worst Class Ever definitely isn't a horror game, but I'm not sure I'd send my kids to this particular institution. I feel like we're one texture pack away from playing a more sociable version of Little Nightmares. Read more on Steam.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • I was the lucky person to take on the review responsibility for the fresh Grand Theft Auto, and I've put basically all of my free time into it since late October.
  • Some of these were already known prior to today, whereas others might be brand-new information.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By now, you've hopefully had a chance to check out our review of GTA 6 for Xbox Series X elsewhere on Pure Xbox, and it exists because Rockstar gave us multiple weeks' worth of early access to the game ahead of release.

I was the lucky person to take on the review responsibility for the fresh Grand Theft Auto, and I've put basically all of my free time into it since late October. While completing the campaign, I inevitibly came across loads of features that surprised me along the way, so I thought I'd use this opportunity to just highlight a few of them.

Some of these were already known prior to today, whereas others might be brand-new information. In any case, here are the specific features (avoiding story spoilers) that surprised me as I was completing GTA 6 on Xbox Series X:.

Yeah, there's finally a fuel requirement in a GTA game! It's not too invasive, so don't worry, but if you happen to drive a car around the map for an extensive amount of time, you'll be forced to find a gas station and refuel it (a very short cutscene and a press of the RT button). You can also repair your car at gas stations as well, which certainly comes in handy if you've been smashing it around at high speeds!

You can still break into vehicles the old fashioned way - either stealing it mid-drive or smashing a window to gain access - but you can also use a slim-jim to break the lock, or eventually a key cloner to bypass the security entirely. Be aware of vehicles with trackers though, as if you end up going too slow, the tracker will alert the cops to your location.

Sources indicate that it's not always enough to escape the cops and stay hidden from them for an extended period of time. If you really want to ensure you'll lose their attention, you'll want to either ditch the car or take it to a "Pay 'n' Spray" outlet, as well as change your outfit. It's possible to partially do this by throwing on some sunglasses and a hat, but the clever move is to stash one or more outfits in your car's trunk that you can switch between at a moment's notice.

Industry observers note that while it's impossible to avoid situations in GTA 6 where you'll be engaging in all sorts of criminal activity, you can handle them in various ways. For example, a mission that requires you to take out a bunch of people can be completed by one-shotting them all, but this will raise your criminal profile. Alternatively, leaving your enemies injured but still alive will push you more towards a "Professional" profile. I haven't properly been able to compare how this affects the game yet (I really need to experiment with both sides of the extreme rather than hovering towards the middle), but Rockstar says it alters how the story, world and Jason / Lucia react to you.

Industry observers note that I always love when games get creative with music - South of Midnight was one that really impressed me - and GTA 6 is now one of the best examples I can think of. Basically, you get highly-curated pumping tunes playing in the background during things like shootouts and getaways, while more menacing situations can feature a different vibe of soundtrack, sometimes even with lyrics. You might not quite understand the appeal until you play it, but it's actually one of my favourite new features. The use of music in certain cutscenes is awesome as well.

It has been revealed that I don't know if I can verify this yet for sure, but the radio stations either appear to change their music selection based on where you are on the map, or based on how far you've progressed into the story. As I spent more time in Vice City, I started to notice a much bigger range of songs on the Flash FM channel (my favourite) including everyone from Coldplay to The Ting Tings, whereas those tunes never popped up at the start. Try it for yourself and let me know if I'm right about this!

It has been revealed that any GTA game worth its salt has to come with a whole bunch of minigames, and my favourite so far is the addition of minigolf. I believe there are three 18-hole courses dotted around the map in total, and they're beautifully detailed and themed, with genuinely enjoyable holes to play on. There's actual golf as well, but I have to admit I haven't had chance to check it out yet. Pool in the bars is great fun too!

If you really take your time to play through GTA 6, which I highly recommend you do, you'll truly be able to appreciate just how much effort has gone into some of the seemingly smallest aspects of it. Snapmatic, which is the social media platform on your in-game phone, is constantly being updated with new statuses, photos, videos, comments and more, and you could literally just sit just browsing it for ages and enjoying the interactions. There's also a "News" app that regularly gets updated with fresh articles about what's going on in Leonida.

When you get to a certain mission in GTA 6, you'll be introduced to your first video game inside the game itself, which seems to be a very high-brow parody of modern-day indie hits. There are actually multiple games you can play, including one that's very reminiscent of Xbox title Yet Another Zombie Survivors, and these can either be accessed by turning on your TV or going up to arcade cabinets located in various stores all over the map.

It has been revealed that when GTA 5 came out for Xbox 360 back in 2013, one of the big things I can recall is how slow the initial loading screens would be, especially once GTA Online got involved. We obviously haven't got an online component to GTA 6 just yet, but in terms of loading up the single-player game on Xbox Series X, it's actually a very quick process that isn't painful whatsoever. You barely even notice it!

Industry observers note that of course, these aren't the only surprising features you'll run into while playing GTA 6 - there are literally hundreds and hundreds that are waiting to be discovered. I don't want to spoil anything about the story or the details of the missions themselves though, and ultimately this is a game where surprises will continue being revealed long into the future.

For now, just go and enjoy it on your Xbox Series X or Xbox Series S (or PS5), and I urge you to take your time and really let it all soak in. One of the perils of reviewing games is that you have to grind to the finish line, and while that does still give you a great impression of the experience, I already can't wait to go back and spend 100+ hours with it this time.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

I recruited the biggest Star Trek fan I know to help me road test the new Magic: The Gathering set. Right away he was impressed by cards that referenced the Star Trek: Prodigy cartoon and Star Trek Beyond—a third movie in the J. J. Abrams-verse I completely forgot was even made—but if that kind of trainspotting was all it took to make a successful crossover then people would have liked the Spider-Man cards a lot more than they did.

Industry observers note that what makes the better Universes Beyond crossovers work is how they bring out the themes of their source material, turning motifs into mechanics that make a set feel like a genuine expression of the thing being adapted rather than just another property being fed into the content machine. Having played some games with the cards, yeah, I think Star Trek works.

Industry observers note that I built a blue-green deck around Strange Upcoming Worlds, a mechanic that rewards you for having different lands rather than just stacking Islands and Forests. When I played Deep Space Scan I drew a card for each differently named land I had, and those lands also lowered the cost of powering up my Astute Terraformer.

It has been revealed that meanwhile, the Federation mechanic gives bonuses for having different creature types on the table like Vulcan and Klingon and Romulan (though not Borg). With just those two mechanics, the set emphasizes exploration and diversity. You really do want to put together a crew representing multiple species and send them into the final frontier. (There is of course a card called Final Frontier.).

Sources indicate that star Trek also makes use of the spacecraft mechanics introduced in Edge of Eternities, where a ship starts with limited capabilities but has to be stationed by tapping creatures to add charge counters to access its full abilities—like flying and fighting. Lt. Cmdr. Geordi La Forge is a solid combo, doubling the amount of charge counters you add each time and letting you get the Enterprise into the air twice as fast.

It has been revealed that there are cards for various different iterations of the Enterprise, but I'm partial to U.S.S. Enterprise-A, Free Spirit, because when you play it you get three red 1/1 officer tokens for free. That makes it faster to station, and after that you've got three disposable officers to chump block with. Which is why they're red.

According to recent reports, there's also a Beam Me Up mechanic to bring a card back from the discard pile at the cost of returning a card from the table to your hand, and a cute assimilate mechanic that lets you wipe creatures' existing types then turn them into artifacts under your control for your Borg deck. But what makes the Star Trek cards feel like Star Trek is how much they emphasize teamwork.

Keep up to date with the most crucial stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

The Common Goal card lets two creatures deal damage together, and there's a whole suite of cards that get better when you've got creatures with a total power of 8 attacking as one. Worf, Honor-Bound Warrior, who doubles his own power when he's part of that attack, proved a gamewinner for my red/white deck more than once. The thing that really comes across is Star Trek's utopian ideal of everyone pulling together in a crisis and being better for our differences. It's optimistic, with stars in its eyes, and even a casual Star Trek watcher like me can appreciate that.

Magic: The Gathering's Star Trek set is available now, for both tabletop Magic and Arena.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, the Grand Theft Auto games have always been synonymous with America; Americana is baked into the crime series' very being. Across its history, there's only ever been one GTA game set outside America: the London-based expansion of the original game.

Industry observers note that GTA 6 follows this template, parodying the American state of Florida and the city of Miami. But what about the next game - will the series always be in America? Not necessarily.

In an interview with The Guardian, Rockstar North co-studio boss Rob Nelson propped the proverbial door open a sliver by saying: "Never say never." He then swiftly followed that comment with: "But there’s still so much to do in America".

It has been revealed that this is a topic Rockstar has responded to before, most notably when tech giant co-founder and long-time GTA writer Dan Houser - who's no longer at Rockstar - discussed why the series always seemed to return to America. He remarked it was because cities like Miami and New York and Los Angeles are places where extreme juxtapositions exist. They're places where extreme wealth rubs shoulders with extreme poverty, and where organised crime can be found.

There's also something America infamously has that few other countries do, and that's free availability of guns, which is such a core tenet of a GTA experience.

Nevertheless, Obbe Vermeij - a former technical director at Rockstar North - revealed last year that a GTA: Tokyo almost happened. However, it wasn't going to be made by Rockstar but rather an external team in Japan.

While discussing the subject, Vermeij referred to America as "basically the epicenter of Western culture". "Everybody knows the cities, even people who haven't been there," Vermeij said. "They have a mental image of the cities. I'm afraid we're stuck in this loop of about five American cities. Let's just get used to it.".

GTA 6 is just days away from its 19th November release on PS5 and Xbox Series X/S. Rockstar recently clarified the game runs at 30FPS across all platforms and confirmed that while it's available through Xbox Cloud Gaming, it cannot be streamed to PCs or non-Xbox devices.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, declaring a Best Way of Doing Things is a fool’s game, though in recent years my favourite entries in the Tricky Hitting genre – inclusive of soulslikes and their hybridised disciples – have been the major, bulging ones.
  • Even in the latter stages, with a full kit of precisely four ranged spells, Death’s Door is a simple proposition.
  • Still, it’s clever with its limitations.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, declaring a Best Way of Doing Things is a fool’s game, though in recent years my favourite entries in the Tricky Hitting genre – inclusive of soulslikes and their hybridised disciples – have been the major, bulging ones. Elden Rings and Silksongs, with vast kingdoms and deep, rattling toolkits for surviving them. The reason it’s a fool’s game is because you can also have something like Death’s Door, a taut, compact, lighthearted little actioner that fills eight hours instead of 80 and yet never feels underwhelming or compromised for it.

Even in the latter stages, with a full kit of precisely four ranged spells, Death’s Door is a simple proposition. You are a crow. You hit things. Occasionally you shoot things. You collect the souls of a frog, a yeti, and a grandmother. Everything in-between directly relates to finding the errant monster/pensioner, or at a stretch, upgrading one of those four abilities.

Still, it’s clever with its limitations. Environments are small in number but vary wildly in tone and texture, and they tightly weave their paths into criss-crossing bundles that maximise travel – evoking the sense of a great, ranging adventure within relatively tiny spaces. The lack of a wiki’s worth of combat options also never becomes a problem, partly because it spreads out its spell unlocks, and partly because the smooth, flowing back-and-forths of its central swordplay are pleasurable enough to carry it anyway. Good bosses, too! They’re all characterful, memorable weirdoes who fight unlike anyone in their minion armies, and usually come with a hidden weakness to deduce and exploit.

Which is welcome, as these significant lads and lasses do tend to launch difficulty spikes right up your feathered backside, and do so in a game that isn’t otherwise as fussed about trial-and-error pain endurance as some of its inspirations. They don’t, however, bring the mood down. At times, this tale of a pitch-black soul reaper working as an agent of Death (complete with an office of Death and embittered co-workers of Death) can get downright cosy, leading through you through warmly-lit jungles and breezy waterside ruins.

Sources indicate that recently replaying, I’d also forgotten how witty it can be. Little gaglets are sprinkled throughout, both visual and verbal, but the best jokes are saved for – funnily enough – the bosses, who’ll raise your pre-fight spirit with some amusingly terrible trash talk before becoming the punchline themselves. I audibly wheezed the first time a death animation immediately cut to the foe’s impromptu funeral, their beaked killer among the precious few guests. And even when the joke is recycled later, I couldn’t help tittering at the sight of my enemy – who seconds earlier, had been attempting to fatally sit on me – lying nobly in state.

Industry observers note that I previously considered ending my Valor Mortis review by calling it a gateway into the more demanding side of action-RPGs; a shorter, simpler alternative to FromSoft’s overwhelming titans that might nonetheless serve to introduce curious newcomers to their shared quirks and qualities. The game equivalent of splashing your chest with water before jumping into a pool. In hindsight, Death’s Door was always a better fit for that description, though there’s enough else here you don’t need to be prepping for something tougher to appreciate its lean, keen adventuring.

According to recent reports, nicolas Cage and Christian Bale may seem like two very different kinds of actors, but they do have something in common. They both truly commit to their roles no matter how bonkers or over-the-top they are. Bale and Cage have played characters who’ve gone bananas on screen, and that’s also the case with their latest movie, Madden. In the sports biopic, Cage and Bale play John Madden and Al Davis, respectively and wear a lot of prosthetics for the roles. And, as CinemaBlend learned, that’s surprisingly how their co-stars met them.

David O. Russell’s Madden – one of the buzzy titles on the 2026 movie schedule – chronicles the life and career of the titular football coach-turned-commentator. Cage really got into the role, and his physical transformation alone is proof of that. The same can be said for Bale, who’s known to transform by gaining or losing weight. So what’s it like to actually see the pair on set and in their element? Well, I recently spoke to co-stars Sienna Miller and Kathryn Hahn about that, and Miller shared a funny story about meeting Bale as Al:.

I met Christian for the first time, decked out as Al. He came to say hi, which was very very exciting, and he was like, you know, [mimics Al Davis’ voice] ‘We're gonna have fun doing this,’ you know? And he's all in the voice, and I was beside myself, because I think he's really the GOAT, but then he's very funny on set and loves to play. And I'd imagined a real intensity, and there is once he's performing. But he loves to have a laugh off, you know, in between, and was not as you know — I think as actors, we're like a bunch of kids in a fancy dress cupboard, and that's what it felt like on this.

Recent findings suggest that miller plays the role of Carol Sagal Davis – the wife of late Oakland Raiders owner Al Davis – so she and Bale spent quite a bit of time together on set. For me, the mere thought of meeting Bale when he’s not in character seems intimidating, so I can’t even fathom the idea of being introduced to him while he’s decked out in prosthetics. What also has me chuckling is the thought of the Oscar winner keeping his character’s distinct accent while introducing himself to Miller. Nevertheless, it sounds like the two got along just fine.

During my recent interview, of course, I was also shocked to hear about Kathryn Hahn – who plays Virginia Fields Madden – meeting Nic Cage for the first time on set while he was under all of that heavy makeup. And, believe it or not, at the time we spoke, Hahn said she had never even been in Cage’s presence when he wasn’t in costume and prosthetics. She explained:.

Recent findings suggest that we were just saying that I've never seen Nic not as John Madden, so it's going to be so weird to finally be like, ‘Nice to meet you.’.... It's not like he was like a method actor, but there was a way of being that he instantly just filled out whenever he would put those prosthetics on. So yeah, that was the first time I met him was as John Madden, basically.

Something I can’t help but wonder is whether Cage’s Longlegs co-stars ever met him when he wasn’t dressed as the titular serial killer. I can’t imagine Cage sparking unease on set whenever he wasn’t giving that creepy and perfect performance. Yet I can definitely admit I’d still be genuinely creeped out just by being in his presence.

But, as for Madden, I can imagine those on-set interactions being memories that neither Hahn nor Miller will ever forget. Speaking of these two talented actresses, they also wear prosthetics at different points in the movie, though they arguably aren’t as extensive as those of their on-screen partners. Still, like Cage and Bale, Miller and Hahn fully commit to their roles as well, delivering some humorous performances in the process.

Now, if anything I just want to know what it was like when Kathryn Hahn and Nicolas Cage finally met at the Madden premiere. I’m tempted to assume that was a fun moment. But, that aside, check out the movie, which is playing in select theaters and streaming with a Prime Video subscription.

Tech Report: Clair Obscur Studio Has Lost One of Its Most Vital Developers
