General 📈 Bullish 🌐 Rockpapershotgun ↗ Open Full Page

My murderous wine merchant whines for a chance at republican rule in Crusader Kings 3’s Silk and Silver expansion, which isn't only about the money

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read (2082 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rockpapershotgun

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The tentacles of my trade empire snake up towards France in the west, down towards Africa in the south, and off into Hungary in the east.
  • Sources indicate that I’ve shed blood in its name, the blood of someone else named Marco no less.
  • It should, in theory, help that he’s my best mate, thanks to a well-timed feast.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The tentacles of my trade empire snake up towards France in the west, down towards Africa in the south, and off into Hungary in the east. Yet, I still can’t reach out and grasp the throne that sits right in front of me. I’m Marco Sanudo, and the throne of the serene republic of Venice eludes me.

Sources indicate that I’ve shed blood in its name, the blood of someone else named Marco no less. I’ve managed to avoid punishment for that crime, despite the fact it earned me a fiefdom to rule while I’ve tried to up my patrician score enough to be the lucky party the next time a ruling Doge dies in office (or runs out their 10 year term). Sadly, Doge Leonardo, the mysterious masked lord who’s had an iron grip on power since the first couple of old blokes to hold the position in this playthrough popped their clogs, is proving incredibly tough to oust.

It should, in theory, help that he’s my best mate, thanks to a well-timed feast. It certainly did in being granted a pardon for offing that other Marco, but not even that and a plague which infected nearly everyone in the realm aside from me have paved the way to Dogedom. In the meantime, I’ve striven to gain wealth and influence. I’ve worked up to having four trade routes running at once, with goods like wine, iron, and textiles flowing from market to market across southern Europe and bringing a steady supply of coin back to my Venetian estate. I’ve built trade posts at the extremities of my routes, giving me the option of starting from further afield and reaching fresh lands if the cash flow dries up closer to home.

It has been revealed that this is where Crusader Kings 3’s Silk and Silver expansion has blended a bit with the game’s traditional feudal moneymaking to supercharge my coffers. The land holding I killed a dude for, the Proveditorate of Zara, means I’ve also had tax money from modern day Croatia to add to both my trade profits and the income my domicile generates on its own. I am, as the medieval kids say, minted.

It has been revealed that getting to the point of serious pocket clinkage is, as you might imagine given Silk and Silver’s focus on filling the game’s world with travelling merchant companies and wheeler-dealing republican patrician families, the beating heart of the expansion. A near-constant stream of notifications about prices of different goods I’m trying to hawk in different locations encourage me to regularly prune and re-work my routes so that max profits are being earned and no carrying capacity’s being wasted. The bubbling up of wars and plagues impacts prices in affected cities, making it a never-ending battle if you’re desperate to optimise everything within an inch of its life. I’ve found that degree of micromanagement unnecessary if the goal is just to keep a decent profit margin ticking over. Just remember to replace the trader assigned to a route if they die, recall them every few years so they don’t stress themselves to death, and check in every so often to re-evaluate whether you’re running goods that are suitably in demand.

It has been revealed that if you stick at it for a decent amount of time, with a certain type of good - alcohol or jewellery, for example - your expertise in dealing in them increases, making it easier to sell for better prices. Trade routes left running between the same markets also gain boons from being in place for a long time, offering a counterpoint to rejigging them every five seconds to wring out a few more coins. Most of my routes have run along a path that includes stops at four markets, with the occasional location boasting a monopoly I’ve bargained for with the local ruler, so I don’t have to worry about competition at every stop.

When you’re playing as a merchant who isn’t locked into the ruling inner circle of a republic, making your routes as lengthy as possible is one of the three moneymaking areas your company can specialise in. That first one’s caravaneering, and is the one I leant into in a non-Marco Sanudo playthrough. Beyond that, you can become an expert loan shark, lending cash to rulers or paying their ransoms in order to recoup interest and collect hooks you can use for favours. Manufacturing expensive artifacts that can be sold individually to collectors for a profit is the third option. The latter two I’ve only dabbled in a little bit as of writing, having earned enough gold mostly from caravanneering to buy the land containing the city with my home market and be anointed a Sheikh. So, beginning as a landless merchant is a nice alternative to Crusader Kings 3’s long-established wandering adventurer starting point, with both allowing you to work your way up from lowly serf to landed lordly dynasty in your location of choice.

According to recent reports, if you’re after a more specific historical scenario, Silk and Silver has Guelphs and Ghibellines. This is where we find Marco Sanudo, as well as the other patrician family head I’ve played as thus far, Speronella Dalesmanni. The setup is that the Pope and the Holy Roman Emperor have had a bit of a tiff, essentially rooted in who should have certain powers, with different cities and powerful families in northern Italy taking either the Guelph (Pope-likers) or Ghibelline (Holy Roman Empire-enjoyers) side depending on what suits their goals or principles. I’ll be honest, aside from being another way to easily earn friends or enemies in the ruthless crucible of merchant republican politics, where votes and reputation-bolstering aid from other nobles are key, the situation’s not had a hugely obvious bearing on my playthroughs thus far.

Sources indicate that I think the closest it’s come is during my Dalesmanni run, if largely due to the existence of the By God Alone expansion allowing a latest branch of Catholicism, dubbed Italian Christianity, to be created. The initial conversion push from the bishop responsible led a number of my fellow northern Italian nobles away from the Roman Rite headed by his Popeliness, making the Guelph/Ghibelline split more clearly defined.

In the early hours of both my Sanudo and Dalesmanni playthroughs, I’ve been far more focused on simply trying to push the respective patrician families up the hill from posh toffs with naught but a vote and a manor to elected rulers of their great cities, with land holdings to match. Speronella’s situation in Padua is made incredibly tough by the fact she’s a woman in a world where every succession rule is designed to put blokes first, so I’ve had more success with Marco and his quest to become the Doge of Venice.

As the head of a patrician family, one of select few elite clans who steer the oligarchical republic, I was faced with earning Marco enough respect among his fellow family heads that they’d consider voting him to the top of the succession list, thus securing his power whenever the current Doge got the boot. Pulling that off, while also not kowtowing to the requests and schemes of those same peers, isn’t easy. A large cocktail of factors go into determining whether another noble likes you enough to vote in support of your succession. There’s your patrician rating, which is upped by doing things which specifically show you to be good at this Italian noble house lark, such as establishing trade monopolies for the republic, gaining the Pope’s favour, or having close relatives who also hold key positions in the republic. However, how close a friendship you have with the target and how their character traits align with you also play a huge rule.

It has been revealed that thus it was that, at one point, Marco was best mates with the current Doge and had a decent patrician rating, but had only amassed 68 of the 72 points needed for said Doge to vote for him because the Doge was generous, and therefore didn’t care for Marco’s ambitiousness. That same Doge either liked or respected Marco enough to grant him a council position and the status of regent, but he would not back Marco to replace him permanently for love nor money. This is the same man who liked Marco so much that when I pulled off that not-so-sneaky murder on another noble house head in order to inherit the keys to the Proveditorate of Zara, the Doge was instantly willing to pardon me and prevent Marco suffering any punishment for the crime.

Not even a couple of serious plagues hitting Venice, which at one point had all three people ahead of Marco in the queue suffering from smallpox, could get him on that throne. Eventually, it took a bit of lucky timing when his Doge mate died of old age - a few years after beating smallpox - to finally install Marco as Doge. Given that delayed promotion, as of writing I’ve not yet had enough time in the substantial chair to give a proper verdict on how it differs from regular feudal rulerdom in the long run.

What I can do instead is tell you a bit about the fun of council votes. The same pool of voters who in a republic like Venice, get a say in who succeeds the ruler, also vote on the passage of laws and decrees. One proposal you can put forward is a vote to change who exactly is allowed a seat in this voting pool. It defaults to just being heads of patrician families, but can be extended to include all vassals, or tightened up so only the Doge’s councillors or the ruler themselves have a say, that being the way despotism lies. As you can imagine, passing a change to who can vote can drastically change the state of play, either tightening up the number of folks who might oppose or support you, or bringing fresh folks into play in a fashion that dilutes individual power, but gives you more pieces on the board to mind or manipulate to your advantage.

Sources indicate that I’ve found it suitably tough to orchestrate successful votes to change laws and customs which medieval Italian noble families, expectedly, have firmly entrenched stances on. Getting rid of checks and balances, such as the requirement to vote on banishments or wars - so the Doge can rule as a despot - has proven one such challenge, as has changing laws governing men being prioritised over women. I tried to pass equal succession as a substitute for men being put first while playing as Speronella, but met an insurmountable wall of resistance due to the region’s culture and faith. So, all I could do was try to put my young male heir in the best position possible to make the sorts of gains I couldn’t.

Much easier to weasel into place, either through some canny swaying or the offering of hooks, are laws giving state backing or other priority to trading in certain types of goods. Alcohol, for instance, which certainly hasn’t hurt the profits of Marco’s two wine trade routes.

Thus, cash continues to flow through the tentacles of my trade empire in sizable globs. As he’s now Doge, I’ve got Marco using the ample funds of Venice’s treasury to build a new piazza and have him focused on making the city’s already-strong trade league even more formidable, by attracting new members from the few other northern Italian blocs.

Sources indicate that while I’m fairly sure there are folks who’ll find Silk and Silver's constant barrage of trade route notifications annoying, or that their power-grabbing skills and sheer multitude of money-making means combine to make playthroughs less challenging than they could be, so far I've found it another enjoyably sonorous string to Crusader Kings 3’s bow. Above all else, playing as a merchant gives more reason to invest in stewardship skills beyond just maximising your tax yields, while the republican politics of the DLC's main region fleshes out rewarding intrigue-focused builds. Diplomacy and martial skills are less key, but still have their place at times.

If you’re an absolute stickler for historical accuracy, you may well find other things to gripe about, but aside from the Guelph and Ghibelline conflict fading into the background, I’ve found plenty to like in my quest to become top Doge.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • You'll find the Dinka Enduro motorcycle and Crest Kayak around Jason's House in Key Lento, Mariana County.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

GTA 6's Ultimate Edition features a collection of different items and pre-order bonuses, including vehicles, weapons, and cosmetics. These are unlocked at different points in the story, and some need to be collected from locations around the map. This GTA 6 guide includes step-by-step instructions on how to collect them and when they become available.

Sources indicate that there are 15 extra packs included if you pre-ordered GTA 6's Ultimate Edition. This is where you find them:.

You'll find the Dinka Enduro motorcycle and Crest Kayak around Jason's House in Key Lento, Mariana County. They're marked on the map, as shown below:.

Here's the Dinka Enduro motorcycle underneath Jason's house:.

The Crest Kayak is then at the bottom of the ramp leading into the water:.

You can also equip a custom Retro livery to Jason's Vapid Ganado by taking it to any Mod Shop, like Coastal Auto Care. Here's what the Retro livery looks like; you'll find it under Pro Builds > Full Kits > Retro Build - Ultimate Edition:.

These items are only available in Chapter 1.

An early mission in Chapter 1 will see you go to an Ammu-Nation to purchase a new weapon. Having done so, the Duval Signature ES9 Variant will unlock in the nearby Weapon Locker.

Here's where the mission will take you on the map, with the Duval Signature ES9 Variant for Jason first found there:.

The Electric Fang Tattoo Parlor is located on Coral Ave, Stockyard, Vice City, Vice-Dale County from Chapter 1. Here's how it looks from the outside:.

And here's its location on the map:.

You can set a waypoint under the tabs Style > Tattoos:.

Many of the items here are Ultimate Edition exclusive, and marked with a blue tab in the top-right corner:.

Industry observers note that the Goodtime Gear items can be purchased beginning Chapter 1 at The Wonder Whale shop on Sunbelt Hwy, Key Lento, Mariana County. This is how it looks from the outside:.

In a recent development, here's the location on your map. You can also set a marker to the exact store by selecting the Style > Souvenir & Swimwear tabs, as below:.

You'll find the Goodtime Gear items inside the shop, on mannequins just left of the entrance:.

The Ultimate Edition exclusive items are marked with a blue tab, as shown:.

According to recent reports, you can find One-Eyed Willie's Auto Shop just off SR-27 in North Leonard County starting from Chapter 1. It looks like this from the outside:.

And here's a map view to help direct you to the right spot:.

You can set a waypoint using the menu tabs Vehicles > Mod Shops:.

Drive in to the mod shop to find exclusive paint jobs and body work, many of which are exclusive to the Ultimate Edition:.

According to recent reports, you'll need to have visited South Vice-Dale County before the PTT Youngin$ Illegal Goods robberies unlock starting from Chapter 1. Once you have, you'll find two robberies in and around SW 13th St and El Joven Blvd in Southside.

Here's how one looks from the outside:.

And here's a map view of the two:.

You can set a waypoint directly to them from the Robberies > Illegal Operations tab in your map:.

Take out the gang members inside and loot all the jewelry and drugs before the police arrive:.

Then make a quick getaway in your vehicle:.

Remember to stow the stolen goods and take them to a nearby fence for cash:.

According to recent reports, the Rideout Custom Mod Shop is located in Crosstown, Vice City, Vice-Dale County. Here's what it looks like outside:.

And here's a its location on your map:.

It has been revealed that note that it's marked with an Ultimated Edition symbol. It can be found under the Vehicles > Mod Shops tab of the map menu:.

Take your car here to customise it with all kinds of specialty rims and interiors. Items exclusive to the Rideout Custom Mod Shop will be marked:.

You can visit Sara's Unisex Salon from Chapter 1, but Signature styles will not unlock until Chapter 2. Here's what the shop looks like:.

And here's its location on your map, which can be found under the Style > Hair & Beauty tab. It's located on Cicada Ave, Hamlet, South Vice-Dale County, Vice-Dale County:.

Ultimate Edition exclusive items are marked with a blue tab in the top-right corner:.

Stock 305 can be access on NE 15th St, Stockyard, Vice City, Vice-Dale County from Chapter 1. It looks like this from the outside:.

Here's its location on the map:.

You can find it with the map tabs by selecting Style > Casual & Street:.

Inside you'll find Ultimate Edition exclusive clothes for both Jason and Lucia:.

You'll get a notification as you progress through Chapter 2 that your '67 Dominator Buggy is available to collect from your Paradise garage, which looks like this:.

In a recent development, the Paradise garage is in Watson Bay, Mariana County. Here's its location on your map just in case you get lost:.

Get inside the '67 Dominator Buggy to register it. Any current cars you're using will be sent back to one of your other garages automatically:.

You'll also unlock some liveries for the '67 Dominator Buggy you can access by taking it to any Pay 'n' Spray.

Shortly after collecting your '67 Vapid Dominator from the Paradise garage, you'll receive a text message on your phone from Wyman telling you about a classic car you can recover and tune up. The message looks like this:.

This triggers a fresh chain of quests under the Exploration tab of your map. To unlock the cars you need to find multiple scraps and WAiNK them so Wyman can collect the parts and restore them.

Go to any Ammunation store around Leonidas and select Manage Weapons at the Weapon Locker, like below:.

From Chapter 2 onwards, you'll find the Hawk & Little Morgan in the Revolvers section of both Jason and Lucia's Weapon Locker:.

Your Vintage Vice City Pack pre-order bonus will become available shortly after you arrive in Vice City. A marker will appear on your map telling you to visit the familiar Ocean View Hotel in Vice Beach, telling you to pick up your '55 Vapid Stanier, which can be located like below:.

In a recent development, the car is unlocked, and once you get inside you'll automatically receive the Shore Court garage as well as latest clothes in your wardrobe. A prompt will inform you of this:.

You'll also find new hairstyles and more in the Special tab at salons as well as various gun liveries at Ammunation, marked with the Vintage Vice City Pack label:.

Industry observers note that you can collect your Shitzu Squalo beginning Chapter 4, docked near to Atlantic Ave, Washington Beach, Vice Beach, Vice-Dale County. Here's where you'll find it:.

In a recent development, here's a map view. It's just east of the Y Hotel:.

You will find it on the Personal section of your map tabs, but only when you're in a nearby area:.

Once you've made progress in Chapter 4, items from the Vice City Style items will be automatically added to your Wardrobe and the Special tab of of most hair salons and tattoo parlours, as below:.

Recent findings suggest that you'll get a notification about the '95 Grotti Cheetah upon completing Honest Abe in Chapter 5. Follow the waypoint to Pegassi Residences and go through the main front door, as shown:.

Go inside the main entrance and use the lift opposite the entrance:.

Head down to Parking B1 in the lift:.

Your '95 Grotti Cheetah will be parked up and waiting for you to get inside:.

Industry observers note that GTA 6's Ultimate Edition costs $99.99/£89.99/€99.99. The Standard Edition costs $79.99/£69.99/€79.99.

Yes, I personally think GTA 6's Ultimate Edition is worth it, but it really depends how excited you are for the game and whether you want to get the most out of it.

All of the additional Mod Shops and Stores exclusive to the Ultimate Edition, along with their unique inventory, means you're really adding a lot of cosmetic and personalisation options to the title with the Ultimate Edition.

If you're not the type of player that aims to dress up Jason and Lucia and fiddle with their vehicles, then you may not find value in this.

But it's worth adding that the Classic Car Collection, which adds collectibles quests involving Wyman, are also exclusive to the Ultimate Edition.

You can still enjoy GTA 6 to its fullest without paying for the Ultimate Edition, but you'll get much more out of the game if you do.

Yes, the Ultimate Edition Upgrade can be purchased from the PS Store at any time for $20.00/£20.00/€20.00 and will automatically add all of the extra content to your game once installed.

You'll need to buy the Ultimate Edition Upgrade if you purchase a physical edition of GTA 6, as this content isn't included with the retail release.

Sources indicate that if you've followed this guide carefully, then you should now have collected all of your Ultimate Edition items and pre-order bonuses in GTA 6. Congratulations for getting them all!

Remember, you can refer to our GTA 6 guide for a lot more info on the game, including collectibles, walkthroughs, and much more.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, I don’t know about you, but my curiosity about Robert Downey Jr. in Avengers: Doomsday just keeps growing. Even though we know he’s under the mask of Doctor Doom, there’s a lot we still don’t know about his role in the newest upcoming Marvel movie. Now, with just a month between us and Doomsday, RDJ got real about where he was at with the MCU before he got the call to join it again.

Downey was revealed to be Doomsday’s Victor von Doom in the summer of 2024, during Marvel’s Hall H panel at San Diego Comic-Con. It was a huge surprise not only to fans but to the actor, too. As the Oscar winner shared:.

I kind of made my peace with it, and it felt so definitive by the time Endgame had been released. When it was first broached by Kevin [Feige], who said, ‘Hey, do you think you would ever?’ And then, I really just thought, ‘How many surprises are left?’.

When Avengers: Endgame came out in 2019, it was the end of an era for the MCU. It felt like the franchise had found a great way to wrap up the arc of Tony Stark/Iron Man by having him be the one to save the universe from Thanos. As RDJ said in a upcoming Marvel video, he had made his “peace” with no longer being part of the MCU. But then Marvel president Kevin Feige called.

According to recent reports, recasting the same actor in the same franchise in a different role is pretty unheard of, unless you’re the MCU. It’s the ultimate massive move for The Multiverse Saga, and clearly they convinced the actor to rejoin the Marvel family in a whole new way. As Downey Jr. continued:.

Any of these movies is only as good as its villain. Victor is a master manipulator, and because of that, there’s levels to the stakes here. It’s such a long bench of talent. These people are people that I would do any movie with eight days a week. We just really keep trying to earn it with every breath. It’s really hard to explain the love I have for this.

Aww, this is sweet. I mean, it’s quite the honor to be asked to play a Marvel villain, especially when it’s one that will assemble just about every character in the universe. It’s wild when you think about it, because the villain that was originally being teased as the massive bad of this saga was Kang. However, after Jonathan Majors got caught in some legal trouble, Marvel made a pivot. However, according to recent words from Feige, Doctor Doom was allegedly always in the cards.

And let’s not forget that Chris Evans’ Steve Rogers is also set to come back alongside the likes of Chris Hemsworth’s Thor, Paul Rudd’s Ant-Man, Anthony Mackie’s Sam Wilson, Tom Hiddleston’s Loki, and the casts of Fantastic Four: First Steps, Thunderbolts* and the original X-Men movies.

Industry observers note that RDJ’s comments certainly make me wonder what we don’t know about Doctor Doom. And I can't wait to learn more about him when Avengers: Doomsday hits theaters on December 18. While we wait, you can catch up on all the Marvel movies and TV highlights thus far with a Disney+ subscription.

Industry News: Interest in The Legend of Zelda was "getting smaller and smaller" before Breath of the Wild, according to former Nintendo marketing leads

💡 Key Takeaways
  • The Legend of Zelda was in "dire straits" before Breath of the Wild gave the beloved series a massive second wind, according to two former Nintendo marketing leads.
  • Sources indicate that the Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time's most recent remake has been a mega success, becoming the fastest-selling Switch 2 game so far, but the shiny fresh adventure has also prompted some online debate over where the series should go next.
  • Nintendo of America's ex-director of social media marketing Kit Ellis and former public relations manager Krysta Yang chimed in on the discourse in their latest podcast (below), and explained that Zelda wasn't doing too hot before the Switch era.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Legend of Zelda was in "dire straits" before Breath of the Wild gave the beloved series a massive second wind, according to two former Nintendo marketing leads.

Sources indicate that the Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time's most recent remake has been a mega success, becoming the fastest-selling Switch 2 game so far, but the shiny fresh adventure has also prompted some online debate over where the series should go next. Should Zelda lean into its carefully directed history - like the one brilliantly remade in Ocarina of Time - or keep the ball rolling with Breath of the Wild's wide open, spontaneous sandbox?

Nintendo of America's ex-director of social media marketing Kit Ellis and former public relations manager Krysta Yang chimed in on the discourse in their latest podcast (below), and explained that Zelda wasn't doing too hot before the Switch era.

"There has been some revisionist history out there lately," Ellis noted in response to fans who reckon "the Zelda team ripped away" series staples, like classic dungeons and linear worlds, at the height of their popularity.

Industry observers note that "I remember, I was going to the focus groups where it was a really dark moment," Ellis continued. "The feedback was like, 'The fan base is dwindling. This is not bringing in newly introduced players.'".

According to recent reports, the Legend of Zelda was supposedly "shrinking," while "interest in the audience was getting smaller and smaller" with each latest entry. "They had to do something dramatic," Ellis remarked.

It has been revealed that "This series was in dire straits. They were selling, like, nothing," Yang added.

The Zelda series was certainly never irrelevant, but there's a pretty big gap between the roughly 8m copies Twilight Princess sold at the beginning of the Wii generation, the roughly 3m copies Skyward Sword sold at the end of the console's life, and the 34m copies that Breath of the Wild sold just one console generation later.

According to recent reports, it was a success so big it spawned a wildly ambitious sequel, Tears of the Kingdom, and even influenced the latest 2D Zelda, Echoes of Wisdom. Now that classic Zelda's back in the spotlight, though, I do hope Nintendo's able to slot the series' curated dungeons into whatever the next mainline game becomes.

Spirit Crossing, the fresh Zelda-ish hangout MMO from the creators of Cozy Grove, understands that sometimes you just want to be alone

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (643 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rockpapershotgun

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Newly introduced multiplayer game Spirit Crossing offers up a visually blissful, but inwardly draconian world in which other people are not allowed to talk to you – indeed, not permitted access to the visible electromagnetic spectrum – unless you have given them a high five.
  • In a recent development, deign to slap somebody's hand, and they'll pop into colour and be able to join you for various activities.
  • There's nothing forcing you to do any of this in firm, mind.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Newly introduced multiplayer game Spirit Crossing offers up a visually blissful, but inwardly draconian world in which other people are not allowed to talk to you – indeed, not permitted access to the visible electromagnetic spectrum – unless you have given them a high five. By default, players appear to each other as shadows, all exploring a skybound landscape of magic animals and layer-cake mountains that reminds me of both Sable and The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom.

In a recent development, deign to slap somebody's hand, and they'll pop into colour and be able to join you for various activities. For example, going fishing, playing instruments round the campfire, playing dress-up and pulling emotes in group photos, bouncing around on strangely inflated yaks, or questing forth to heal troubled spirits. There's some material gathering and crafting, and there are recurring storms that make the ambience more threatening, but overcoming a challenge doesn't feel like the point of Spirit Crossing. The "missions" are just an excuse to hang out together.

There's nothing forcing you to do any of this in firm, mind. "Stay a mysterious shadow, lend a hand when you feel like it, and disappear before anyone can make it weird," the devs explain, adding a hug emoji to make plain that they don't think you're some kind of smelly misanthrope for shunning other players.

Industry observers note that I, personally, am a smelly misanthrope, and will only ever appear in your game as a skulking opacity, peering through the window of your personal gingerbread house, with its tastefully accessorised lava lamps and throw rugs. No, I will not join you for a group hang-glider tour. No, I do not want to play the banjo with you. You will experience me only as the nagging sensation of being watched, while you chat to the local "Stylesmith" about fetching rucksack patterns.

It has been revealed that spirit Crossing has an upfront cost that "gives players full access to the complete game experience in perpetuity", but you can also take out a subscription for some cosmetic items and access to a "limited resource exchange shop". They're avoiding traditional microtransactions, which is nice.

Recent findings suggest that spry Fox are also the developers of Cozy Grove - "the best grove since Byker", wrote Graham, in one of his regular 'senior moments'. I myself know them as the studio behind wintry puzzler Road Not Taken, with its randomised woodlands, and block-merging city builder Triple Town, with its unexpectedly terrifying bears. Little about Spirit Crossing seems terrifying, unless you count the shadow loitering at the edge of your conversation pit.

According to recent reports, you can read more about the game on Steam. I find Spirit Crossing quite novel, especially when it dispenses with the WholeCosy "discover your inner fashonista" stuff and leans into the supernatural elements: I like the idea of hunkering by the campfire during a storm, watching the clouds hurtle past. Still, I'm disappointed to hear that Spry Fox have made use of generative AI during its creation.

As has been pointed out to us on Bluesky, the developers called on Anthropic's Claude tools for various behind-the-scenes tasks - the example they give in a Discord post is editing several config files at once. There's no disclosure on the game's Steam page because Spry Fox haven't used AI tools to generate any of the art or music - Valve rewrote Steam's disclosure requirements in January to exempt the usage of generative AI for "efficiency gains", which the above presumably falls under.

It's hardly a full-throated endorsement of generative AI, but it still forms part of a political and cultural project I consider reckless and morbid. For a longer account of my objections, albeit one that doesn't cover Claude in particular, here's my longform thinkywangle from July last year.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • "Ubisoft is reducing its workforce by 166 positions across its Montréal and Québec City operations," the company states in a statement provided to IGN and other outlets.
  • Recent findings suggest that the firm's statement does not specify which projects are affected by the layoffs, though IGN reports that the layoffs primarily affect employees who'd been working on canceled or reworked games.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, ubisoft has been slowly rolling out mass layoffs since its big restructure earlier this year, and its latest will directly affect the studios responsible for games like Assassin's Creed and Far Cry. Well over 100 developers will lose their jobs at Ubisoft Montréal and Ubisoft Québec.

"Ubisoft is reducing its workforce by 166 positions across its Montréal and Québec City operations," the company states in a statement provided to IGN and other outlets. "As our portfolio evolves, our production needs are changing, requiring us to adjust the size of some teams to ensure our resources are aligned with current production priorities and business needs.".

Recent findings suggest that the firm's statement does not specify which projects are affected by the layoffs, though IGN reports that the layoffs primarily affect employees who'd been working on canceled or reworked games. (Both GamesIndustry.biz and VGC offer near-identical background reporting on the nature of the layoffs.).

Recent findings suggest that the Montréal studio has been around since 1997, and is one of the publisher's flagship development houses, leading development on the Splinter Cell, Prince of Persia, Far Cry, and Assassin's Creed franchises over the years. It's now leading development on Assassin's Creed Hexe. Ubisoft Québec has similarly led many Assassin's Creed titles, including Odyssey and Shadows.

Both offices are now part of Vantage Studios, a Tencent-backed subsidiary focused on developing games in the Assassin's Creed, Far Cry, and Rainbow Six series. Some of Ubisoft's Montréal operation is now also part of Massive Entertainment, which primarily handles Tom Clancy-branded titles, including The Division, Ghost Recon, and Splinter Cell.

"We deeply value the contributions of these teams and recognize the impact this may have on our colleagues," Ubisoft's statement concludes. "We are committed to supporting them through this process with care and respect. Those affected are being provided with severance, extended health care benefits, career transition services and other resources.".

After laying off thousands, Ubisoft says losing "key talents and skills" is a massive danger for the organization.

#51606. Tech Report: Microsoft's SideWinder Strategic Commander was a failed attempt to reimagine RTS controls. 23 years later, why are some players still using it?

📅 17 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 8m • 📚 Deep Dive (1517 w)
📖 Baca
AI & Tech 📈 Bullish 🌐 Rockpapershotgun ↗ Open Full Page

Tech Report: Microsoft's SideWinder Strategic Commander was a failed attempt to reimagine RTS controls. 23 years later, why are some players still using it?

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1517 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rockpapershotgun

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, PC players have been conditioned for decades to accept the keyboard-and-mouse setup for RTS games.
  • According to recent reports, unveiled on March 1st 2000 at Microsoft's Gamestock event, the Strategic Commander was one of three additions to their SideWinder line, with a scheduled release that October at a pricey $64.95.
  • It has been revealed that microsoft, all the while, were taking notes.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, PC players have been conditioned for decades to accept the keyboard-and-mouse setup for RTS games. One hand has to handle movement and commands through a keyboard, while the other points, drags, and selects with a mouse. Peripheral makers have, usually with the addition of more buttons, made many minor variations to this time-honored arrangement, but there's only ever been one real attempt to rethink it entirely for the PC: the Microsoft SideWinder Strategic Commander.

According to recent reports, unveiled on March 1st 2000 at Microsoft's Gamestock event, the Strategic Commander was one of three additions to their SideWinder line, with a scheduled release that October at a pricey $64.95. At E3 later that May, Microsoft demonstrated the Strategic Commander for the first time with SimCity 3000, while promoting its potential for other such games as Diablo II, Warcraft III, and Baldur's Gate II. This was all taking place during the so-called 'Golden Age of Real-Time Strategy Games,' which spanned roughly from the mid-1990s to the mid-2000s. It was when the RTS genre was at the peak of its mainstream popularity, and we fans were devoted to mastering its intricacies in any way we could to have a competitive edge.

It has been revealed that microsoft, all the while, were taking notes. "The team conceived the Strategic Commander in the late 1990s," Carl Ledbetter - then Industrial Design Manager for Microsoft's PC Hardware Group, now Head of Design for Xbox Devices - recalls to me. "As RTS games grew in popularity, we saw an interesting opportunity to design a new physical interface around a new interaction model. The idea was for it to be used left-handed in concert with right-hand PC desktop mouse control. We wanted to enable players to perform faster with more fluidity, comfort, optimised control placement for multiple hand sizes, simplicity of set-up, and ease of programming.".

It has been revealed that for Ledbetter and co. to realise this ambition, the Strategic Commander was designed as a unique combination of mouse, joystick, and gamepad. To manage the increasing complexities of the RTS games of the day, it came equipped with six programmable buttons, three shift buttons, and a three-position profile switch. Back then, these atypical features provided an unprecedented 72 possible key combinations across various configurations, all at the tip of our stubby little fingers. Better yet, it allowed us to toggle between three pre-configured profiles at a time, so that we could switch up our configurations on the fly depending on which stage of an RTS match we were in.

According to recent reports, on release, contemporary reviewers acknowledged its originality, with critics like ActiveWin's Julien Jay describing it as "probably the most innovative (with the GameVoice) and revolutionary" peripheral designed specifically for strategy players. Others, like Neoseeker's Arnel Lim, suggested that it might’ve gone overboard with its customisation options, saying "you won't use anywhere close to all of them," in reference to the controller's programmable key combinations. Either way, the Strategic Commander failed to supplant conventional peripherals in the hands of most RTS players, and it was discontinued in 2003. As was the rest of the original SideWinder line, owing to declining sales and the industry-wide shift toward standard M+K setups for all PC games and genres.

However, unlike so many of its Microsoft-made siblings, this was not the end for the Strategic Commander. Niche as it was, it went on to enjoy a surprisingly long post-shelf life, one that was stretched out by a dedicated cult following - and that continues to this day. But why? Why, after all these years, is this forgotten peripheral from a discontinued line maintaining such a enthusiastic fanbase, years after the industry around it had written it off as a failure?

According to recent reports, the answer lies in software and OS compatibility, as much as the hardware's own appeal. Andreas Weis was the developer of one of the first unofficial patches for the Strategic Commander, allowing players to keep on using it even after the original software stopped being compatible with newer versions the Windows. By that point, the device was a decade old, and well into 'official' obsolescence, yet Weis still answered the call of the Strategic Commander's righteously frustrated - if numerically few - fans. "There was a lot of interest back in the early 2010s in software patches to keep the Strategic Commander functional when the original software for the Strategic Commander stopped working," he explains. "Users were asking around on internet forums about how to get it to work on Windows 7 and Vista machines. Since I was studying computer science at the time, I was quite interested in reverse-engineering, and I hacked together a simple tool that would cover my use cases for the device.".

Recent findings suggest that in the years that followed, other patches were released to keep the Strategic Commander operational, the most notable of which was Philip Merwarth’s Strategic Engine software in 2013. Unfortunately, they weren’t open-source. Worse was that the protocol for programming the Strategic Commander wasn’t documented anywhere online in a way that was accessible for customers. This is why Weis realized that he could make a unique contribution.

Sources indicate that "I polished my old prototype code for the Strategic Commander software patch and released it as a library, so that other people could use it to write their own applications for programming the tool," he claims. "As for me, I released one application that made use of the library publicly, the vJoy feeder application, which allows the device to be used with games that support joystick inputs." Curiously, Weis, by this time and like many others, had found other applications for a device with such a specific selling point, and even continues to use the Strategic Commander sparingly in 2026.

"The production quality of Microsoft hardware at the time was just top-notch, and I love the design of the old SideWinder devices, which is why I did not just throw the thing out when the software stopped working," he tells me. "It was worth keeping around to find upcoming uses for it over the years, and I eventually realized that it makes quite a nice addition to a HOTAS (Hands-On Throttle And Stick) setup, where I could put actions that aren’t time-critical and don't fit well on the throttle on the Strategic Commander instead. For example, when I’m playing Elite Dangerous in VR, I’d put actions like deploying the landing gear on the Strategic Commander to free up buttons on the throttle for actions that were more relevant for combat.".

When looking back at the history of Microsoft’s SideWinder line, it’s easy to call the Strategic Commander a failed experiment, given the fact that most of us are still using the same standard mouse-and-keyboard setup to play RTS games. However, the central premise behind its design philosophy was that the interface between a player and a game could be redesigned to cater to specific genre quirks, and decades following its release, it’s still maintained a coalition of loyal users: some RTS players who believed the Strategic Commander really pulled it off, and those found other uses for the device in other flavours of PC game. And with the concern of modern compatibility, a roadblock for so much retro hardware, bypassed by homemade patches, both camps can continue twisting and clicking their Strategic Commanders unimpeded.

All the same, I wonder if it might have basked in more conventional success, had Microsoft made more forward-thinking decisions. The Strategic Commander has proven over the years that its unprecedented customisation had applications far beyond what Ledbetter’s team had envisioned, and once the popularity of RTS games settled down, other, similar click-heavy subgenres like MOBAs and Real-Time Tactics got big as well. Would a more officially maintained, potentially refined Strategic Commander model have served those crowds? I think it might. The narrow focus on RTS games may have also hurt the device's since-demonstrated broader appeal; if Microsoft had fully capitalised on this customisation selling point by communicating its benefits to everyone, not just those playing the single most popular PC genre at the time, it could have provided the blueprint for a proper, long-lived alternative to controllers, mice, and keyboards.

In a recent development, alas, gaming history is littered with revolutionary peripherals that failed to actually revolutionise the industry surrounding them. The Strategic Commander is no different, but for the fact that it’s had this surprisingly long post-shelf life - and, as a result, the opportunity for insight into what could have been done to salvage the its failures. Still, that unexpected longevity can provide come comfort to the Strategic Commander's creators, as well as its lingering customers.

Recent findings suggest that "I think the design made sense for its time, especially with the rising popularity of RTS games," Ledbetter reflects. "Looking back, I would have liked more time to test and refine the Strategic Commander. I’m proud of what we brought to market, and I’m glad to know that it remains beloved by many players to this day.".

If you're fed up of GTA 6 at 30 fps, this tool gets it up to 60 and injects DLSS 5 if you have a powerful enough gaming PC

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (762 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Pcgamer

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • With a game as gorgeous as GTA 6, could you want even more, graphically?
  • In both cases, you can either use a capture card or Remote Play to get the game streamed to your gaming PC.
  • Sources indicate that you just have to run a PowerShell command, get Remote Play linked up, and run a short setup with the new Veyra executable.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

With a game as gorgeous as GTA 6, could you want even more, graphically? Well, some PC gamers seem to be answering 'yes' and throwing some DLSS 5 neural rendering into the mix. Oh, and perhaps more importantly for those of you concerned about the low frame rate on console, they're managing to up the frame rate to 60 fps, too.

Sources indicate that how, you ask? In both cases, you can either use a capture card or Remote Play to get the game streamed to your gaming PC. Then, for DLSS 5, you use a tool called Veyra, which can be easily installed and set up by running it via another tool from the modder Phosphen (via VideoCardz).

Sources indicate that you just have to run a PowerShell command, get Remote Play linked up, and run a short setup with the new Veyra executable. Assuming, that is, you have a graphics card that can handle the extra DLSS 5 work. And assuming you can get it to work—my colleague couldn't get the tool to link up to his PS5 when he tried.

Judging by some gameplay capture of GTA 6 with DLSS 5 running on top, and to perhaps state the obvious, it's very graphically impressive. That goes for both the environment and characters.

This tool should get you up and running at 60 fps, too, using frame gen. Essentially, whether by 60 fps capture card or via Remote Play, each of the game's 30 frames per second is duplicated, giving you a 60 fps output that still feels like 30 fps. The tool removes the duplicated frames and then adds frame gen to double them, giving you genuine newly introduced frames interpolated between each actually rendered one. A proper 60 fps, but using frame gen.

Naturally, this will add some latency, especially because extra latency from frame gen is most noticeable when starting at a low base frame rate. Still, it might be worth a try.

It has been revealed that you also don't have to use that tool try to and hit 60 fps, as you could try Lossless Scaling instead. You have to pay for that on Steam, but it lets you add upscaling and frame gen to a bunch of different windows or games, not just GTA 6. If you use this method, you just wrap it over your Remote Play stream of GTA 6.

Keep up to date with the most notable stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

One potential problem with this method, though, relates to what the modder states in their readme: "Frame generation fed with copies makes stutter instead of smoothness." So, if you use Lossless Scaling with GTA 6 streamed over Remote Play for frame gen, the already-doubled output frame rate—ie, the duplicated frames—will likely cause a problem for frame gen, causing stuttering. So, it might be best to stick to upscaling only when using this method.

GTA 6 is a gorgeous game even without DLSS 5, but it doesn't seem like too much hassle to try out the neural rendering, too, if you have the PC for it. And speaking to the frame rate, I imagine there might be more interest in getting this upped to 60 fps on its own, so the tool might be worth a look.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

UPDATE 17TH NOVEMBER: The Blood of Dawnwalker update 1.2 - the update that brings a Latest Game Plus mode, predominantly - is now available on PC, PS5, and Xbox Series S/X.

New Game Plus, as mentioned below, raises the level cap to 100, and scales enemies and regions in the game around you. Previously, the game was zone-scaled, so some zones were tougher than others. In New Game Plus, this will no longer be the case, so you can go and explore Xanthe's region at the back of Vale Sangora straight away, if you want to.

There'll be latest versions of equipment with new stats to find, and they'll be labelled with "NG+" so you know when you've picked one up. You can unlock New Game Plus from the main menu after choosing your base save and difficulty option. All of your accrued skill perks and abilities will be available to you at the start of the Withering Away quest in the game's prologue.

The full patch notes for Dawnwalker upgrade 1.2 are:.

ORIGINAL STORY 13TH NOVEMBER: A Fresh Game Plus mode is coming to vampiric RPG The Blood of Dawnwalker next week.

Developer Rebel Wolves has now detailed everything coming with The Blood of Dawnwalker's Patch 1.2, right now planned to go live sometime next week, and top of the list of changes is a New Game Plus for players who have already rolled credits on the game.

Industry observers note that "If you completed the Epilogue, you can dive right back into Vale Sangora with Latest Game+," the developer revealed earlier today. "Your level, skills, and inventory will carry over." Rebel Wolves is upping the level cap to 100 for New Game Plus, which will also have items with updated stats and enemies "balanced and scaled uniformly across all regions.".

Elsewhere in Patch 1.2, the studio is making tweaks to "enemy health pools and how often they use their abilities during combat," and improving terrain geometry to allow for "smoother movement during combat and exploration." We'll need to wait for more comprehensive patch notes before finding out which enemies are getting spongier or flimsier, however.

While the incoming patch doesn't seem to be as beefy as the last - the one that added animal petting and an easier Story mode - it'll be a good way to sink your teeth deeper into a game that's already begging to be replayed, thanks to a time management mechanic that can drastically change any given run.

Sources indicate that the latest game from some former The Witcher 3 veterans came out in September and seems to have been a hit. Eurogamer's The Blood of Dawnwalker review called the game a "familiar dark fantasy adventure, but one with bold and provocative ideas of its own, that's mostly, enormously successful.".

GTA 6 is a single player game, but Sony’s servers are taking a hammering as the game goes online around the world.

While you can’t play Rockstar’s latest with other people, you will need to verify your digital license once the title is available in your region – a timely reminder of the digital era we’re all now living in.

As the game has released in Fresh Zealand, Australia, and parts of Asia, the PSN servers have held up sturdily – but there have been sporadic reports of outages over the past few hours, as Europe and the UK prepares to play.

According to Sony’s own Service Status Page, everything is working as it should. A quick reboot to your console is a quick way to remedy most challenges.

Remember, you won’t be able to play GTA 6 without the PS5’s latest firmware update v14.23.00 installed, so make sure you’ve got that downloaded and ready.

We’ll continue to monitor the situation as GTA 6’s all-important American launch nears, but fingers crossed there are no challenges and the launch goes flawlessly.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that spoilers for the first five episodes of Rings of Power Season 3 are ahead!
  • On Rings of Power, we’ve spent seasons trying to figure out the identities of the wizards who were sent to Middle-earth.
  • In Episode 3 of the season of Rings of Power that’s currently airing on the 2026 TV schedule, Gandalf has an interaction with the Secret Fire, where it’s revealed to him that five wizards were sent to save Middle-earth.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that spoilers for the first five episodes of Rings of Power Season 3 are ahead! You can stream the series with an Amazon Prime subscription.

On Rings of Power, we’ve spent seasons trying to figure out the identities of the wizards who were sent to Middle-earth. In Season 2, after we spent a lot of time guessing and theorizing, we learned that The Stranger was indeed Gandalf. However, the identity of the Dark Wizard was still unknown. In Season 3, his true name was finally revealed, though, and I asked the co-creator of the show why they wanted to make the Dark Wizard the Blue Wizard Pallando.

In Episode 3 of the season of Rings of Power that’s currently airing on the 2026 TV schedule, Gandalf has an interaction with the Secret Fire, where it’s revealed to him that five wizards were sent to save Middle-earth. That’s how we learned that Pallando, one of the two Blue Wizards, killed his partner, and it’s also when Gandalf learns that he’s been sent to save the corrupted Blue Wizard. When I asked co-creator Patrick McKay why they wanted to make the Dark Wizard Pallando, he began by saying:.

It has been revealed that here's the thing that we do on the show: We trust our audience. We're really thinking of it as one 50-hour movie. That's always been the plan and the aspiration. That also means that when we introduce a upcoming character, you might not know where his or her allegiances lie. You might not know his or her name, but we know, and we have a plan.

While the end of Rings of Power Season 2 made me think the Dark Wizard was Saruman (even though that actually makes no sense timeline-wise), the other prevailing theory was that he was a Blue Wizard. Now, it’s confirmed that that’s the case, and McKay told me they made this decision because of how fascinating the lore is behind these two rather mysterious characters:.

And you know there is this great lore in Tolkien about the two blue wizards who went east. And Tolkien had different versions of it and different ideas he played with. And a recurrent theme was that maybe one of them went bad, and no one knows what happened to the other one. And then, you know, thinking about that and bringing our wizard, our hero wizard Gandalf, sounds good to say that now, into that story, now you're weaving, right?

It has been revealed that at one point, Tolkien wrote that the Blue Wizards could have been “founders or beginners of secret cults and magic traditions that outlasted the fall of Sauron” (via ScreenRant). It’s not confirmed if this is used as inspiration for Rings of Power; however, it does point to the potential moral ambiguity surrounding these magical beings.

Industry observers note that on the show, they ultimately decided to run with the notion that Pallando might have done something terrible and killed his partner. Exploring the complexities of that was very interesting to them, as McKay told me:.

What might be interesting? Well, gosh, what if Pallando has murdered his partner, and that's where he got his power from, but maybe there's complexity to it. Maybe he has guilt over it. Maybe, you know, he even has a desire for redemption. But how much? And then building a story around that was one of the joys of this season. But you know, the idea of the Blue Wizards is always tantalizing to us as fans, and part of our job is the inner fanboy getting to play.

Industry observers note that well, now I’m certainly excited to see where things go from here. I want to see Gandalf and Pallando interact more. I want to know if Gandalf can help his fellow wizard get away from the evil. And I want to know more about why the Blue Wizard killed his friend.

Your Daily Blend of Entertainment News.

Hopefully, that will be unveiled as Rings of Power wraps up its third season and releases Episodes 7 and 8 on November 25.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • A judge has denied a motion to dismiss a US lawsuit against chip makers Samsung, SK Hynix, and Micron.
  • The class action suit was filed at the United States District Court for the Northern District of California in June this year.
  • Sources indicate that the trio of companies deny having colluded, arguing in a upcoming motion to have the case dismissed (thanks, IGN) that this suit simply retreads old ground covered in a previous antitrust case and quoting deceased judge Richard Posner.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A judge has denied a motion to dismiss a US lawsuit against chip makers Samsung, SK Hynix, and Micron. The suit acccuses the companies of fixing RAM prices and supply, thereby contributing to worsening the effects of the ongoing memory crisis.

The class action suit was filed at the United States District Court for the Northern District of California in June this year. It accuses Samsung, SK Hynix, and Micron of moving in lockstep away from production of consumer-focused DDR3 and DDR4 RAM and towards HBM memory more typically used in AI datacenters. The suit claims that "in a competitive commodity market", "at least one of three large producers, seeing record prices, would expand output of the product whose price was rising", thereby forcing their competitors to either follow suit or risk losing out on customers.

Sources indicate that the trio of companies deny having colluded, arguing in a upcoming motion to have the case dismissed (thanks, IGN) that this suit simply retreads old ground covered in a previous antitrust case and quoting deceased judge Richard Posner. "[C]ompetitors in concentrated markets watch each other like hawks," was the Posner quote they wheeled out, which I mention because otherwise the response I'm about to lay out will sound like a very weird tangent.

"But Plaintiffs’ allegations go beyond hawks watching each other," judge Noël Wise wrote in her order to deny the dismissal motion. "Their contentions are more akin to hawks flying in formation – an activity that hawks ordinarily do not do.".

Recent findings suggest that you know a case is getting serious when facts about Avian behaviour start being wheeled out in response to similes. Bird chatter aside, all this decision means is that the case will rumble on, with both sides still having a chance to present more evidence or make points in their favour before any eventual decision is made by the courts.

So, shelve any hopes you might have of a rapid solution to the memory crisis, which presently looks likely to last until at least 2028.

Arcade Archives 2 TX-1 V.8 will launch for PlayStation 5, Xbox Series, and Switch 2, and Arcade Archives TX-1 V.8 for PlayStation 4 and Switch, on November 19, developer Hamster announced. The Arcade Archives 2 version will cost $9.99 / 1,100 yen, while Arcade Archives version will cost $7.99 / 837 yen. An upgrade from Arcade Archives to Arcade Archives 2 will be available for $2.99 / 330 yen.

Here is an overview of the game, via Hamster:.

TX-1 V.8 is a racing game released by TATSUMI in 1984.

The popular TX-1 has returned, featuring a variety of upgrades to make the game even easier to play!

You can now recover if your car rolls over or spins out, and it’s even possible to jump right over opponents ahead of you.

The eight countries featured in the Grand Prix stages are all new! Enjoy the fresh scenery of each location as you race toward the finish line!

The Arcade Archives series is developed with the concept of faithfully reproducing classic arcade games. It also includes convenient features such as difficulty and screen settings, rewind, rapid-fire, and multiple save slots. In addition, players can compete for the best scores with players around the world through online rankings.

Arcade Archives 2 series introduces a brand-new mode called Time Attack Mode, in addition to the Original Mode, Hi Score Mode, and Caravan Mode from Arcade Archives. Time Attack Mode focuses on how rapidly you can complete the game, regardless of the score you achieve.

What’s more, with VRR (Variable Refresh Rate) support, the gameplay can be reproduced even more accurately, closer to the original arcade experience.

Please enjoy these iconic arcade games that defined an era with the Arcade Archives series!

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Musical virtuoso and the undisputed GOAT of song parodies 'Weird Al' Yankovic has confirmed his inclusion in GTA 6 as a radio host.

Earlier this week, Weird Al posted saying, "Apologies in advance to any friends or loved ones who may want to have some kind of human interaction with me in the upcoming week. I'll be playing a video game." While that seemed very much in line with the litany of people – famous or otherwise – who are going to dedicate their time to GTA 6 over the next week or so, as people got access to the game , they realized it's weirder than they thought. Vice City FM – home of '80s bangers like Prefab Sprout's Cars and Girls and The The's This Is the Day – is hosted by Mr Yankovic himself.

In a post on BlueSky, Weird Al posts an image saying, "now that my NDA has expired… Hey, everybody, I'm in GTA 6." He adds, "I'm the host of GTA 6's 'non-stop '80s' radio channel Vice City FM," which most people had already gathered, marking his second-ever video game appearance after being the announcer for The Grim Adventures of Billy and Mandy – a Power Stone clone for the PS2 and Wii.

Recent findings suggest that I’m the host of GTA 6’s “non-stop ‘80s” radio channel Vice City FM. I also wrote some in-game commercials, and I’m the voice of the Burger Shot ads as well! As a long-time fan of the Grand Theft Auto franchise, I couldn’t be more excited about this. Okay, gotta get back to playing the game!

It has been revealed that but as it turns out, his contributions are more than just a radio host. Weird Al confirms "I also wrote some in-game commercials, and I'm the voice of the Burger Shot ads as well!" The game's credits also list him as a contributor of original music for the game – although unfortunately none of his songs are featured on the in-game radio stations. He adds, "As a long-time fan of the Grand Theft Auto franchise, I couldn't be more excited about this. Okay, gotta get back to playing the game!".

Netflix's long-gestating Magic: The Gathering animated series is called Planeswalker, and it's coming in 2027.

The title was revealed at MagicCon Atlanta, and Netflix shared a first look at the show on Twitter/X on 13th November. "Every great story begins with a spark. Here's your first look at Planeswalker, a new animated series based on Magic: The Gathering. Coming to Netflix in 2027", the company wrote, and shared a teaser, which you can see below:.

According to a synopsis shared with IGN, the series follows Chandra Nalaar, "a volatile pyromancer hunted for her gifts, and haunted by her past". It continues: "Confronted by an insidious force, Chandra and some of the most legendary Planeswalkers must harness their extraordinary abilities, navigate treacherous alliances, and battle their own inner demons to prevent a cataclysmic war that threatens to consume their very existence".

It has been revealed that netflix first declared a Magic: The Gathering series in June 2019, with Avengers: Endgame directors Joe and Anthony Russo attached, and it was originally due in late 2022. Two years in, the original showrunners departed over creative differences, and in September 2024, Netflix confirmed it had started again from scratch with Star Trek: Picard and 12 Monkeys showrunner Terry Matalas in charge.

Industry observers note that IGN reports that Matalas, who most recently ran Marvel's VisionQuest, is running the show alongside Cindy Appel. Budapest-based studio DIGIC Pictures is handling the animation.

At the end of last month, we learned PUBG is also being turned into a live-action series for Netflix, with Donald Glover set to direct, write, executive produce, and star.

Glover is a two-time Emmy and Golden Globe winner, best known for Atlanta and Community. Krafton calls PUBG "one of the world’s most enduring gaming franchises", and indicates the game, which is credited with popularising the battle royale genre, holds seven Guinness World Records.

Star Wars Galactic Racer will get local split-screen multiplayer in early 2027 with fresh 'Free Play' mode, finally letting racers yell at one another in a tangible space

💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, split-screen multiplayer is often treated by developers as a forgotten vestige of a bygone age, something to be left behind as the standardisation of online play makes it redundant, especially following the pandemic.
  • It has been revealed that this fresh mode, Free Play, not only allows for local multiplayer of up to four players (with either humans or CPUs racing together), but also for complete freedom of choice in vehicle, character and planet to race on.
  • As for why this feature may not have been available at launch, other than the cynical view that it wasn't considered a moneymaking priority for Fuse Games and Secret Mode, CD Projekt Red senior technical producer Shayna Moon weighed in to theorise that it took some effort to get four separately-rendered views of the game running without making their machine explode like the Death Star.

In a recent development, split-screen multiplayer is often treated by developers as a forgotten vestige of a bygone age, something to be left behind as the standardisation of online play makes it redundant, especially following the pandemic. It's considered unlikely that you'll have another human being in your home to pick up a controller with you, and since you've inevitably got an internet connection, why not just use that to connect to anyone in the world? I find there's a unique beauty in playing something shoulder to shoulder on a couch with another person, and it seems Fuse Games sees that light too, with Star Wars: Galactic Racer set to be updated to add local splitscreen multiplayer sometime early next year.

It has been revealed that this fresh mode, Free Play, not only allows for local multiplayer of up to four players (with either humans or CPUs racing together), but also for complete freedom of choice in vehicle, character and planet to race on. A simple versus mode like this is a far cry from the roguelite structure of the main game, and one that draws it closer to its arcade racing game roots. An embracing of that is always welcome, as Galactic Racer has been a reminder to many of just how wonderful the arcade racing genre can be, and how poorly served its been in the industry for a while. For example, while the Fuse Games team is partly made up of Criterion Games veterans, Criterion itself has recently been folded into being a Battlefield Studio by EA, making the future of Need for Speed and Burnout uncertain.

As for why this feature may not have been available at launch, other than the cynical view that it wasn't considered a moneymaking priority for Fuse Games and Secret Mode, CD Projekt Red senior technical producer Shayna Moon weighed in to theorise that it took some effort to get four separately-rendered views of the game running without making their machine explode like the Death Star. As Moon puts it: "To be overly simple about it, if the game is running at 30fps for each player, that means it’s actually rendering 120fps." Likely not an issue for a lot of PC players, but a potential issue for console players considering the game is built to run at a locked 60fps for one player on consoles. Past this upcoming update, it looks like the Star Wars franchise as a whole could be set for more smaller games ala Galactic Racer in general, per comments made by Lucasfilms' vice president.

It has been revealed that I feel like I say this once a week at this point, but gaming monitors occupy one of the only bright spots in the dark cloud that is PC hardware right now. They are getting better and cheaper by the day, and it seems I'm not alone in thinking this, as global OLED monitor shipments doubled in the last year. Woo, go OLED monitors.

This is according to Trendforce, which notes Asus is the market leader for global OLED monitor sales (at 21.7%), with MSI coming in second (14.5%) and Samsung coming in third (11.3%). LGE take fourth place with 8.6%, and Dell closely follows that with 8.2%. The rest of the industry has the remaining 35.7% to split among themselves.

As for total sales, Trendforce notes global OLED sales got a 13% bump from last quarter to this year, and more impressively, sales for OLED monitors reportedly doubled compared to the same quarter last year. That means OLED monitors have significant upward momentum right now.

And who can blame people for buying in? OLED monitors are known for having super vibrant colours, true blacks, and they tend to have wicked fast response times and refresh rates. The difference between IPS and OLED is so apparent when you put them beside each other, and I know, as I'm rocking a dual monitor setup with both panel technologies.

In a recent development, they are a bit more expensive than IPS, and older panels can suffer from burn-in, but I can say swapping from an IPS panel to an OLED one is one of the most monumental changes I've made to my gaming setup in the last decade. Though, in fairness, that also came with a resolution bump from 1080p to 1440p.

Recent findings suggest that OLEDs have been getting cheaper over time, too—they're far from the ultra-expensive pieces of kit we saw just a couple of years ago. And with upcoming manufacturing developments such as inkjet printing (IJP), there's every reason to believe the downward trend in pricing could continue.

What great news to hit just as Black Friday has started at Amazon. If you're feeling the hankering to stare into the vibrant blacks of an OLED panel, there are already some sweet savings to be had. Now that OLED gaming monitors are as cheap as $270, they're a seriously attractive upgrade option.

Break up and re-commodify a fallen Earth in Steel Gullet, a satisfyingly funereal factory puzzler that really loves thermodynamics

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (659 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rockpapershotgun

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, it's amazing what a difference a few lines of preamble can make to your understanding of a game.
  • The difference is that you're doing this inside a huge walking fortress city, which stamps across the surface of a largely unseen, devastated and uninhabitable Earth.
  • From a certain, carefully limited point of view, this transforms Steel Gullet into the kind of "Zen experience" I hope death-positive morticians have when really absorbed in their work.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, it's amazing what a difference a few lines of preamble can make to your understanding of a game. Out now on PC, Steel Gullet is a factory engineering puzzler that, while notable for its meticulous interest in thermodynamics, broadly compares to the foundational work of Zachtronics, together with more recent and focussed conveyor belt wranglers such as Modulus. Resources come in, and you arrange machines on a grid to transform them into something else, before sliding them into an output hopper.

The difference is that you're doing this inside a huge walking fortress city, which stamps across the surface of a largely unseen, devastated and uninhabitable Earth. Your resources are the refuse of a bygone human civilisation: knots of concrete and rebar, flaccid rubber hose and splintered plank, that must be separated out before you can manufacture anything.

From a certain, carefully limited point of view, this transforms Steel Gullet into the kind of "Zen experience" I hope death-positive morticians have when really absorbed in their work. My task is to lay a civilisation to rest, by dissecting and cleansing the remains, readying a fallen objectworld for an after-life that extends somewhere beyond the map's huge rusty walls (walls that, perhaps appropriately, constrain your camera movement a bit too much for comfort).

It makes me think of the vertigo I get when I look at devices such as, well, the computer I'm writing this on, and think about how many materials and histories of production lie entangled within it. Steel Gullet answers the desire for clarity and accounting there. Of course, the other part of the premise is that I am doing busywork for some kind of totalitarian organisation, G.R.I.D. But shh, no time to think about that! I'm trying to work out how hot rubber needs to be before it can be moulded.

According to recent reports, thermodynamics is Steel Gullet's fixation, and a worthwhile one. Every material encased in each lump of salvage has different physical properties – a melting point, density, solubility, ferromagnetism, etcetera. You meed to exploit these differences to separate the pieces. Wood, for example, is more buoyant than metal and concrete, so if you feed the clump into an oil bath, the planks will float to the top. If there's rubber, you can run the clump through furnaces to melt and drain it, then cool and reheat the resulting puddle to create a malleable material.

It's still just the usual automation game routine of funnelling greebly wotsits through various smashy boxes to produce a commodity. But the thermodynamics sim element both supports the above feeling of purifying a hopelessly muddled world, and makes for a surprising visual feast: I enjoy watching each material emerge from the inital jumble and assume different shapes. There are the usual supporting infrastructure elements, such as elevators, splitters and manual junction boxes. I dare say somebody will build a logic circuit in Steel Gullet, sooner or later - let's start the clock till they get Doom running on the thing.

In a recent development, in terms of overall strategy, you alternate between sending outputs to hoppers that earn you cash, and sending them to hoppers that generate research progression. You'll also unlock latest rooms, removing walls and exposing new output hoppers. As you're issued new work orders, you must break open your production lines to install new machines and redirect the flow. Fortunately, you can sell back components to keep your cash reserves healthy – or at least, you can in the demo.

Between chapters, you'll be invited to join the resistance against the aforesaid G.R.I.D., perhaps sending information to the rebels. But again, no time, no time! I have all this concrete I need to powderise, all these girders I need to liquefy and make new, all these crisp, gleaming circuitboards I need to manufacture. The city's hunger is as vast as it is holy. Read more on Steam.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Call of Duty Endowment is marking Remembrance Day and its 17th anniversary by encouraging Modern Warfare 4 and Warzone players to pick up its Valor Pack, with all of Activision's net proceeds going towards helping veterans find jobs.

The Call of Duty Endowment Valor Pack - which has been available since Modern Warfare 4 debuted on 23rd October - was designed by the Endowment and Infinity Ward with US Marine Corps veteran and Medal of Honor recipient Kyle Carpenter in mind.

The items include a melee weapon blueprint inscribed with "Worth Fighting For", plus items called Relentless and Still Standing.

According to the Call of Duty blog, 100 percent of Activision's net proceeds from the pack (after VAT and sales tax) go to the Endowment.

To mark Remembrance Day, players who owned it and launched either game before 6pm GMT on 12th November also received double XP tokens and a DMZ survival kit.

"Veterans bring incredible skills into the workplace after military service," noted Carpenter.

The Endowment, which supports veterans in the UK as well as the US, states it has now helped place more than 180,000 into "high-quality jobs", and wants to reach 200,000 by 2030.

Recent findings suggest that other partners are also raising money, with Pilot's round-up campaign raising more than £4.7 million ($6 million) for the Endowment since 2019. Polaris will also donate around £19,500 ($25,000) if players collectively complete 5 million rides in its DAGOR vehicle across Modern Warfare 4 and Warzone by 25th November.

Industry observers note that it comes two weeks after Activision apologised to bereaved families of the Itaewon crowd crush victims and confirmed it would remove real footage of the tragedy from Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4. Players discovered that the game's opening cinematic uses short news clips to depict fictional civilian casualties during a North Korean invasion of South Korea. Those clips have since been found to include archive footage from the 2022 Itaewon disaster, in which around 160 people died.

Call of Duty's anti-cheat team Ricochet recently revealed it's officially cracking down on Warzone Agent.
