#51560. Industry News: What would Rockstar have done if GTA hadn't taken off? Former tech director Obbe Vermeij on Scottish zombies, James Bond and the "curse" of success

📅 17 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 8m • 📚 Deep Dive (1692 w)
📖 Baca
General 📈 Bullish 🌐 Rockpapershotgun ↗ Open Full Page

Industry News: What would Rockstar have done if GTA hadn't taken off? Former tech director Obbe Vermeij on Scottish zombies, James Bond and the "curse" of success

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1692 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rockpapershotgun

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that it's bizarre today to think of Rockstar working on games that aren't Grand Theft Auto.
  • Once upon a time, Rockstar weren't just known for GTA and to a considerably lesser extent, Red Dead Redemption.
  • It has been revealed that during the noughties especially, when the most expensive games took considerably less time to make, Rockstar tried their hand at a number of projects besides GTA.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that it's bizarre today to think of Rockstar working on games that aren't Grand Theft Auto. Frankly, it's bizarre to think of Rockstar working on games that aren't GTA 6, which rolls onto console hard drives this week. A decade in the making, with a development team of thousands scattered across an international network of studios, GTA 6 aims to be the Maximum Game. It's both a dense, lively open world and a monument to the exhausting impersonality of "triple-A" game productions. It contains multitudes: birdlife! Realistic cloud formation! Fuel mechanics! Romance! Soda visibly sloshing around in bottles! It's an imperial production shadowed by labour disputes, that appears to have given Rockstar's various teams little time or space to think about anything else.

It wasn't ever thus. Once upon a time, Rockstar weren't just known for GTA and to a considerably lesser extent, Red Dead Redemption. Once upon a time, they had a reputation for slightly dodgy experiments. I recently interviewed former Rockstar North tech director Obbe Vermeij about a few of them, including Agent, the unofficial James Bond game Rockstar toyed with before putting all chips on Grand Theft Auto 5.

It has been revealed that during the noughties especially, when the most expensive games took considerably less time to make, Rockstar tried their hand at a number of projects besides GTA. There was 2002's Manhunt, a rancid parody of snuff films – not much loved, but sufficiently admired to spawn a sequel in the hands of Rockstar London. There was 2005's adaptation of Walter Hill flick The Warriors - a mouthy Homeric beat 'em up in which you cross Upcoming York on foot over the course of a single night - and 2006's Rockstar Presents Table Tennis - an inexplicable pivot towards realistic sports simulation from Rockstar San Diego. Later in 2006 came Bully, aka Canis Canem Edit, a boarding school life sim from Rockstar Vancouver (née Barking Dog Studios). I didn't warm to Bully, myself, but I've never been able to get its sardonic OST out of my head.

In amongst all these, Rockstar weighed up several game projects that never made it out of the building. The aforesaid Agent is perhaps the best-known, but my conversation with Vermeij (who worked at Rockstar from 1995 to 2009) began with "Z", a fleeting attempt to expand into the world of zombie action games, which Rockstar spent a few weeks mulling over in the wake of Grand Theft Auto: Vice City. It was set in the islands of Scotland, which would have made it the only Rockstar North project to unfold in the studio's backyard. "I think it was meant to be smaller than GTA, map-wise, and there weren't going to be any deserted cities - it was really just islands and some villages," Vermeij told me. "But it really didn't get that far.".

Industry observers note that the pitch for Z couldn't be further from the sweat and glitter of GTA 6's Miami, but the two projects would have shared a taste for 'simulation' elements. "It actually was going to have cars running out of fuel," Vermeij told me. "That was going to be one of the things, and the whole idea was that you'd find cars and they'd only have a little bit of fuel in them." As for why Z never entered full development, turns out desolate North Atlantic archipelagos full of corpses can be a bit of a downer. "Everybody was super excited to do something newly introduced," Vermeij went on. "And then pretty rapidly, we kind of realised that it's really just a depressing version of GTA, and it sort of died.".

Recent findings suggest that the increasing success of Grand Theft Auto during these years was something of a "curse", Vermeij went on. It meant that a lot of Rockstar's ventures beyond GTA were eventually folded back into the series. "It's very difficult to have a studio and have one mega game, and then do something on the side," he explained. "It's almost impossible, because at any time during the development of the smaller project, management's going to say 'oh! The major project's in trouble. We need more people.' And they're just going to pull everybody from that small team onto the big team, so even if we had progressed with [Z], what would have happened is we would have had to start GTA 4 at the same time, and eventually the small team would just be merged with the big team again.".

Recent findings suggest that rockstar's Bondalike game Agent got a lot further down the road to release than Z. It was in development for several years following GTA 4's launch, and was touted by co-founder Sam Houser as Rockstar's next megagame. "A lot of work had been done on that," Vermeij recalled. "And then we ended up just cutting and cutting it, because the same thing happened – at some point you kind of go OK, well, we better get on with the next GTA.".

Industry observers note that agent sounds like it could have been a hoot, at least going by Vermeij's description of his own time with the project. It was a relatively linear, level-based action game with a touch of camp. "There was a French ski resort, and there was going to be a Mediterranean town like San Tropez, somewhere like that," Vermeij explained. "There was going to be a North African place, like Morocco or Egypt. The last level was going to be on the moon, with lasers – like Moonraker. There was another one, London or something, I can't remember. But then we just ended up cutting everything down, because what we could see happening was that at some point, we would have to go back to work on GTA. It wasn't close to being finished.".

While never a spoof in the vein of Austin Powers, Agent would have been a sillier production than the grimy and downbeat GTA 4. "It was meant to lean into all the cliches," Vermeij remarked. "It was like James Bond from the 1970s - there was a girl with white boots. It wasn't a comedy, it was just completely over-the-top cliched.".

According to recent reports, as for the choice of a level-based format, this came from a desire for variety the studio couldn't realistically achieve in a GTA-style open world. "If you had to have them all on one map, you would basically have had to model a mini version of Europe," Vermeij said, "So you couldn't do that." Players might have been able to revisit locations containing several missions, which calls to mind Io Interactive's later Hitman: World of Assassination games, to say nothing of their own bash at the Flemingverse, 007 First Light. "I don't how whether it was going to be completely linear, or whether you were always going to be able to visit all those locations." Vermeij said.

Needless to say, Rockstar's Bondalike would have featured chase scenes. Vermeij himself worked on the moving parts. "I remember doing some work on what we called the car recording stuff for GTA," he went on. "So if a level designer wanted to set up a chase scene, they would drive one car, record it, and then play back the recording, drive a second car and record that... and so driving one by one, you could set up a whole chase scene. I did a version of that for [human] characters as well, because for one of the Agent missions in the French ski resort, there was like a chase where the bad guys were on skiis and using their machine guns. So I set up a thing where you'd play them one by one, and then play the whole thing back. There was maybe like five or six bad guys and they'd ski after you, and then it was just up to the player to avoid them.".

According to Vermeij, Agent never had a defined story during his time with it. It was more of a mix of scenario concepts, "kind of how we used to do games with GTA 3 and Vice City". Mind you, the absence of a nailed-down plot isn't necessarily a sign that Agent was lightyears from being finished. Even at their most byzantine, Bond movie plotlines often feel like an afterthought. "It's like oh yeah, there's a bad guy and there's a thingally-dingally that needs to be captured before the world comes to an end," summarised Vermeij. Still, Agent would spend a long time in limbo after Vermeij left. It's still unclear how much it was in active development before Rockstar's trademark finally evaporated in November 2018.

Sources indicate that one thing I learned while reading up on Rockstar's checkered history was that GTA 3, the game that made GTA a Thing on PlayStation, wasn't deemed an immediate hit at launch. According to Vermeij himself, it was months before Rockstar realised what they'd built. This inspired an obvious closing question: what might Rockstar have done, if GTA 3 hadn't blown up the way it did? Which of those other projects might have become the focus?

"I really have never thought about it," Vermeij pondered. "When Rockstar San Diego joined, it was 2002, and they already had a bunch of games and a bunch of franchises, like Midnight Club and Smuggler's Run. They were already into driving games and city games in that way, so it wouldn't have surprised me if we'd gone in that direction anyway. But then they were more about car modding and decals and stuff like that.

Recent findings suggest that "At Rockstar North, we only had Manhunt and GTA," he went on. "With Manhunt, that team was in development hell for a while, they had a couple of rough years where they got stuck and in the end, they pulled through, and they got a pretty decent game. But I don't think that would have been the future. I don't think [Rockstar North] would have done a Manhunt 2. So yeah, it would be Table Tennis, I think! Everything on Table Tennis!".

According to recent reports, I know it, you know it, hell, I'm sure developer Archetype Entertainment know it: Exodus is kind of just Mass Effect again. That's in part because the DNA of the game has been built by series vets like Drew Karpyshyn, Chad Robertson and James Ohlen. But it's also because, well, they're putting FemShep in the game. Yes, I'm being a tad facetious here, but when the latest trailer for your game is literally titled "Female Jun Reveal," well, comparisons will be made!

To top it all off, a blog post from the devs literally refers to the alternate gender for the protag as FemJun. They know what they're doing. In any case, first up, her voice actor! She's being played by Carina Conti, an up and comer last digitally heard in Mafia: The Old Country as Isabella Torrisi. Male Jun (who hasn't been given a nickname, which couldn't possibly serve to other female Jun (and MascJun is right there!)) has also had his voice actor confirmed as Stephen Oyoung, who you'll have heard as Mister Negative in Insomniac's Spider-Man games and Red Hood in Gotham Knights.

It's been previously confirmed that no matter which gender you pick for Jun, you'll be able to romance whoever you like, so, happy smoochin'! The story will stay the same too, as will dialogue options, though I'm imagine some pronoun switcheroos will take place somewhere along the line.

It has been revealed that I'm mostly just left feeling that this doesn't really seem like it'll fix the game's boring hero problem. Edwin made note of Jun's quite lacklustre vibe earlier this year, aptly tearing down MascJun's Instagram visage, though this was prior to the face model and voice actor change the character has undergone. Personally, I'm not sure that'll be enough, and FemJun kind of matches that Instagram look; the perfect bun and bangs that pop out when she takes her helmet off is quite silly too. Ah well! A game isn't done until it's done (which, in theory, will be April 7th next year).

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A upcoming Cyberpunk 2077 mod has overhauled Night City's rain, swapping the game's flat wet weather effects for individual 3D drops and adding lightning storms.

As spotted by DSOGaming, modder CyanideX's mod, Torrent, gives each raindrop its own size and falling speed. The drops also react to the player's movement, so they stream towards the windscreen when you're driving fast. If you find the wind has picked up, blustery weather can also push them sideways, too.

According to recent reports, the rain also catches the light from street lamps, neon signs, car headlights, and taillights, and won't fall through roofs or inside buildings. Drops splash on the ground, heavy rain leaves mist in the distance, and cars throw up spray from their tyres on wet roads.

The mod complements this with a newly introduced lightning system, with branching bolts that flash and flicker before fading, and that can arrive in bursts during heavier storms.

If you like a little lightning, the frequency of bolts can be adjusted across 10 levels, and with the AudioXL mod installed, thunder follows each strike, timed to how far away it landed.

For players sensitive to flashing lights, a Reduce Flashes option dims the lightning, replaces its flicker with a single slow glow, and halves the number of strikes.

Torrent supports Nova City 2 and other weather mods, and adds extra storm effects for Nova City 2 players, including mist that rolls through the streets with the wind. It’s available now on Nexus Mods.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that I thought we'd already gotten our fill of prehistoric creatures on the 2026 movie schedule, thanks to The End of Oak Street. The film sees Anne Hathaway and Ewan McGregor spending a summer trying to survive a neighborhood full of creatures that should have been extinct for millions of years. Then, as soon as the movie hit streaming, the internet started arguing over footage supposedly showing a pterodactyl flying over Mexico. The timing feels a little too perfect.

According to recent reports, the latest monster-of-the-week discussion took off on November 13, when someone posted images to Reddit's r/Cryptozoology forum. The poster claimed the winged creature had been caught on airport security footage in Ciudad Juárez and that additional witnesses had photographs. None of that was verified, but you can probably guess how the comments went.

I'll give the image this much: It's pretty cool. The creature has an enormous wingspan, a long, pointed head, and a silhouette you'd expect to see flying over the Platt family's house in The End of Oak Street. Of course, it also looks suspiciously like something you'd find in Jurassic Park. Several Reddit consumers noticed that resemblance, too, and weren't particularly convinced.

According to recent reports, there's apparently more to the sighting. According to Mexican outlet El Financier, an earlier video, reportedly recorded October 29 in the Anapra area of Ciudad Juárez, highlights a mysterious winged figure flying across the night sky. Jaime Maussan, a Mexican broadcaster known for his interest in UFOs and other unexplained phenomena, picked up the footage and helped spread the story. Before long, additional alleged sightings circulated online, and naturally, the internet had a field day.

No cryptic sighting is worth its weight in dino dung unless the internet loses its collective mind, and the comments weren't disappointing. One commenter with the username r/alfred0t0rnad0 pretty much summed up my feelings:.

I WANT TO BELIEVE, but I just can't.

Somebody else was considerably more enthusiastic about the possibility of prehistoric creatures making a comeback. R/AsadAliShadowhunter wrote:.

At this point, I hope the Dinos are back.

Recent findings suggest that look, I'm not opposed to a little prehistoric excitement. I'd just prefer anything with a 20-foot wingspan to stay away from my backyard.

Your Daily Blend of Entertainment News.

Industry observers note that those two comments barely scratch the surface, though. Some customers had legitimate questions about the footage, while others were just enjoying the absurdity. Here are a few of my favorites:.

Industry observers note that personally, I'm partial to the idea of a prehistoric creature emerging from the hollow Earth for tacos. But the commenters questioning how an entire population of giant flying reptiles could have gone unnoticed for millions of years have a pretty good point.

The End Of Oak Street Ending: Yes, They Had Conversations About The Dog Dying.

Sources indicate that there's also the small matter of what local authorities have said about the footage. EFE's fact-checking team reported Wednesday that Ciudad Juárez's civil protection director, Sergio Rodríguez, dismissed the recordings as digital entertainment content. One widely shared version also appears to show signs of AI manipulation, although the origins of the various clips haven't all been established.

It has been revealed that unfortunately for those of us hoping The End of Oak Street had somehow become a documentary, there's no credible evidence that a pterodactyl is flying around Mexico. Still, I have to admit I've enjoyed watching the internet speculate over the possibility.

The End of Oak Street is now streaming with an HBO Max subscription, which makes it an excellent choice if this whole thing has you craving some cinematic dinosaurs.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

There's been an awful lot of debate about the overall quality and lasting commercial success of Call of Duty across the last few years, with many arguing that the once unstoppable series is steadily losing its edge.

As such, this latest report from Circana won't make for easy reading if you're Xbox or Activision.

According to the ever-informative Mat Piscatella, the recently released Modern Warfare 4 was the best selling game of October in the US.

However, despite a strong debut and a mostly positive reception — especially with regards to its single player campaign — the big budget shooter has failed to break into the top 10 best selling titles of 2026 so far.

For Call of Duty, such an absence would have been unthinkable just a few short years ago; it really does suggest that it's struggled to match the kind of sales figures we've come to expect of the franchise.

Case in point: the current-gen port of Black Ops 2 remains on 2026's top 10 list.

Of course, there's still time for Modern Warfare 4 to make up some ground with the holidays right around the corner, but this seems to be a continuation of the downward trend that we saw with last year's very poorly rated Black Ops 7.

Indeed, it's possible that the Black Ops 7 backlash has negatively impacted Modern Warfare 4's appeal — and that's not the kind of spiral that Activsion will want to find itself in.

Elsewhere, Gears of War: E-Day — which was famously cancelled on PS5 just weeks ahead of launch — managed second place for October, and the eye-watering Star Wars: Galactic Racer entered in third.

Another new release, the largely fantastic Final Fantasy Resonance, landed in sixth — which feels like a win for Square Enix given the flood of games that came out last month.

* Projected digital sales ^ Actual digital sales.

Mondrayn is a putrid, crunchy pixel art RPG about escaping from limbo where "dying doesn't mean the end of your suffering"

I'm not entirely sure how that manifests, you do seem to be able to do both regular attacks and special moves, the state of characters seems to have an impact, but truthfully I don't mind not understanding because what I'm here for are the utterly, delectably rancid vibes on display.

Everything's a bit grim these days, so let's just go all in on the misery shall we? Let's start with this line from the game's Steam page we'll be talking about today: "Mondrayn is a grim JRPG with survival elements where dying doesn't mean the end of your suffering." Crikey! You're telling me the sweet release of death won't be so saccharine after all? Sounds rough, so it's a good thing Mondrayn looks so darn compelling.

The world of Mondrayn is a dead one. You start out waking up in a city, it's in a gnarly state, of course, overrun by a disease of unknown origin. Horrible monsters are roaming about the place, cults are performing nasty rituals, and you've got no memories, so all you can do is try and make any friends you can, kill the undead and get out of, all places, limbo.

Mondrayn is an RPG in the sense that it utilises turn-based combat, "intertwined with shootouts." I'm not entirely sure how that manifests, you do seem to be able to do both regular attacks and special moves, the state of characters seems to have an impact, but truthfully I don't mind not understanding because what I'm here for are the utterly, delectably rancid vibes on display.

It has been revealed that every single pixel in this game looks like it was dipped in a vat of grime, puss, blood and vomit, and I revel in it! The enemy portraits are crunchy and violet, they look ripped straight out of some obscure art book for a Warhammer-esque tabletop game no one has ever heard of. It looks a bit fantasy, a bit steampunk, and incredibly, incredibly grimdark. It's the kind of world I'd rather instantly top myself than spend a second longer in, so, kudos to the fictional characters in it that have no choice in the matter for managing better than me. As it stands, Mondrayn has no release date, but you can wishlist it on Steam in the meantime.
